From 3 to 5 inches of rain fell over Adams county in a short amount of time during the morning hours of June 3rd.  Numerous roads were closed due to flooding including 90th Street 3 miles south southeast of Fowler, various roads in Payson, and several county and secondary roads in the Kingston and Richfield areas.  A couple of the secondary gravel roads were washed out due to the flash flooding.  Mill Creek, just north of Marblehead, was out of its banks and brought down several nearby trees and flooded East 753rd Lane for a time.

Up to 6 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time over northern Pike county during the morning hours of June 3rd.  Numerous secondary roads had water over them.  Around 810 am, an eastbound Norfolk Southern freight train derailed on a bridge that just got washed out between Kinderhook and Barry.  Hadley Creek was out of its banks and the force of the water washed out the railroad bridge as the train was going over it.  Thirty-two cars of the 78 car train derailed.  The cars were not carrying anything toxic, just coal and corn oil product.  In Pittsfield, the heavy rains caused a basement wall to collapse on a home while several other homes suffered water damage to their basements due to sewer backups.  Near the Pike/Adams county line, a couple were driving on a local road when the road gave way and collapsed.  The car remained suspended between the two sections of roadway, so the couple had to carefully exit the vehicle. The driver sustained a broken foot and a badly sprained foot on the other leg.  Her husband was able to get her out of the vehicle without the car falling further into the hole.  They then used their cell phone to call for help.

Up to two inches of rain fell on already saturated soils in Montgomery county.  Water was over several roads in the Raymond area including Illinois Route 48 west of Raymond.

Numerous secondary roads had water flowing over them including Highway J south of Lewistown, Highway 6 in Lewistown, and Highway 16 east of Monticello.  County Roads 305 and 356 had a section of road washed out due to the heavy rains.
Over 3 inches fell in a short amount of time in Knox county during the morning hours of June 3rd.  The intersection of Highway K and M was flooded just south of Millport.

The ASOS at the airport in St Charles (KSET) reported a gust to 55KT (63 mph).

At 7:28 pm CDT, ambulance drivers estimated 70 mph winds near the intersection of Highway 24 and Highway 61 just northwest of Hannibal. Six minutes later, permanent MoDOT signs were reported downed near the intersection of Highway 61 and County Road 421, just east of the initial report.
The ASOS at the Spirit of St Louis airport (KSUS) reported a gust to 52KT (60 mph).

At 8:29 PM a tornado began near the community of Elmont, MO, producing EF1 damage primarily to trees and one large barn. The tornado moved quickly to the northeast, and produced additional tree damage along Missouri route 185, and along Ridge Road within the Long Ridge Conservation Area. The tornado then continued northeast before ending very near Highway 47. Near the end of its path, the tornado damaged several homes, outbuildings, telephone poles and trees within the southern outskirts of Union, MO. The most significant of this damage occurred near N Bend Road, where damage to a home and barn suggested maximum wind speeds of approximately 105 miles per hour.

At approximately 8:33 PM a tornado began south of Kohl City, MO in Franklin County and continued northeastward for 5.5 miles before dissipating just southwest of Etlah, MO in Franklin County around 8:39 PM. Most damage was confined to tree limbs, but a few structures were damaged closer to Etlah. This tornado was assigned a rating of EF-1 with a maximum wind speed of 105 mph.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down tree branches between Hawk Point and Troy just south of Highway 47. The thunderstorm then produced a 78 mph wind gust at Avery Park in Troy.
Thunderstorm winds blew the doors of a farm outbuilding in. These winds also blew a camper on its side.
Hail ranging from 1 inch to 1.5 inches fell in Columbia.
Hail ranging in size from dimes to quarters fell for nearly 6 minutes.
Wind driven quarter sized hail damaged the siding of a building in Addieville.
Wind driven quarter sized hail caused damage to siding near New Minden.
Thunderstorm winds downed one large tree limb in Centralia.
Quarter to golf ball sized hail fell south and east of Salem.
Half dollar sized hail was measured with a ruler by the emergency manager in Nashville.
Quarter sized hail fell in French Village for approximately 5 minutes.
Quarter sized hail fell in Caledonia. Some hailstones may have been slightly larger than  quarters.

A levee on the Mississippi River near Meyer failed and caused flash flooding in an area from Bear Creek northward toward the Adams/Hancock county line.  The flood waters spread as far east as East 500th Street along the bluffs.  A couple hours later a second levee break occurred aggravating the flooding situation.  A couple dozen homes in Meyer were flooded as well as a couple of businesses.  The entire town of 40 to 50 people had evacuated before the levee was breached.

A 150 foot section of the Cap Au Gris Levee failed about a quarter of a mile south of the Winfield Lock and Dam on the Mississippi River.  It flooded mostly farmland as well as a couple of houses and farm buildings.  The secondary Winfield Levee (Pin Oak) kept the flood waters away from Winfield at this time.

A levee break was reported near Highway M, southeast of Elsberry.  It flooded areas east of Highway 79 to the Mississippi River in the Kings Lake and southern Elsberry Levee districts.  The flood waters moved into Foley, flooding a couple dozen homes.  Another levee broke further north a couple of hours later affecting the areas to the north of the original levee break.

A levee broke just north of Highway M in Lincoln county and near Kickapoo Road.  It flooded portions of the Elsberry Levee District in extreme southeastern Pike county east of Highway 79 and from Annada southward.

The Elm Point Levee failed causing flood waters to pour into a portion of far northern St. Charles county.  The area affected was from just north of Highway 370 to Huster Road on the east to Elm Point Road on the south and Truman Boulevard on the west.  The St. Louis Youth Association's 18 soccer fields were flooded and about 500 acres of farmland were affected.  A couple of businesses were flooded as well.  Highway 370 was closed for a brief time as there were hundreds of deer and other wildlife crossing the highway to higher ground and they were causing a major hazard to traffic in the area.
The Pin Oak Levee near the Mississippi River failed causing flood waters to rush towards the town of Winfield.  At least 60 homes were flooded in Winfield west of Highway 79.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs in Washington.  One large tree limb damaged three fences as it fell to the ground.
A large hotel sign was blown down by thunderstorm winds in Sullivan.
A large section of roof was blown off of a storage building in Hallsville.  The debris was deposited about 100 feet away.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted a large tree at the corner of N. Olive and Bourne Streets.  The tree blocked access to the home's front porch but did not cause structural damage to the home.
Numerous large tree limbs were blown down in Auxvasse.  Also, several power lines were blown down in Auxvasse and Kingdom City.
Several large trees were blown down onto Highway BB near Mount Sterling.
Lightning struck a barn in far southwestern Cole county.  It burned to the ground in less than half an hour.
Up to 3 inches of rain fell on already saturated soils in eastern Madison County.  Numerous roads were flooded including Walnut Road south of U.S. Highway 40 and Illinois Route 160 south of Highland.

Between 2 and 4 inches of rain fell on already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including U.S. Highway 50 in Breese, Germantown Road in Breese, and Illinois Route 161 near Albers.
Numerous large tree limbs were blown down in Hannibal.
Several large tree limbs were blown down onto Illinois Route 106 northwest of Pittsfield.

Over 2 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils in northern Ralls county.  Several secondary roads were flooded for a time including Cedar Cove Place south of Highway M.

Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs onto Highway 15 north of Mexico, blocking the highway for a time.  Also, a couple of power lines and power poles were blown down at the intersection of Highway 22 and Ringo Street in Mexico.
Numerous tree limbs and a couple of power lines were blown down in Roodhouse and areas just to the east of Roodhouse.

A tornado briefly touched down in a farm destroying a machine shed and flipped over an unoccupied and unanchored mobile home.  Also, the farm house sustained minor roof damage and several trees were blown over.

Three to four inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils in about a 40 minute time frame causing flash flooding.  In the southern sections of Hannibal, water was 3 to 4 feet deep in the area of Irwin Street and Bowling Avenue as the nearby creek overflowed its banks.  A couple of cars were destroyed in the flood and a couple of mobile homes had some water damage.

Lightning struck the county courthouse for the fourth time since June 4th of this year.  This time it knocked out part of the 911 capabilities, along with other software and computers throughout the courthouse.

A tornado developed at 8:56pm on March 14th, 2025 on the east side of Villa Ridge, between American Inn Road and Saint Marys Road north of I-44. The tornado very quickly intensified as it moved into a neighborhood near the intersection of Interstate 44 and US Highway 100. In that neighborhood, the tornado damaged numerous homes, making several of them uninhabitable. The strongest estimated wind speeds in this neighborhood were estimated at 130 mph, based on significant damage to three of these homes. The tornado continued to the northeast, damaging an industrial facility before moving into a heavily wooded area in northeastern Franklin county. Here, the tornado resulted in a narrow track of concentrated, intense tree damage. There were also a number of homes in the path that sustained damage. Before crossing into St. Louis County, the tornado hit a microwave tower, knocking the top portion of the tower to the ground. These winds were also estimated to be 130mph.

The tornado then moved into western St. Louis county from Franklin County, where it continued to produce concentrated, significant tree damage before dissipating at the bend in Highway 100, northeast of Fox Creek.

A long track tornado began at approximately 9:16 PM just north of Marquette High School in Chesterfield, MO, and continued northeast through the communities of Maryland Heights, Bridgeton, Hazelwood, and Florissant before dissipating just east of New Halls Ferry Rd at approximately 9:39 PM. The tornado reached peak surveyed intensity just south of St. Louis Lambert International Airport, where a house sustained EF-2 damage (122 mph). The tornado had a path length of 20.67 miles with a maximum path width of 880 yards.

The tornado continued into St. Charles County after exiting St. Louis County at approximately 9:43 PM. The tornado was nearly �� mile wide as it entered St. Charles County. Some of the most significant damage of the track occurred as the tornado passed through West Alton. Multiple homes sustained damage in the city. The tornado then passed into Madison County, IL. In St. Charles County the tornado had a path length of 4.22 miles with a maximum path width of 1125 yards. It was rated an EF2.

As the first EF2 tornado in St. Louis County was dissipating, a second long track tornado formed near Jana Elementary School in Florissant and tracked northeastward, producing widespread damage through Old Jamestown. In St. Louis County the tornado had a path length of 4.36 miles with a maximum path width of 1250 yards.

At approximately 9:18 PM a tornado began just south of Morse Mill, MO causing damage to trees and homes as it moved northeast. The worst damage in Jefferson County occurred in the southwest corner of Arnold where the roof of a residence was torn off on Shelley Lynn Drive. The tornado then passed into south St. Louis County. In Jefferson County the tornado had a path length of 20.9 miles and a maximum path width of 850 yards. It was rated an EF2.

The tornado continued into south St. Louis County at approximately 9:37 PM where it produced tree damage and minor damage to multiple homes and one hospital. The tornado dissipated at around 9:39 PM. In St. Louis County the tornado had a path length of 4.43 miles and a maximum path width of 550 yards.

A tornado that originated in Oregon County, MO and caused EF-3 level damage in Carter County, MO tracked into southern Reynolds County where it busted out the glass of a single family home. From there it continued northeast, uprooting and snapping trees along a track that passed just south of Grady and ended at Highway H. The tornado lifted here at approximately 10:29 PM. In Reynolds County the tornado was rated EF-1 with a path length of 9.22 miles and a maximum path width of 50 yards.

At approximately 10:20 PM a tornado began near Missouri Highway HH in the Clearwater Conservation Area to the northeast of Garwood, MO in Reynolds County where it caused tree damage and collapsed the roof of a shed. From there the tornado continued northeast and passed over Clearwater Lake where it destroyed multiple outbuildings on and near the water. Further northeast on County Road 468, the tornado damaged more trees before exiting into Wayne County. In Reynolds County the tornado was rated EF-2 with a path length of 9.99 miles and a maximum path width of 1525 yards.

In Iron County the tornado caused some of its most significant damage in Des Arc where residences were significantly damaged. Two injuries were confirmed here. The tornado continued to track northeast beyond Des Arc where it caused damage to a few more residences, an outbuilding, and numerous trees. It then exited into Madison County. In Iron County the tornado was rated EF-3 with a path length of 7.64 miles and a maximum path width of 800 yards.

In Madison County, the tornado mostly caused tree damage. The only structural damage was to a residence and an outbuilding on Highway C. From there, the tornado continued northeast before dissipating between the St. Francois River and Madison 418 at approximately 10:57 PM. In Madison County the tornado was rated EF-1 with a path length of 6.75 miles and a maximum path width of 770 yards.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted multiple large pine trees on the reporting party's property.

Thunderstorm winds uprooted large trees on the reporting party's property and caused large tree branches to snap. These tree branches appeared to have fallen on a second story deck causing it to collapse. A large tree also fell on the home's roof causing its brick chimney to crumble.
Thunderstorm winds snapped multiple healthy trees of various sizes on the property.
Thunderstorm winds downed multiple trees in the forest on McKelvey Woods Trail.
A mid-sized home experienced damage to the entire front side of their roof from thunderstorm winds. As the roof was covered in tarp, the extent of the damage is unknown.
Thunderstorm winds tore the roof off a garage and off a portion of the connected home. There was also damage to the roof's trim.
Thunderstorm winds snapped two large trees near their base.
Thunderstorm winds blew an entire intact garage or shed roof onto the ground and into a standing tree, splitting the roof around the tree.
Thunderstorm winds downed multiple trees, knocking them onto homes in the area.
Thunderstorm winds collapsed a carport and blew roofs from multiple homes in the area. They also downed power lines and multiple trees.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree. The tree fell onto a vehicle, blocking the street south of Industrial Lane.
Multiple large trees were downed over New Halls Ferry Road in Florissant.
Thunderstorm winds peeled a large amount of siding from a home and caused damage to the roof trim.
Thunderstorm winds caused roof damage to multiple homes in the area. Multiple trees were also downed.
Thunderstorm winds knocked a tree onto a home near the intersection of Harris and Lindbergh.
Thunderstorm winds knocked multiple limbs from trees. They also caused some roof damage to properties in the area.
Thunderstorm winds downed multiple trees in the area.

The tornado exited St. Charles County and passed into Alton in Madison County, IL at approximately 7:49 PM. In Alton, the tornado caused tree damage and minor damage to homes and farm outbuildings. It then dissipated at about 7:53 PM. In Madison County the tornado had a path length of 2.46 miles and a maximum path width of 430 yards. It was rated an EF1.

At approximately 9:52 PM a tornado began southwest of Valmeyer, IL in Monroe County and continued northeast where it impacted the towns of Valmeyer and Waterloo. The worst damage was to residences and small businesses within these municipalities. From Waterloo the tornado moved into a rural area where it produced minor tree damage along the Monroe/St. Clair County border. In Monroe County the tornado was rated EF-1 with a path length of 12.3 miles and maximum path width of 275 yards.

At approximately 10:28 PM a tornado began in the northeastern outskirts of O'Fallon, IL where it caused damage to multiple mobile homes, single family homes, outbuildings, and trees along its track northeast. The tornado then passed into southern Madison County. In Madison County the tornado was rated EF-1 with a path length of 6.75 miles and a maximum path width of 770 yards. In St. Clair County the tornado was rated EF-1 with a path length of 5.9 miles and a maximum path width of 450 yards.

The tornado crossed into Madison County where it lifted the roof off of a farm outbuilding near the intersection of Rose Road and Cedar Road. It dissipated shortly after at approximately 10:33 PM. In Madison County the tornado was rated EF-0 with a path length of 0.91 miles and a maximum path width of 25 yards.

The tornado then moved into rural St. Clair County where it caused minor tree damage northwest of Floraville. It was here where the tornado dissipated at approximately 10:15 PM. In St. Clair County the tornado was rated EF-0 with a path length of 2.37 miles and a maximum path width of 25 yards.

At approximately 10:30 PM, a tornado began near Scheve Park in Mascoutah. In Mascoutah the tornado caused roof damage to multiple residences as well as the local high school. Power poles and outbuildings were damaged as well. The most intense damage in town occurred near the intersection of Beechcraft Blvd and Fuesser Rd. The tornado continued northeast where it damaged a grain elevator and more farm outbuildings. The most significant damage in the county occurred near the Madison/Clinton County border where farm outbuildings were completely destroyed and residences sustained heavy roof and window damage. The tornado then crossed into Clinton County. In St. Clair County the tornado was rated EF-1 with a path length of 7.88 miles and a maximum path width of 700 yards.

The tornado caused significant roof damage to a home immediately after crossing into Clinton County. It continued to track northeast, causing additional damage to residences and outbuildings before entering the east side of Trenton. Here, the bulk of tornado damage consisted of minor roof damage, although one business did sustain significant damage to its siding and air conditioning units. The tornado dissipated in Trenton at approximately 10:39 PM. In Madison County the tornado was rated EF-2 with a path length of 3.13 miles and a maximum path width of 150 yards.

At approximately 11:11 PM a tornado began just southwest of Hagarstown, IL in Fayette County and continued northeastward for 13.4 miles through Vandalia, IL before dissipating southwest of Sefton, IL in Fayette County around 11:23 PM. The worst damage occurred northeast of Vandalia, where several trees were uprooted. This tornado was assigned a rating of EF-1 with a maximum wind speed of 90 mph.

In Randolph County, most tornado damage occurred to trees. A few outbuildings did sustain significant damage to their roofs along the track. The tornado dissipated near Leanderville at approximately 11:55 PM. In Randolph County the tornado was rated EF-1 with a path length of 6.63 miles and a maximum path width of 175 yards. This is a continuation of a tornado that caused EF-1 damage in Bollinger County, MO and EF-2 damage in Perry County, MO.
Thunderstorm winds overturned a semi-truck on the Illinois side of the Jefferson Barracks Bridge.
Thunderstorm winds downed trees in the area.
Thunderstorm winds felled a tree in Cahokia Heights. This tree fell on a house on Melvin Drive, injuring a 9 year old girl.
Thunderstorm winds snapped numerous branches from trees of various sizes.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down a large tree near a residence. It is unclear whether this tree was snapped or uprooted.
Thunderstorm winds caused damage to trees and sheds.
Thunderstorm winds caused damage to trees and outbuildings.
Thunderstorm winds snapped a large tree which fell onto a house and its deck.
Thunderstorm wind driven hail destroyed the siding and windows on numerous homes spanning entire neighborhoods in O'Fallon.
Thunderstorm winds destroyed a mobile home.
The St. Clair County emergency manager reported that thunderstorm winds downed power lines in more than 20 places spanning O'Fallon, Mascoutah, and Lebanon.
Thunderstorm winds damaged barns, silos, and outbuildings.
Thunderstorm winds damaged trees and outbuildings.
Thunderstorm winds damaged a shed and fence in Aviston.
The St. Clair County emergency manager reported an overturned mobile home with residents trapped inside.
Thunderstorm winds caused a home to collapse with two elderly residents inside.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted a 4 foot diameter pine tree.
Thunderstorm winds downed a large tree which then blocked Wolf Road near Westview Road.
Thunderstorm winds knocked a tree on a home, trapping two residents in the house.
Thunderstorm winds broke a light pole at ground level outside of Irvington Grade School.
Thunderstorm winds downed power lines which caused a minor fire.
The Centralia emergency manager reported multiple power lines downed due to thunderstorm winds.
Thunderstorm winds downed trees over Highway N and Highway 21 near Lesterville.
Thunderstorm winds downed a few power lines on Main Street in Dupo.
A member of the public reported estimated thunderstorm winds of 60 mph which is consistent with the ASOS observation at KCPS 10 minutes prior from the same thunderstorm.
Thunderstorm winds downed multiple trees near Albers.
Thunderstorm winds downed multiple trees near Bartelso.
Thunderstorm winds downed multiple trees near Beckemeyer.
Thunderstorm winds caused minor damage to a roof near Ramsey.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down a few powerlines in Salem. They also produced sporadic tree damage throughout the county.
Thunderstorm winds broke several large limbs off of trees.
Thunderstorm winds caused damage to a farm building.

At approximately 5:05 PM a tornado began northwest of Pierron in Bond County, IL, damaging a few trees. The tornado tracked northeast over Dolls Orchard Avenue, causing further tree damage while paralleling Interstate 70 to the south. The most significant damage was surveyed at the intersection of Millersburg Road and Cottonwood Avenue, where several structures were almost completely destroyed and debris lofted for nearly a mile. One injury was reported at this location. Significant tree damage was also observed, with several large trunks being sheared off and bark peeled back. The tornado continued northeast through the southern fringe of Greenville, causing minor tree and structural damage. Further weakening was observed as the tornado approached Mulberry Grove, where a barn collapsed. In Bond County the tornado had a path length of 19.85 miles with a path width of 200 yards. The tornado was rated EF2.

The tornado then crossed into Fayette County and caused minor tree damage southwest of Shafter before lifting at 5:29 PM. In Fayette County the tornado had a path length of 2.98 miles with a path width of 150 yards. The tornado was rated an EF0.

At 3:13 PM, a tornado began southwest of Berryman, MO in east-central Crawford County, producing damage to trees in the northern half of Mark Twain National Forest. In Crawford County the tornado had a path length of 2.32 miles with a maximum path width of 50 yards. It was rated an EF0.

The tornado then entered Washington County and crossed West State Highway 8 east of Berryman. The tornado continued northeast, damaging mobile homes and snapping trees around Cape Lakewood before approaching State Highway 185 and the town of Latty. Once there, the tornado strengthened and caused significant damage to homes in the northwest part of town. This damage was the worst observed, with winds estimated as strong as 165 mph. The tornado continued northeast into rural areas northwest of Old Mines before lifting at 3:39 PM. In Washington County the tornado had a path length of 19.63 miles with a maximum path width of 200 yards. It was rated an EF3.
A 58 mph thunderstorm wind gust was recorded by a highway sensor.
The ASOS at KSUS measured a 60 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
Thunderstorm winds knocked over a healthy hickory tree approximately 10 to 12 inches in diameter. The tree tilted over about 45 degrees from its roots and did not fall over completely.
The ASOS at KSUS measured a 58 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
Thunderstorm winds caused damage to a metal roof at the intersection of Route 15 and Route 13 in Freeburg.

What was likely a very brief tornado touched down somewhere in a field just north of the community of St. Libory and lifted shortly thereafter. Damage surveys revealed that a two-door garage/shed was destroyed, but surrounding trees and homes were largely untouched aside from a tipped over RV/trailer approximately 1 mile downstream. Given the very narrow scope of the damage, and the fact that debris from the destroyed garage was strewn several hundred yards downstream, it is more likely than not that this was a brief tornado, rather than straight-line winds. The tornado was rated EF-0 with a path length of 0.45 miles and a maximum path width of 25 yards.
Thunderstorm winds downed power lines and tree limbs near West Kell Road and North Cherry Road in Centralia.
Thunderstorm winds downed numerous trees and power lines throughout Salem. Some trees were blown onto homes.
Thunderstorm winds damaged a barn roof. A few pieces of sheet metal were strewn into a nearby field.
Thunderstorm winds destroyed a couple of outbuildings along Kinmundy Road just south of Williams Road.
Thunderstorm winds downed multiple trees around Forbes State Park.
Broadcast media relayed photos of 1.5 inch to 2 inch hailstones from social media.
An NWS employee reported hail falling that was at least quarter sized.

A brief, weak tornado touched down between Carlyle Lake and Pope near 6:30 PM and moved northeast. Along its track, the tornado removed several shingles from a home and caused tree damage. The tornado lifted near County Road 700 at approximately 6:38 PM. The tornado was rated EF-0 with a path length of 5.01 miles and a maximum path width of 50 yards.

Shortly before 7pm, the tornado formed just south of County Road 750 in Fayette County, southeast of Shobonier, damaging trees and structures at a farm. The tornado tracked northeastward through fields and pockets of trees before impacting farms along County Rd 1100. Shortly after this point, the tornado reached its maximum surveyed strength, where it leveled an outbuilding near the intersection of County Rd 1100 and E 900 Ave. The tornado continued northeastward, producing mainly tree damage and minor structural damage before dissipating shortly after crossing County Rd 1300 north of Augsburg. The tornado was rated EF-2 with a path length of 4.33 miles and a maximum path width of 150 yards.
Thunderstorm winds downed multiple 6 to 8 inch tree limbs in Clarksburg.
A mesonet station measured a 61 mph wind gust near California.
Multiple tree trunks were snapped on and around Sundeck Drive in Columbia.
The KCOU ASOS measured a 58 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
The KJEF ASOS measured a 66 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
Thunderstorm winds caused tree damage of varying degrees from downed limbs to uprooted trees.
Thunderstorm winds caused roof damage to the Parkade Baptist Church in Columbia.
A member of the public reported wind gusts estimated to be 65 mph.
The Columbia-Bradford Missouri Agricultural site measured a 66 mph thunderstorm wind gust.

The NWS surveyed straight-line wind damage at a farm north-northwest of Kingdom City. Photos of the damage were provided by county law enforcement and showed extensive damage to multiple farm outbuildings. Large, healthy tree branches were also snapped on the property.
Thunderstorm winds snapped a 2 foot diameter tree at its base.
The Vandalia Agricultural Site measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 63 mph.
Thunderstorm winds caused damage to sheds on a property. They also caused damage to a support column and the wall of a home.

Two sources reported estimated 70 mph thunderstorm wind gusts west of Hannibal. Multiple instances of damage around Hannibal due to thunderstorm winds were reported, including the destruction of a trailer near Hannibal Regional Hospital.
Thunderstorm winds downed a large tree across a road in town.
Thunderstorm winds downed power lines in De Soto.
Thunderstorm winds downed power lines at Camilla Street and Polk Avenue near Park Hills. They also downed power lines in Desloge.
A trained spotter reported estimated 60 mph thunderstorm wind gusts.
Thunderstorm winds downed power poles along Illinois Route 57 near Hull. This is not to be confused with Interstate 57.
Thunderstorm winds snapped and uprooted several trees near Fall Creek.
Thunderstorm winds destroyed a barn near Ursa.
Thunderstorm winds lifted off a portion of a school's old gym roof.
Thunderstorm winds snapped a large tree about 5 feet above its base.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down trees in Grafton.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree over Vogel School Road just north of Floraville.
Thunderstorm winds snapped multiple trees and toppled several at their base.
Thunderstorm winds downed power poles west of Hecker.
Broadcast media reported estimated 65 mph thunderstorm wind gusts in Waterloo. They also reported visibility near zero statute miles coinciding with the wind gust.
Thunderstorm winds downed trees crossing Illinois Route 15.
Thunderstorm winds damaged 2 grain silos and a handful of other farm buildings.
Thunderstorm winds snapped several large tree limbs in Centralia.
The AWOS at Salem measured a 58 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
Thunderstorm winds downed numerous tree branches.
Thunderstorm winds downed a utility pole in Coulterville.

Illinois Route 153 north of Lively Grove was reportedly under 1 foot of water due to heavy rain. Heavy rain also caused ponding in fields to the south of Lively Grove, resulting in water flowing over Route 153.

Heavy rain caused ponding in the park across from Salem Community High School with 2 to 3 feet of flowing water across the parking lot. Nearby, a member of the public reported minor flooding due to Crooked Creek overflowing.

A brief tornado touched down just west of Bates Creek Camp near Potosi during the afternoon. Here, the tornado caused building and tree damage. Most notably it destroyed the garage of a home in Bates Creek Camp. The tornado then moved northeast into southern Potosi, causing tree damage along the way. It then lifted near Washington County Memorial Hospital where it caused minor tree damage. The tornado was rated EF-1 with a path length of 4.24 miles and a maximum path width of 150 yards.
Thunderstorm winds knocked a tree down over the road at Missouri Route O and Highway 32.

The tornado touched down south of County Road 362 at 1:31 PM and quickly strengthened, blowing in the garage and removing a significant section of roof from a home along County Road 362. This was the worst observed damage and was rated as 120 mph (EF-2). The tornado then moved north-northeast, crossing State Road Y and removing siding from a church along Blessing Lane. The tornado dissipated along County Road 347 at 1:36 PM. Additional damage along the path mainly consisted of tree damage. The tornado was rated EF-2 with a path length of 2.61 miles and a maximum path width of 100 yards.

The tornado touched down at 5:18 PM about one mile north of Columbia along Rangeline Road. The tornado moved east, producing tree damage before passing just north of Albert-Oakland Park. Beyond Albert-Oakland Park the tornado took a northeast turn and crossed Highway 63. The tornado continued producing tree damage as it moved northeast toward Paris Road. The tornado was rated EF-1 with a path length of 3.31 miles and a maximum path width of 100 yards.

A brief tornado tracked south to north just west of Highway MM in north-central Audrain County, destroying a couple of outbuildings and rolling two smaller grain bins. Debris was generally thrown northward and strewn widely, likely due to a downburst immediately following the tornado. The tornado was rated EF-1 with a path length of 0.32 miles and a maximum path width of 50 yards.

A brief tornado tracked northeast near Highway E, 2 miles northeast of the community of Spencerburg where it caused significant damage to an outbuilding and a few trees. The tornado was rated EF-0 with a path length of 0.34 miles and a maximum path width of 25 yards.

A weak tornado began near the intersection of Highways 172 and 57, and traveled roughly 4.2 miles to the northeast before dissipating. Damage to trees was most common, with some damage to bleachers as well. The tornado was rated EF-0 with a path length of 4.18 miles and a maximum path width of 25 yards.

A weak tornado touched down along Hickman Road at 7:04 PM and destroyed an outbuilding with winds estimated as strong as 85 mph. It then moved northeast through Bailey Park and produced roof damage to another outbuilding along E 2400th Street near N 2150th Ave. The tornado continued to move northeast past Golden, IL and produced roof damage to multiple outbuildings along E 2700th Street between N 2500th Ave and N 2600th Ave before dissipating just north of N 2600th Ave at 7:10 PM. The tornado was rated EF-0 with a path length of 8.17 miles and a maximum path width of 100 yards.

The tornado touched down at 8:00 PM along Koch Road, southeast of Madonnaville, and moved northeast, producing minor damage to a home and an outbuilding along Rock Road. Further to the northeast along LRC Road the tornado overturned an outbuilding and caused tree damage. More tree damage and minor outbuilding roof damage occurred along JJ road as the tornado tracked northeast between Wartburg and Burksville. The tornado moved into southern Waterloo and produced minor roof damage to one of the greenhouses at Waterloo High School before turning to the east and damaging power poles along Highway 156. The power pole damage was the worst damage and winds were estimated as high as 100 mph (EF-1). The tornado dissipated shortly thereafter at 8:07 PM.The tornado was rated EF-1 with a path length of 7.33 miles and a maximum path width of 100 yards.

A brief and weak tornado touched down along EE Road just south of Gilmore Lake and quickly moved northeast before dissipating at the intersection of EE Road and Gilmore Lake Road at 8:13 PM. When the tornado touched down it overturned an outbuilding, and was rated at 99 mph (EF-1) at this point. Tree damage was also recorded. The tornado dissipated shortly thereafter at 8:07 PM.The tornado was rated EF-1 with a path length of 0.35 miles and a maximum path width of 100 yards.

A brief and weak tornado touched down on Schwab Road, southwest of Millstadt at 8:14 PM. It destroyed an outbuilding and produced tree damage along Schwab Road with winds estimated as high as 85 mph. The tornado dissipated shortly thereafter at 8:15 PM. The tornado was rated EF-0 with a path length of 0.75 miles and a maximum path width of 100 yards.

The tornado touched down on Baldwin Road at 8:25 PM, producing tree damage with winds estimated around 70 mph. The tornado then moved northeast and uprooted and snapped trees along Ridge Road. The snapped trees were the worst damage, with winds estimated as high as 93 mph. Moving northeastward, the tornado removed the roof of a grain silo along Pearidge Road before lifting at 8:26 PM just east of Pearidge Road. The tornado was rated EF-1 with a path length of 1.32 miles and a maximum path width of 75 yards.

A member of the public measured 1.32 inches having fallen 1 mile southwest of Warrenton just before reports of flooding started coming in. All reports came from the emergency manager and all locations listed typically flood when heavy rain falls. Spots include: Highway O at Walnut Crest, Highway F at South Stracks Church Road, Schreckengast Road at Cedar Lake Cellars, and Highway J at BMC Stone Quarry.

Broadcast media and members of the public reported various instances of flooding in St. Louis County. This ranged from Deer Creek flooding outside of its banks in Town and Country and Shady Grove Creek flooding outside of its banks in Webster Groves. Deep standing water along Wild Horse Creek Road in Chesterfield was also reported due to Wildhorse Creek having risen out of its banks. In Black Jack, Cold Water Creek rose out of its banks as well. Rainfall amounts across the county vary from 2.5 to 6.3 inches ending on April 6th.

Multiple instances of flash flooding were reported in St. Louis County due to heavy rain. Reports of flash flooding varied across the county. One report stated there was 2 to 3 feet of standing water on a road adjacent to Wildhorse Creek near Chesterfield. Another was of a stranded vehicle at the intersection of I-70 and I-270. Cold Water Creek also rose out of its banks in Hazelwood and entered the parking garage of the Hazelwood Civic Center on Dunn Road. The same creek came about 1 foot from reaching businesses on Bypasse Drive in Hazelwood. There was also a public report of roads closed due to flooding in Oakville. Rainfall amounts across the county vary from 2.5 to  6.3 inches ending on April 6th.

Heavy rain across St. Louis County and upstream caused the Meramec River at Valley Park to rise into major flood. Floodwaters seeped onto Missouri Route 141, closing the road at its intersection with I-44 for 2 days (April 8 - 10) while the river crested and began to retreat. Multiple cars became stuck in the floodwater, but no injuries were reported.

Heavy rain caused Joachim Creek to rise out of its banks near Crystal City and Valles Mill and caused Saline Creek to rise out of its banks in Jefferson County west of Fults, IL. Up to 7 inches of rain fell in portions of Jefferson County between April 4th and the evening of April 5th.

Heavy rain caused a few road closures in Jefferson County. One road closure was near Regina on Missouri BB and Regina Road. Here, downed power poles were reported. The other was near Imperial around US Highway 61/67 and Scott Lane/Mill Creek Drive/Montebello Road.

Heavy rain on the scale of 9 to 11 inches caused Dry Creek near Bismarck and Indian Creek near Iron Mountain Lake. Near Farmington, 6 inches of water was reported on Maple Street, and Westmeyer Road had an estimated foot of running water over it. An older model Chevy Trailblazer drove through the water and floated to the other side. This is a persistent issue when nearby creeks such as Wolf Creek and Kennedy Branch flood.

Multiple water rescues were reported in St. Francois County, one in Blackwell and another in an unnamed location in northern St. Francois County. Near Libertyville, an estimated 3 feet of water was running swiftly across Highway DD into a small lake across the street. The lake was reportedly spilling onto the road.

An emergency manager reported multiple vehicles trapped in high water on I-70 eastbound under the East Carrie Street overpass. This is a low area. A vehicle was also trapped in flood waters in St. Louis at Lindell Boulevard and Vandeventer Avenue. These areas received between 2 and 4 inches of rain.

Heavy rain resulted in lots of running water over Highway 94 near Terri Road. This made the road completely impassable. Near St. Paul, there were reports of heavy flooding north of Dalbow Road, though the extent of the flooding is unknown. Otherwise, there was a report of Dardenne Creek overflowing in St. Peters. This area received anywhere from 3 to 6.5 inches of rain over the duration of the event.

The Department of Highways and the public reported multiple inaccessible roads in Franklin County due to flooding. These include parts of Highway A and Highway YY due to side ditches overflowing and Highway CC due to Big Creek flooding over the road and onto the other side. Notably, this is a low point on the highway. On April 5th, the Missouri Department of Transportation reported that Route W just past Sand Ford Road at the entrance to Meramec Caverns was closing due to flooding of the Meramec River. Franklin County received up to 6.2 inches of rain during this event.

Several road closures were reported mainly in the Ellington area has rainwater flooded roadways and areal creeks overflowed. Examples of road closures include: MO 106 1 mile west of Route F, Route B between CR 785 and CR 784, and CR 838 at its intersection with CR 837. Logan Creek overflowed, making its bridge on Route B impassable and causing extensive damage to the bridge.

The Missouri Department of Transportation has reported multiple road closures in Iron County due to flooding that began on April 3rd. Some of these closures continued into May. Road closures include: Route F from CR 160 to CR 135, Route 40 at Route BB, and Route F from Missouri 49 to CR 165. Over the duration of the event, portions of Iron County received up to 7.5 inches of rain.

Fourche a Du Clos flooded over Highway Y at Jackson School Road deeming it impassable through the first low bottom bridge headed eastbound. A water rescue was reported at this location. On April 5th, water was reported over the roadway near Missouri 32. During the event, portions of Ste. Genevieve County received 3.75 to 6.25 inches of rainfall.
The Dent Branch of the Big River was reportedly swiftly running over Highway C where a bridge crosses the road. Rainfall totals through the event were on the order of 2.5 to 4.3 inches.

The 911 Call Center reported numerous events in Fredericktown including water over the roadway at Morley St and Villar St, City Lake Road, Buford Boulevard, Highway Z and North Chamber Drive, the 200 block of East College, and North Main Street. Southeast of town, Route F was closed where it meets Route V due to flooding. During the event, up to 7.75 inches of rain fell in Madison County.

A water rescue took place on Illinois Highway 13 near Lenzburg due to a vehicle being stranded in flood water. Heavy rain of up to 5.25 to 6.1 inches fell in St. Clair County during the duration of the event.

Town Creek in Salem rose rapidly due to heavy rain and was level with Eastlawn Cemetery and Tully Park. The emergency manager in Salem issued a voluntary evacuation of Starlight Mobile Home Park, which occurs anytime flooding conditions of this scale are present. A majority of main routes in and out of Salem were inundated with water and closed with cars floating in the floodwater down West Main Street. The reservoir overflow channel was topped and water flowed into the town park and inundated homes to its south. In Centralia, 4 to 5 fete of water covered Locust Street near a major production facility. Heavy rains of up to 8.5 inches fell during the event.

Numerous roadways across Washington County were deemed impassable due to floodwater. Nearby communities to these roadways include Nashville, Okawville, Lively Grove, Saint Libory, Addieville, Hoyleton, Covington, New Minden, Venedy, Beaucoup, and Wamac. Over the duration of the event, up to 7 inches of rain fell. At times, rain rates were in excess of 2 inches per hour.

Heavy rain caused several feet of water over County Road 18, leading to a vehicle becoming submerged. The occupant was safe. Route 4 north of Sparta also had water over the roadway. During the event, up to 4.5 inches of rain fell in Randolph County.

A brief tornado developed just east of Hinkson Creek at 5:33 PM where it caused significant damage to the Columbia Recycling Facility. The building was completely destroyed and the machinery inside significantly damaged. The tornado continued moving northeast, causing more tree damage before dissipating just north of E Highway HH along N Deer Valley Lane at 5:35 PM.
Several trees were blown over.  Also, a couple of homes sustained minor roof damage when shingles were blown off.
Several trees were blown down along Interstate 64, just north of Scott Airforce Base.

Thunderstorm winds blew over a machine shed about 2 miles south of Highland on Illinois Route 160.  Some equipment that had been inside the shed were damaged.  Also, another building on the same farm had about a third of its western wall blown out and a 14 foot sliding door on the shed was blown 500 feet off its rollers and over the top of another building.  Several power lines and numerous tree limbs were blown down in the area.

A bus barn for the Liberty High School had its roof blown off.  Three buses had minor damage and the metal roof sections were blown across the running track and a nearby road.  Also, a power pole was snapped in half.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs in Worden.  One tree limb landed on an unoccupied truck causing minor damage.
Several power lines were blown down in Pocahontas.

Numerous tree limbs were blown down around town.  Also, a 55 foot tree was blown over crashing through a fence and into a back yard.  The tree was alive but hollow.  Several power lines were blown down as well.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted a large tree and blew down a couple of fences in town.
Numerous large tree limbs were blown down around town.

Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree onto Illinois Route 140 at the intersection with Pokey Road, just east of Old Ripley.  In Greenville, several large tree limbs were blown down around town.  One fell onto Third Street, blocking it for a couple of hours until it could be removed.
Thunderstorm winds flattened corn fields to the east and southeast of Hillsboro.

Between 2 and 4 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils.  This caused flash flooding.  Several secondary roads were flooded including Highway C, west of La Grange.  Eight to twelve inches of water was flowing over Highway C.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines as well as numerous tree limbs.
Thunderstorm winds blew 2 semis off of U.S. Highway 61, 3 miles south of Hannibal.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a couple of power lines and trees onto Highway 79 on the north side of Louisiana.
Numerous large tree limbs were blown down.
Numerous large tree limbs and several power lines were blown down.
Thunderstorm winds downed power lines in Edina. Knox County Dispatch also reported one tree down in the town of Baring.
Thunderstorm winds downed trees, causing Highway BB to be blocked near Rocheport.
Thunderstorm winds knocked a large tree onto power lines at the intersection of Hamilton and Dickerson in Palmyra. This caused a power outage that affected about 100 residences.
Heavy rain caused waters on Camp Creek to rise out of their banks. This resulted in flooding at Camp Creek Lane and Highway O where a police truck was moved by flood water.

NWS Storm Survey found that an EF-1 tornado formed just east of Hwy 109 in Wildwood at 2:50pm and tracked northeastward. It dissipated in the Chesterfield Valley just south of the Missouri River at 3:00pm. The tornado was rated EF-1 with a path length of 6.81 miles and a maximum path width of 300 yards.

Heavy rain caused Jacobs Station Road near Towers Road to flood. Neighborhood yards also had about 1 foot of water in them. 2 miles west of Harvester, there was maybe a foot of water over an unnamed road. A small 2 door car stalled in these waters. Dardenne Creek rose onto St. Peters Howell Road. Up to 1 foot deep water was reported in nearby homes from the creek.

NWS storm survey concluded an EF-1 tornado touched down in southern Jefferson County. The tornado mostly produced tree damage and minor structural damage. The highest degree of damage occurred at its beginning where it caused two homes to slide off their foundations. The tornado had max winds of 105mph, was 4.9 miles long, and had a maximum width of 300 yards.

An EF-0 tornado briefly touched down and remained on the ground for about 1.25 miles, resulting in removal of a large portion of a barn roof, roof damage to a home, and notable damage to a number of trees. The tornado was rated EF-0 with a path length of 1.25 miles and a maximum path width of 65 yards.
Thunderstorm winds downed two trees of unknown size in the yard of the person reporting.
Thunderstorm winds knocked multiple trees onto power lines in Florissant. More trees were downed near Shackelford and New Halls Ferry Roads.

An EF-1 tornado moved through parts of eastern Pike County, MO south of Clarksville, damaged a few homes and trees from 10:55 AM to 10:58 AM CDT. The most severe damage was to a 70 year old home where most of the roof was caved in. Here, a 9 year old boy sheltered in a bathtub during the tornado and was unharmed. The tornado was rated EF-1 with a path length of 2.96 miles and a maximum path width of 100 yards.

The EF-1 tornado from Pike County, MO then crossed into Calhoun County between 10:58 and 10:59 AM as evidenced by multiple videos on social media. No damage was found in Illinois. The tornado was rated an EF-U with a path length of 0.6 miles.
Broadcast media from KSDK sent in a video of measured 2 inch hailstones.
Thunderstorm winds downed several trees and power lines across Franklin County. Several vehicle accidents along I-44 were reported at this time as well.
A Washington School District official submitted a photo of half dollar size hail.
The Warren County emergency manager reported golf ball sized hail at Marthasville.

Multiple reports came in of downed power poles and power lines in the area. 12 power poles were downed near Highway N and Money Drive as well as Highway N between Highway K and Bryan Road. 4 power poles were downed cutting off the entrance/exit to a neighborhood 1 mile northeast of Dardenne Prairie.
Golf ball sized hail 3ENE of our office specifically.
Hail persisted for 10 or more minutes.
The caller also reported estimated 60 mph winds with the hail.
A photo of the hail was provided by Spectrum News.
The photo of the hailstone was received via social media.
The photo of the hailstone was received via X.
Emergency management relayed a photo of a hailstone.
Thunderstorm winds shattered the windows of a business in Chesterfield. Numerous injuries were reported, but the exact number is unknown.
An official from the City of Chesterfield submitted a photo of 2 inch hail.
Half dollar sized hail was reported in Overland and Charlack.
Thunderstorm winds downed numerous trees and wires in northern Jefferson County around the High Ridge and Saline Valley area.

NWS Survey determined a tornado touched down in west Clayton, twisting power poles, guttering, and trees as it tracked east. In Richmond Heights, the tornado blew out the windows of St. Mary's Hospital. It also damaged its exterior and threw insulation and metal around the area. At Washington University large fences and trees were blown over. The tornado then continued into St. Louis City.

The tornado was its widest and strongest in St. Louis City. After it crossed into the City, the tornado caused major tree and structural damage in and around Forest Park and its northern neighborhoods. The then EF-3 tornado continued northeast into North St. Louis City where 4 individuals lost their lives. Continuing northeast still, the tornado began to weaken. Overall, thousands of buildings were damaged in St. Louis City costing an estimated $1.6 billion in damages.
Hail fell near Clearview and Hatherly in north city.
An EF-2 tornado touched down in Des ARc and tracked for 3.26 miles. Some buildings damaged by a tornado on March 14th were damaged again by this tornado.
An NWS employee received this information from a family member in the area.
Quarter sized hail fell at US 61 and Market Street in Ste. Genevieve.
Hail fell near KREI Radio in Farmington.
Quarter sized hail fell at St. Charles Rock Road and McKelvey Road.
Thunderstorm winds damaged a carport near Affton.

A man was driving on Grand Drive in Carondelet Park when a tree was uprooted and collapsed on his truck. He was killed instantly. This was not due to the tornado but possibly from rear flank downdraft winds on the south side of the supercell.
Thunderstorm winds snapped large tree branches near Highland.
Thunderstorm winds felled trees and powerlines in the area.
Thunderstorm winds snapped numerous large trees in the area.
There were several reports of trees and power lines down over northern St. Clair County.

After crossing from St. Louis City, the tornado weakened. It caused EF-1 structural and tree damage in Granite City and Pontoon Beach before dissipating near Southern Illinois University - Edwardsville.
Quarter sized hail fell near Pontoon Road and Maryville Road in Granite City.
Thunderstorm winds snapped one large tree branch from a large healthy tree.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down tree limbs that were 12 inches in diameter. The caller reported estimated winds of 70 mph.
Thunderstorm winds knocked a tree down across the intersection of Summerfield Road and Lilac Road.
Thunderstorm winds knocked one tree down. The tree took out a transformer and power pole as it fell.
Thunderstorm winds downed one large tree.
Thunderstorm winds downed trees near Route 16 and Route 127.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted a few small trees in Taylor Springs.
Thunderstorm winds downed multiple power poles in Patoka.
Thunderstorm winds caused tree damage of an unknown extent throughout Carlinville.
Thunderstorm winds caused the walls of a brick outbuilding to collapse after its roof was ripped off.
An NWS Storm Survey revealed an EF-U tornado northwest of Olympian Village.
Thunderstorm winds downed numerous trees near Mapaville.
A picture of a 2 inch hailstone was submitted via Twitter with a measurement.
Cole County Dispatch reported several trees with limbs down in rural Cole County.
A few quarter sized hailstones fell east of Maryland Heights.
Missouri State Highway Patrol reported golf ball sized hail in Florissant.
A brief tornado touched down in far northern Iron County where it downed and damaged numerous trees along Highway DD. The tornado then continued into Washington County.
The tornado crossed the Iron/Washington County line where it continued to uproot and damage trees. It dissipated at 20:01 along Highway DD just north of its junction with Martin Road.
The spotter also observed winds estimated around 40 mph.

Thunderstorm winds downed two trees near the split of US 61 and US 24 at the intersection of Route F south of Palmyra. These trees blocked traffic at this intersection. Northeast of Palmyra, thunderstorm winds downed trees along Missouri 168 near Route JJ.

A tornado touched down near Eight Wheeler Road outside of Richwoods and caused tree damage as it moved north-northeast before dissipating just north of Highway H. The peak wind speed was 80 mph and the path was 2.21 miles long and 140 yards wide.
A brief tornado touched down on County Road 920 south of its junction with County Road 926. The tornado produced tree damage before heading northeast and dissipating just north of County Road 906.
Thunderstorm winds downed a powerline on the south side of Cuba. To the southwest, thunderstorm winds damaged and uprooted numerous large trees in Davisville.

A tornado touched down along Hobo Road near Cherryville and moved north-northeast, quickly producing tree damage and destroying a farm outbuilding before dissipating. The peak wind speed was 107 mph and the track was 1.03 miles long and 270 yards wide.

In De Soto, thunderstorm winds damaged trees near Highway 100 and Fountain City Road. In Mapaville, thunderstorm winds snapped two 12 inch diameter tree branches. These branches landed on and damaged a soft metal fence in the reporter's backyard.
Thunderstorm winds downed numerous trees across Ironton and Pilot Knob.

A tornado touched down in Iron Mountain causing tree damage and minor roof damage before moving northeast. From there, the tornado moved northeast causing similar damage on Highway N and severely damaging a home's roof on Lake Avalon Road. The tornado dissipated shortly after.
Thunderstorm winds downed powerlines in Park Hills and trees in Farmington.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted, snapped, and topped numerous large trees west and northwest of Bloomsdale. This wind damage is separate from a confirmed tornado that occurred nearby.
A brief tornado touched down near Dry Fork, uprooting trees. From there the tornado tracked northeast, causing more tree damage before dissipating near Cindy Lane.
Thunderstorm winds downed numerous tree limbs, including snapping and uprooting a few larger trees.

Two of three lanes of I-64 westbound at Forest Park and Hampton became flooded and impassable. Several cars became stuck in flood water. This is a low spot and typically has high water when heavy rain falls.
A spotter reported 2.6 inches of rain falling between 20:30 CST and 00:15 CST. Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in the city of St. Louis.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree and branches onto the roadway near the intersection of State Highway 104 and East 2400th Street southeast of Liberty.
An emergency manager reported a subject stuck in her car in a foot of flood water between 12th Street and 18th Street on Seminary Road.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree which blocked traffic along Spring Lake Road near Atlas. Near Pittsfield, a tree fell on a vehicle.
Thunderstorm winds knocked numerous tree limbs down and caused minor cosmetic damage to a home.

A brief tornado touched down just south of Prairie du Rocher, destroying an outbuilding before heading north-northeast. From there the tornado caused tree damage and damaged another farm outbuilding before dissipating just southwest of Route 155.
Thunderstorm winds downed tree limbs across Fredericktown.
Thunderstorm winds blew one large tree limb down in Harvester.
An NWS employee estimated thunderstorm wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph. These winds downed small tree limbs.
Several large tree limbs and trees were reported downed in a swath from Webster Groves/Shrewsbury southeast through Marlborough and Wilbur Park/Affton.
Thunderstorm winds snapped healthy tree branches of up to 6 inches in diameter.
Thunderstorm winds knocked over a large tree. The tree blocked the roadway at Highway 124 and Barnes School Road.
Thunderstorm winds downed multiple tree limbs on Parkwood Drive. In the Park Charles neighborhood, thunderstorm winds caused lots of damage to trees and knocked out the power.

Thunderstorm winds downed several trees at the Sunbrook Apartment Complex. Near Ehlmann Road, there was significant damage from winds including light poles being blown over and trees up to 60 feet in height being uprooted. To the southeast at Clemens Drive and Dawson Road a power pole was downed.
Thunderstorm winds downed multiple trees and wires in Caseyville and Collinsville.
Thunderstorm winds downed a large tree across Route 4 in Lebanon.
Thunderstorm winds knocked multiple trees onto power lines in Nokomis.
A brief EF-0 tornado occurred near Bingham causing damage to a few farm outbuildings and crops. Video evidence confirmed the tornado.
A home in Ramsey saw significant basement flooding, including walls being knocked down by flood waters.

A video submitted recorded extensive standing water and flooding along Madison Street including the parking lot of Ace Hardware Store. Water was reportedly several inches deep in the backyard of a home nearby, and flood water seeped into their basement. A total of 5.04 inches of rain fell in Lebanon within a 2.5 hour span. Nearby Summerfield also received 5 inches of rain, but flash flooding was not reported here.
An amateur radio operator reported a measured wind gust of 68 mph in Auxvasse.
Thunderstorm winds downed multiple tree limbs in the area. Billboards were blown away and an RV was tipped over at the I-70 RV Center. Multiple RVs were damaged.

Fredrock Glampground received 4 inches of rain in 1.5 hours. This resulted in Twelvemile Creek overtopping a private bridge and making portions of the campground inaccessible. Near Saco, a portion of a resident's property were inaccessible due to road washouts.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree approximately 2.5 feet in diameter.
Thunderstorm winds downed 2 trees in Hannibal. The trees were approximately 2.5 feet in diameter.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down a large tree which blocked Highway 79 at an unknown location.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down a tree onto Highway NN.
Thunderstorm winds blew down trees and powerlines around Quincy.
Thunderstorm winds downed a power pole near Elsberry.
Thunderstorm winds knocked electric lines down at Fox Run Road and Vee Valley Farms.
A HAM radio operator reported 60 mph wind gusts and up to 8 inch tree limbs down near Bluebird Lane and Illinois Route 109.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree in the Godfrey area.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree at the Ramsey substation. The storm then moved southeast where it snapped tree limbs of up to 4 inches in diameter in St. Elmo.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree in the general location of this point.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree on Valley Road.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree along Route 66.

Heavy rain caused flash flood conditions on Route 13 south of Freeburg where 4 to 5 feet of water flooded the road. One car also stalled in water on US-50 west of Trenton where both directions were flooded.
A caller reported that 4.05 inches of rain fell in 2 hours in St. Rose. Here, 2 to 3 feet of water was reportedly covering roads.
Thunderstorm winds knocked a tree onto a home in Pittsfield. The tree was about 12 inches in diameter.
Individual reported quarter sized hail that was 2 to 3 inches deep on the ground.
Quarter sized hail fell about halfway between Auxvasse and Mexico.
Wind driven hail caused extensive damage to west facing homes and buildings.
The Columbia police department reported hail between quarter and golf ball sized.

Multiple towns and municipalities in northern Fayette County were affected by flash flooding according to emergency management, broadcast media, law enforcement/fire, and members of the public. In Wrights Corner, multiple roads had at least several inches of water covering them, with the intersection of N 2800 and County Road 2 having 3 to 6 feet of water on it. In Ramsey, rain rates of greater than 3 inches per hour caused 3 to 5 inches of water over the road at 8th Street and Fayette Street. The Ramsey Blacktop outside of town was also impassable due to water over the road. Near St. Elmo, a car was stalled in knee-deep water and the fire department was called to rescue the stranded individual. In Avena, US-40 was impassable due to flooding, and a vehicle and fire truck became stuck in around 2 feet of water. In Brownstown, a family's car became stuck in flood water, but they were able to walk out on their own. Near Shafter, a vehicle became stuck in flood water at County Road 2200 and N 200. E 1500 was flooded out in Saint James. Near Vandalia, a vehicle rolled over in 4 feet of flood water on I-70. Overall, this area received up to 13.5 inches of rain with 7.39 inches falling in 4.25 hours.
Heavy rain caused a culvert to wash out on Polk Avenue. This destroyed Polk Avenue north of Greenville.

Multiple roads were closed in Lincoln County due to heavy rainfall. These include Highway A outside of Hawk Point, Highway P in Elsberry, Highway B at Bryant's Creek Road, Highway C in multiple locations near Moscow Mills, Highway H near the Cuivre River due to water exceeding the river's banks, and numerous other unnamed roads. On Highway 61 near Davis, vehicles were stopped due to water on the road at multiple locations, including its intersections with County Roads K,V,B, and E.

Heavy rain caused numerous roads to become impassable in Audrain County. These include Highway 54 in Farber, two unnamed roads north of Laddonia, many roads in Laddonia proper, Highway BB just west of Highway W near Middletown, and Highway J at Highway B north of Rush Hill. A water rescue was completed on Highway 54 between Farber and Bassinger Corner. Another vehicle was stuck in water in front of the POET Biorefinery. A third vehicle was stuck in water on Highway 19 in Martinsburg.

Heavy rain resulted in 42 water rescues in Lincoln County. The only official report of a road closure was MO-79 at Brownsmill Road where swift moving floodwater was reported. In Elsberry, 50 homes and 20 to 30 businesses were affected by the flooding, and a state of emergency was declared.

The Calhoun County sheriff reported at least 5 trees across roads around Hamburg. The closed roads in the county include Route 100, Michael Hamburg Road, Treshman Hollow Road, Irish Hollow Road, Gresham Hollow Road, East Panther Creek Road, and Indian Creek Hollow Road. Several of these roads were closed due to pavement or culverts being washed out.
Thunderstorm winds caused a large tree limb to snap and fall onto a vehicle.
Thunderstorm winds snapped several trees in and around Palmyra, including a large tree that fell on the roof of a home.

Thunderstorm winds downed several large, healthy branches and power lines near Pevely. The canopy at the Mr. Fuel Travel Center had large sections blown off with several trees in the vicinity snapped or uprooted.

At around 6 AM CDT, deputies were called to the seen of an overturned vehicle with an individual thrown from it at the intersection of Fountain and Levee Roads. The person was pronounced dead at the scene. The official investigation determined that extreme fog was the cause of the accident.
A brief EF-1 tornado struck a farm just northeast of Leonard, MO on Shelby 129.

A brief EF-1 tornado touched down just east of Leonard and moved northeast. The tornado caused damage to farm structures, homes, and trees along its short track before dissipating just west of Highway BB.
Thunderstorm winds downed 4 inch branches between Leonard and Highway J just east of Highway W.
A backyard anemometer recorded a 58 mph wind gust. Minor tree damage was reported along with the gust.
A Marion County ambulance at Highway 6 and Highway V in Maywood had to pull over due to estimated 70+ mph winds, zero visibility, and heavily leaning trees.
A spotter estimated 60 mph winds on the west side of Quincy.
A resident of Adams County reported a 65 mph wind gust.
Thunderstorm winds downed numerous tree limbs 12 to 18 inches in diameter. A few trees were downed in an area from Grand Ave to Jefferson Ave north of 5th Street.
The ASOS at Lambert International Airport measured a wind gust of 58 mph from microburst winds. Shortly after, a large oak tree fell onto a home causing significant damage.
Thunderstorm winds downed many tree limbs which took down powerlines. Winds caused roof damage to two buildings.

Thunderstorm winds downed multiple trees along Spring Bluff Road and Highway 185. They also downed 2 limbs: an 8 inch diameter tree limb along Karen Ann Circle and a 10-12 inch diameter tree limb along George Street in Sullivan.
Thunderstorm winds snapped a large tree branch and removed large patches of shingles from a house.
Flash flooding led to the road closures of several interstates including I-44, I-55, I-64, and I-70.
A trained spotter on St. Louis Ave in East Alton reported half inch to 1 inch sized sized hail.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down power lines and caused damage to structures near Alton.
Thunderstorm winds caused minor damage to an outbuilding including a few broken windows.  Also, numerous large tree limbs were blown down.
Between 3 and 5 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing some roads to be flooded, including Route ZZ on the west side of Columbia, between I-70 and Route TT.
Thunderstorm winds blew over a large oak tree onto a business causing around $100,000 in damage.  Also, the tree fell onto 2 garages destroying them and damaging 3 vehicles inside them.
Thunderstorm winds snapped off a large tree at its base and blew down numerous large tree limbs.  Also, a carport was destroyed.

Over 5 inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded and closed for a time including U.S. Highway 36 east of Letner and east of Shelbina.  Also, Highway 15 was closed in spots, Highway 151 was closed north of Clarence and Routes N, J, AA and K were closed in spots.  Several motorists had to be rescued after driving into water over 18 inches deep on U.S. Highway 36 east of Shelbina.
Between 3 and 5 inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded and several vehicles were stranded in the flood waters requiring water rescues.

Between 4 and 6 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Highway 19 southwest of Center and Route B south of Perry.  There was severe flooding on Lick Creek which washed away several large unoccupied camping trailers.  One business in the area was inundated by 4 feet of water from Lick Creek in the office and shop area.  Also, the water washed away around 140 boats from the business, though most only sustained minor damage from the flood waters.  About 20 boats were severely damaged or destroyed.  A nearby home was flooded as well.  Highway 19 was closed due to 2 to 3 feet of water flowing over it southwest of Center.  Two men had to be rescued from a tree after they drove into these flood waters and their vehicle was swept off Highway 19 near Route EE.
Between 3 and 5 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including State Route 15 east of Novelty.

Between 3 and 5 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded and closed for a time including...Highway 154 west of Curryville, Route M south of Curryville, Route V and Route Y.
MoDOT reported water over the roadway at northbound I-55 at I-255.

Heavy rain resulted in 15 cars being stranded on I-70 at Saint Louis Ave with the eastbound lane being closed for 30 minutes while firemen worked on clearing drains. Additional street flooding was reported to the west along Saint Louis Ave to Jefferson Ave where 5 to 6 inches of rainwater covered the street. Jefferson Ave was closed at Madison St due to water covering the roadway. To the southeast, water covered the roadway at 13th St at North Tucker Blvd and 13th Street at Cole Street. MoDOT also reported water over the roadway at I-44 and I-64 near the Poplar Street Bridge, though no cars were reported stranded here.

Between 4 and 5 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Highway 54 in various places between Vandalia and Mexico.
Between 3 and 5 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time onto already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Route J near the Marion/Shelby county line.
Between 3 and 5 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads in the Centralia area were flooded.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees and power lines in Lewistown.  Thunderstorm winds were estimated around 60 mph two miles east of Monticello.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees, numerous tree limbs and power lines throughout town.
Thunderstorm winds blew over several trees, numerous tree limbs and power lines in Mound Station.  Also, a grain silo was blown over.
Thunderstorm winds caused the partial collapse of an old abandoned building on the south side of Liberty.  Also, numerous tree limbs were blown down.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous trees 11 miles west of Barry.  In Barry, numerous large tree limbs and power lines were blown down.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous tree limbs and flattened some corn in the area.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees in Louisiana.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous trees in Elsberry, Winfield and Troy.  Also, a large tree was blown down onto Highway KK near the intersection with Tuckaho Lane.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a 10 inch diameter tree onto Wanda Road near the intersection with Illinois Route 143.
Several windows were blown out on a local supermarket.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees in Hallsville.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs near the intersection of Highway 19 and Brinkman Road.

Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous trees in Fulton.  Also, the winds blew down a large tree onto Interstate 70 blocking the far right lane of the westbound side of the highway.  This occurred near mile marker 156.
Thunderstorm winds caused minor structural damage, including doors blown in, to several buildings in Millersburg.  Also, several trees, numerous tree limbs and power lines were blown down.
Between 2 and 3 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads in Palmyra had over a foot of water on them.
Between 1 and 2 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads in Quincy had a foot of water over them at times.

Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Several roads in Troy had over a foot of water on them.  A few vehicles tried to drive through the flood waters and stalled out.

Between 2 and 4 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  U.S. Highway 54 had water flowing over it about 2 miles south of Laddonia.  Also, Highway T had water flowing over it west of Highway E, just north of Thompson.
Between 2 and 3 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Several roads in the Hallsville area were flooded.
Between 2 and 3 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Several roads in the Auxvasse area were flooded for a time.

Downburst winds caused a wide swath of damage from just northwest of Lindbergh to southwest of Lindbergh.  Several commercial buildings along the south outer road of Interstate 70 sustained minor to moderate roof damage.  Also, numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down along the path.
A semi was blown off of Highway 6 just southwest of Edina.  No injuries were reported.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a couple of power lines in town.
Numerous large tree limbs were blown down.  Also, some metal flashing from the roof of a business was blown off two miles south of Hannibal.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a tree onto power lines with both landing onto U.S. Highway 24 near Missouri Street in Camp Point.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a couple of trees onto Highway B, west of Montgomery City, blocking the road for a time.
Between 2 and 4 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Several roads were flooded including Highway 15 both north and south of Edina.

The tornado initially touched down a quarter of a mile north of Stephens on County Road 269.  As it travelled to the south through Stephens, two homes and three mobile homes sustained roof and window damage.  At the same time, hail up to ping pong size fell causing additional roof damage.  Three vehicles were damaged by fallen trees and the large hail.  A medium sized camper was tossed by the tornado and landed a quarter of a mile north of Stephens.  The tornado continued travelling south along County Road 269 and damaged three additional mobile homes and three machine sheds.  Sheet metal roofing from the machine sheds was partially uplifted and a number of windows were broken by the hail.  A large barn was totally destroyed by the tornado with the debris field extending over 150 yards to the southeast.  The tornado dissipated approximately half a mile north of Interstate 70.
Hail up to ping pong size fell in Stephens and areas just to the south of town.  Several vehicles sustained minor hail damage and a couple of windows on 3 machine sheds were knocked out by the hail.
Thunderstorm winds destroyed a billboard sign on MO 21/MO 34 north of Van Buren. The frame is still intact.
Photos on Facebook show a healthy tree uprooted by thunderstorm winds in a neighborhood near the Cole County Fairgrounds.
Thunderstorm winds downed multiple trees just east of Millersburg.

Thunderstorm winds snapped off the uprights and crossbar of the southern football goalpost at Southern Boone High School. The same thunderstorm downed several large trees and large tree limbs throughout the town of Ashland, including one tree blocking the roadway at Old Highway 63 and South and East Bullard Road. A member of the public estimated 60 mph winds with the thunderstorm.

Thunderstorm winds blew off part of the roof of North Callaway Middle School. The missing portions caused rainwater to damage the floors of some classrooms and the gym. The gym floor needed full replacement.

Rainfall of 7 - 10 inches fell across North Central Missouri causing flooding at Mark Twain Lake and along the Salt River. This represented the first flooding of the Salt River since the completion of Clarence Cannon Dam which created Mark Twain Lake in 1984.  The crest at New London represented the 8th highest crest of record, resulting in the flooding of numerous farm houses and state roads. Thirty families had to be evacuated from their homes due to the flooding. At least 30 roads had to be closed. Agricultural losses were estimated at $10 million. Initial public assistance damage estimates were put at $200,000.

Rainfall of 7 - 10 inches in North Central Missouri caused flooding along the Salt River below Mark Twain Lake. This represented the first flooding of the Salt River since the completion of Clarence Cannon Dam which created Mark Twain Lake in 1984. The flooding was limited to agricultural and conservation lowlands along the river. Several roads were flooded and had to be closed, including Highway 79.

Numerous trees and tree limbs were blown down in Pocahontas and Greenville.  Also, the winds caused a semi to jackknife on Interstate 70 between Pocahontas and Highland.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines and tree limbs.  Also, a large tree was blown down onto the roof of a nearby house.
