Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous tree limbs from Woburn to just south of Van Burensburg in extreme northeastern Bond county.
Several power lines were blown down north of Mulberry Grove.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous tree limbs in town.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous tree limbs from Germantown to Bartelso.  A few of the tree limbs fell onto cars causing minor damage.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs across town.  A few of the limbs fell onto Illinois Route 3.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted three large trees.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous trees and a power pole in Clarence.  A transformer on the power pole started a small fire after it fell.

Two to five inches of rain fell in St. Francois county in about 24 hours ending on March 5th. This rain caused Flat Creek to rise above its banks as far east as Garrett St and as far west as Camilla St. A few evacuations were required as water approached homes in these areas. Water receded by 4am.

The Boone County emergency manager reported thunderstorm wind damage in Columbia and to its south. Three trees were reportedly downed across roadways, one being 10 inches in diameter. An electric pole was also downed on a roadway northeast of Columbia.
A Bradford Farm Missouri Mesonet weather station measured wind gust.

Thunderstorm winds downed numerous tree limbs and power lines in Salem. At least one large tree was uprooted. Falling branches or a downed tree damaged at least one home. A farm outbuilding was destroyed.
Heavy rain caused Germania Road (listed as St. Francois Road on Google Maps) to flood along the Washington - St. Francois county line.
Heavy rain caused flooding on several streets of Bonne Terre.
Thunderstorm winds caused a barn to lose several sections of its roof. There was no other damage in the vicinity.

Thunderstorm winds caused damage to multiple structures in St. Charles County. A roof was removed from an older, open-side car/boat shed along Wilson Road in St. Charles. A barn in northwest St. Charles County sustained significant damage. Winds also broke 3 power poles.
Thunderstorm winds removed the roofing of an outbuilding at an animal rescue.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree. The tree fell onto a home in Leadwood.
Thunderstorm winds downed several large tree limbs and snapped several small trees.
Thunderstorm winds caused tree damage of an unknown extent in Ste. Genevieve County.

A brief tornado was confirmed both with radar data and detailed photographs of damage. This tornado cause significant roof damage to a local restaurant, along with other miscellaneous to a local hotel and residence.

A brief tornado moved through the communities of Moro and Midway, IL early in the morning of March 11, 2026. This tornado produced wind damage indicative of maximum wind speeds of approximately 110 miles per hour. Damage to trees, homes, and grain bins was observed. One injury was also reported.
A brief tornado touched down just west of I-55 in Madison County where it caused power poles to lean askew. The tornado then headed northeast where it caused minor roof damage to a home.
The tornado continued into Macoupin County from Madison County where it uprooted trees along Double Arch Road before dissipating.

A brief tornado touched down near Griebel Acres Road where it snapped tree trunks. The tornado travelled northeast where it completed destroyed a sheet metal outbuilding and caused major roof damage to a large farm outbuilding. It caused damage to an additional barn and home before dissipating near Dintelmann Road.
A 67 mph wind gust was reported at Alton Regional Airport.
Thunderstorm winds caused significant damage to a solar farm and shipping crates and left 2000 households without power.
Thunderstorm winds damaged an old barn, a car, and a sheet metal roof from an outbuilding.
Thunderstorm winds caused snapped softwood trees and a large hardwood tree. A power pole was also snapped, and a machine shed incurred significant damage.
Thunderstorm winds downed 4 inch diameter limbs from a healthy tree.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree which blocked Baldwin Road near New Athens. They also downed power lines and damaged a home to an unknown degree.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree limb which damaged a mobile home. They also broke 2 power poles near the intersection of Route 154 and Plum Creek Road.
Thunderstorm winds knocked a tree down onto County Highway 6 east of Venedy.
A 66 mph wind gust was measured at Salem Leckrone Airport.
Thunderstorm winds collapsed an outbuilding at Buckhorn General Baptist Church, downed a tree over a road near Buckhorn, then blew a roof from a mobile home in Marquand.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree on East Cherry Street. Live powerlines were also downed on the same street.

Thunderstorm winds downed multiple trees in Franklin County. One fell onto East Vine Street near the Sullivan Country Club, and another fell onto a home in Sullivan. The other two trees fell in Washington and Union, but were not reported to have hit anything.
A row of powerlines was reportedly bent over by high winds near Park Hills. 10 minutes later, a member of the public reported an estimated wind gust of 60 mph 1 mile north of Farmington.

Thunderstorm winds blew open a strong steel door in Des Peres before splitting a Bradford Pear tree into 2 near Webster Groves. Winds then blew down tree limbs up to 8 inches in diameter along Green Park Industrial Drive 1 mile southeast of Lakeshire.
Thunderstorm winds caused debris from trees to cover the roadway of Highway D just north of Highway O.

A tornado touched down just west of the Staunton Reservoir where it damaged trees along Bono Road. The tornado then travelled northeast, causing minor damage to the roofs of a few structures before directly hitting Mount Olive. In Mount Olive, the tornado damaged mostly trees, but the roof of a business was impacted as well. The tornado weakened as it exited town and approached Montgomery County.

The tornado moved into Montgomery County from Macoupin County, where it caused minor damage to a home on W County Line Road. The tornado then took on a near due northerly track as it occluded and caused minor tree damage before it dissipated completely just north of Saint Johns Ave.
A tornado touched down just east of Ames where it collapsed a large farm outbuilding before exiting into Randolph County. The doors of the structure were open at the time of the event.

The tornado entered Randolph County where it damaged mostly trees along its northeastern path. On Ritchfield Road southeast of Red Bud, the tornado did damage the roofs of a few farm outbuildings. The most substantial damage happened on South Prairie Road north of Prairie where the tornado ripped off a substantial portion of a church's roof. It dissipated shortly after just north of Grigg.

A tornado touched down near Niemanville Trail and trekked northeast, producing mostly tree damage in its path. At its strongest the tornado was able to produce minor damage to farm outbuildings and break wooden power poles. The tornado dissipated just east of East 8th Road.

New Athens took a direct hit from this tornado. It touched down near Julia Street where it busted the windows of a local shop and damaged the roof of a warehouse building. The tornado pathed east-northeast through town, damaging, to varying extent, multiple roofs on Lela Drive. The tornado then weakened, causing less and weaker damage before dissipating just east of the Canadian National Railway.

A brief tornado touched down on the Hillsboro Country Club where it produced minor damage to a home. The tornado then travelled northeast where it damaged trees, an outbuilding, and electrical poles. The tornado dissipated just north of White Ave west of Irving.

A tornado touched down near Irving Road and North 17th Ave where it blew over a farm auger and lofted debris nearly a half mile to the southwest. The tornado then hit Witt directly where it lofted a carport and damaged multiple roofs and trees in town. The tornado tracked along State Route 16 into Coalton where it nearly completely removed the roof of a mobile home. From there, it turned nearly due north and entered the northwest portion of Nokomis. Although most of the damage done was to trees, the tornado did blow over an outdoor football scoreboard and ripped off portions of the local high school's roof.

A tornado touched down on the east side of Nokomis where it produced tree damage before exiting town to the northeast. The tornado tracked along State Route 16 past Ohlman, collapsing older farm outbuildings and lofting the debris well to the northeast. The tornado then continued into Christian County (ILX).

A very brief tornado touched down near Brink Road north of Shattuc. Along its path, the tornado damaged trees, a farm outbuilding, and a grain bin. Debris from both structures was lofted well beyond their original location.
A member of the public reported an estimated wind gust of 60 mph in Eldred.
Thunderstorm winds downed trees and power lines in Brighton at North Main Street and Oak Street.
Quarter sized hail was reported in Wood River by Madison County SKYWARN.
Thunderstorm winds downed power lines near Dorsey.
A TV meteorologist noted several gusts over 60 mph in his station's Storm Runner vehicle.
National Weather Service survey concluded that snapped wooden power poles along Reservoir Road were the result of approximately 100 mph wind gusts.
Thunderstorm winds downed power poles and live powerlines along Route 155 west of Ruma. Winds also snapped several large power poles on IL-3 south of Ruma.
A trained spotter estimated 60 mph winds in New Athens a few minutes after a tornado with max wind gusts of 90 mph struck the town.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree south of Coffeen. This tree blocked a road.
A report from social media showed a destroyed carport caused by thunderstorm winds.
A broadcast meteorologist reported wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph in Okawville.
Thunderstorm winds snapped a power pole in Central City and downed a large tree over Boat Dock Road. Boat Dock Road was subsequently closed near North Oak Road by IDOT.

A brief tornado touched down east of County Road 2150 just north of Highway 61 in Adams County. The tornado tracked parallel to Highway 61 where it caused significant damage to several small farm outbuildings and to one home. As it moved east, it damaged mostly trees. The tornado dissipated just after crossing Bigneck Creek.
Thunderstorm winds caused a large tree limb to fall onto a house.
Report of lots of small hail with a few ping pong sized stones.
An emergency manager estimated hail size between golf balls and tennis balls. Photo provided was representative of tennis ball sized hail.
A brief tornado touched down along High Point Road and travelled northeast. The tornado caused tree damage before crossing the Missouri River into Boone County.
The tornado entered Boone County where it caused tree damage near and in Hartsburg. It then dissipated.

A brief tornado touched down southwest of Fulton where it caused mostly tree damage on its northeastward path. The tornado did partially uplift the roof of the Fulton-Elton Hensley Memorial Airport before lifting just west of Fulton proper.
A brief tornado touched down just south of the Missouri River near Etlah. It caused minor damage to trees and possibly crops before crossing the river into Warren County.

The tornado crossed the Missouri River into Warren County south of Pinckney, and moved north-north east, dissipating along Smith Creek Road. Tree damage was observed along the path, with the worst damage consisting of uprooted trees, resulting in estimated wind speeds of approximately 90 mph.

A Tornado Debris Signature off of the KLSX radar appeared just south of the Missouri River and tracked north-northeast. Ground survey was unable to find damage directly associated with tornado, but NWS GIS Mutual Aid analysis of high resolution satellite imagery was able to find tree damage consistent with an EF-0 tornado.

A Tornado Debris Signature off of the KLSX radar continued into Warren County from Franklin County. Ground survey was unable to find damage directly associated with tornado, but NWS GIS Mutual Aid analysis of high resolution satellite imagery was able to find tree damage consistent with an EF-0 tornado.

A brief tornado touched down along Linns Mill Road near Coon Creek, southwest of Troy, and moved northeast. The tornado crossed Forest Acres Lane and Crooked Creek before lifting along Sugar Grove Road. Along it's path it produced tree damage, snapping some tree trunks and uprooting other trees. This damage suggests a maximum wind speed of approximately 95 mph.

Thunderstorm winds caused damage to power poles across the far western portion of the county, extending from New Melle north into Wentzville and Flint Hill. Along its path, there were multiple reports of snapped trees/branches, snapped power poles, downed lines, one downed transformer, and one home with shingles missing from its roof near New Melle. This thunderstorm went on to produce additional wind damage in Lincoln County.
Thunderstorm winds knocked a tree onto a powerline.
Report from social media. Largest stone around 1 inch in diameter.

Thunderstorm winds snapped power poles and numerous tree limbs from just north of Flint Hill northeast to Winfield. Near Old Monroe a farm outbuilding was collapsed, the siding peeled from a home, and the roof removed from a mobile home.
Thunderstorm winds snapped two 6 inch diameter limbs from trees just south of Troy.

Thunderstorm winds caused damage from near the Woodland Airstrip northeast into Winfield. Near the beginning, winds peeled back the roof of an old farm outbuilding and caused a small farm outbuilding to collapse upon itself. Winds blew down tree branches, power lines, and power poles along its path. Between Moscow Mills and Troy, a billboard was blown over onto a mobile home which sustained damage.
Thunderstorm winds damaged the siding and roof of a single family home. A large tree was also split in half, but the center of the tree was rotted and half of the tree was leafless.
Thunderstorm winds downed one large tree in Lewistown.

Thunderstorm winds downed several trees in a forest on Heckemeyer Road. Additional tree damage was reported on Dawson Road. The storm continued northeast where it downed several large trees near Falcon Lane and Route M in Wardsville.
Thunderstorm winds downed tree branches which littered a road.

Strong straight-line winds accompanied a brief tornado that approached Fulton from the southwest. These downed and damaged numerous trees between CR-325 and northwest Fulton. Winds ripped off the front part of a trailer near Carrington. In Fulton, the stoplights at Bluff and Industrial Ave were damaged, as was the Sonic restaurant sign on North Bluff Street. Numerous street lights sustained damage throughout town, and 2 utility poles were downed. The old KFAL radio tower was knocked down. Finally, large and healthy trees were uprooted on the Warson Woods University campus. Here, metal bleachers were blown over and debris was found in trees.

Thunderstorm winds downed a 15 inch diameter tree near Lyon. They then downed a tree 6 to 10 inches in diameter southeast of New Haven. A tornado developed just east of this damage at about the same time.

Thunderstorm winds produced a swath of tree and structural damage extending from Pleasant Hill northeast through Pittsfield, Griggsville, and beyond. Other municipalities within that line include Martinsburg and Chambersburg. In Pleasant Hill, winds peeled portions of the roof from the local high school, threw the roof of an outbuilding a block away, and caused major tree damage. In Pittsfield, a power pole was snapped off on the 200 block of North Illinois Street. Several trees were downed here. Griggsville incurred more structural damage, with a home sustained roof damage, part of a metal roof torn from an outbuilding, power poles snapped, and a large carport structure collapsed onto a combine to the northeast of town.
Thunderstorm winds heavily damaged a machine shed in the bottoms of the Illinois River southeast of Versailles. Winds also knocked a tree onto a mobile home in Versailles around the same time.
A 62 mph gust was recorded at Quincy Regional Airport.

A brief EF-1 tornado touched down in southwestern Monroe County near Route M and Highway 151. The primary damage caused by this tornado was a farm just south of Highway 151. Numerous large tree limbs were broken on the property with one tree limb pointed to the west. One farm building was collapsed on the western side of the barn. The eastern facing part of the building which was attached to the cement slab was still standing, while the western facing part of the building had completely collapsed. Due to this, we estimated slightly below the expected wind speed which also matched the surrounding tree damage.
A video from Alton showed the vortex of a waterspout tornado dissipating as it moved onshore of the Lincoln Shields Recreation Area.
Photo of multiple large hail stones. Largest is measured at 2 inches.
Picture of hailstone received on X from near Kingshighway and Martin Luther King Drive.
Photo of hailstone received on X.
Estimated ping pong sized hail with photo and US quarter.

NWS storm survey found that just south of a tornado, rear inflow jet winds of up to 95 mph caused straight line wind damage in a swath extending from the Monroe/Randolph/Audrain county line northeast just beyond Monroe 931. Along this path, the survey team found multiple trees uprooted as well as structural damage. A home had shingles lost to the wind. A farm outbuilding was overturned, another completely collapsed, and a third had its doors collapsed.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted multiple trees in Creve Coeur.
A trained spotter measured 1 inch hailstones at Midland Ave at I-170.
Thunderstorm winds downed power lines on Ethlyn Road.
A picture of a hailstone compared with a quarter was received.
A trained spotter reported quarter sized hail in Copper Hill.
A HAM radio operator reported quarter sized hail at Cooper Hill.
Stones varied from pea sized to quarter sized.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree at Champion City Road and Red Oak Road.
A report of 2+ inch hail fell near Bourbon Elementary School.
Quarter sized hail fell near Mexico Road at Salt Lick.
Numerous hailstones measuring 2 inches to 4 inches.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted a large tree in Union and another northwest of Union. The storm downed several other trees along its path between Union and Wildwood.

Thunderstorm winds caused a swath of tree damage extending from Wildwood northeastward through Spanish Lake. The same storm produced damage in Franklin County, so it's likely there was damage southwest of Ellisville as well. Large trees were downed, with one landing on a home near Clarkson Valley and others falling onto cars in Saint Ann. Thunderstorm winds also removed shingles from a home near Saint John and collapsed 4 buildings in Florissant.
Thunderstorm winds downed one power line on McCausland and one small tree at IKEA.
Estimated wind gust on I-55 near Arnold.
Thunderstorm winds blew down multiple trees in Ellington.
A trained spotter in Farmington estimated a 60 mph wind gust.

A very brief tornado touched down IL just east of Illinois Route 4 and just north of Lower Marine Road where it collapsed the overhead doors of a metal building and caused minor roof damage to a double wide manufactured home. The tornado lifted shortly after.

A tornado touched down just east of Shiloh on Route 4 and just north of I-64 where it broke multiple power poles before continuing east-northeast. Along its path it damaged mostly trees, but did collapse the walls of one farm outbuilding and remove several shingles from one home. The tornado then continued into Clinton County.

The tornado that formed in St. Clair county moved into Clinton county where it passed just southeast of Trenton and Sugar Creek. Along Route 160, the tornado destroyed power poles, damaged the roof of one home, and removed about half of the roof of one farm outbuilding. Along Highline Road, the tornado peeled part of the roof from a barn before dissipating.

A tornado developed just southwest of Germantown where it damaged part of the roof of an outbuilding. In Germantown, the tornado produced mostly tree damage. However, it did destroy the roof of one manufactured home and it completely destroyed another. From there, it damaged mostly trees until it reached just south of Beckemeyer. Here, the tornado destroyed one outbuilding and flipped another. The tornado produced more tree damage before dissipating just south of Carlyle.
Thunderstorm winds blew a semi-truck onto the median of I-55.
Heavy rain washed out a culvert and a portion of West County Road was washed out.
Heavy rain washed out a culvert and damaged Green Acres Road near Elsah.
Heavy rain flooded roads along East 23rd Road outside of Nokomis.
Thunderstorm winds damaged a shed near Marine.
A trained spotter reported about 6 inches of standing water on Prairie Street.
Thunderstorm winds downed a large portion of a tree onto a home in Hamel. A member of the public estimated 70 mph wind gusts were occurring a few minutes later.

Thunderstorm winds blew a tree onto a home 2 miles southeast of Belleville. Three individuals sustained injuries. Near Swansea and at Scott Air Force Base, winds downed large tree limbs. A report of an estimated 55 mph wind gust was reported in Swansea, but winds were likely stronger based on the damage.
Thunderstorm winds downed power lines all over Centralia. Power poles and trees sustained damage as well.
A large tree was blown onto the North River bridge on Highway 15 just south of Bethel.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines northwest of Granville.

A line of severe thunderstorms moved southeast through Monroe county.  In Holliday, a trained spotter measured an 80 mph wind gust and had sustained winds of 50 to 60 mph for approximately 10 minutes.  Numerous large tree limbs were blown down in the area.  Four miles north of Paris, some siding was blown off of a home and a large tree was uprooted.  A little further to the south of this location several power lines were blown down as well as another large tree.
Fifteen to twenty power poles were blown down along the Shelby/Monroe county line.  Also, several trees were blown down along Highway 15 on the north side of Shelbina.
Numerous large tree limbs were blown down.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees and tree limbs, as well as several power lines.

A line of severe thunderstorms moved southeast through Audrain county.  Several trees were blown down at the intersection of Highway 22 and Highway 151.  Also, in Laddonia numerous tree limbs were blown down and some metal was blown off of a building.
Numerous trees were blown down as well as numerous large tree limbs. Also, several power lines were blown down.

A line of strong to severe thunderstorms moved through the Columbia, Missouri area around 711 pm.  There was a tent revival occurring north of the city and when the storms hit, the high winds caused the tent to collapse.  Twenty people were injured.  Eighteen had minor injuries and two had moderate injuries.  Four were transported to the nearest hospital.  There was also some tree damage in the area and debris from the trees caused minor damage to cars that were parked in the area.  Winds were measured around 30 mph on the University of Missouri campus and a 55 mph wind gust was measured at Columbia Municipal Airport which is approximately 10 miles south southeast of Columbia.
Thunderstorm winds bldw down several power lines in Wentzville.  Also, numerous large tree limbs were blown down in St. Peters.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs onto Highway E.
A large tree was blown over onto Barnicle Chapel Road west southwest of Steelville.
A large tree was blown down onto Route K west of New Hartford.
Thunderstorm winds blew a roof covering off the top of Winfield Elementary School, but the winds did not cause any damage to the roof or the rest of the building.

A line of severe storms moved across Jersey county blowing down numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines.  In Jerseyville, a microburst caused extensive damage to two businesses.  One business sustained roof and window damage and the other just had its windows blown out.  Several of the large trees that fell, fell onto unoccupied vehicles causing severe damage.  One tree fell onto a patio roof collapsing it.  Several witnesses from Jerseyville indicated that winds of 60 mph and greater occurred for approximately 3 to 5 minutes with the strongest gusts occurring near the early stages of heavy rainfall.

The line of severe storms moved across southern portions of Macoupin county.  A microburst occurred just south of Shipman.  Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down.  Also, a barn door was blown off two miles south of Shipman.

The line of severe storms moved across southern portions of Macoupin county.  A microburst occurred just south of Bunker Hill.  Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down.  Also, a mobile home 4 miles east of Brighton was damaged by two fallen trees and another home one and a half miles south of Bunker Hill was damaged by a fallen tree.  Three of four roofs were torn off of the relatively new dugouts at the Bunker Hill High School baseball fields.  Small outbuildings and barns sustained minor damage in the area due to the microburst winds.

A line of severe storms moved through Montgomery county.  Numerous large trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down in the Litchfield and Hillsboro areas.  One large tree landed on an unoccupied pickup truck causing extensive damage in Litchfield.  A ham radio tower was blown down in Hillsboro.

The line of severe storms moved across Montgomery county.  A microburst occurred in the vicinity of Walshville and Panama.  Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down in the area.  A very large tree fell on top of a two story home east of Walshville causing extensive damage.  Also, several power poles were snapped and corn flattened just northeast of Panama.
In Gillespie, a large tree fell onto a house causing moderate damage.  Also, numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down between Gillespie and Mount Olive.
Very heavy rain fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Highway E east of Spencerburg was closed due to water flowing over the road.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees, tree limbs and power lines.
Very heavy rain fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Illinois Route 111 was closed about 4 miles south of Piasa due to flooding.
Very heavy rain fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Illinois Route 111 was closed about 4 miles south of Piasa due to flooding.

The remnants of Hurricane Ike moved through the midwest dumping  between 3 and 6 inches of rain in just under 6 hours on already saturated soils.  This caused widespread flash flooding over St. Louis County.  One of the hardest hit areas was University City.  Two people drowned in University City when trying to move their vehicles away from the rising flood waters.  Another person was killed when a large tree limb that was struck by lightning fell on her in Ladue.  Other areas affected by the flash flooding were Hazelwood, Ferguson, Brentwood, Maplewood, Rock Hill, Webster Groves, and Florissant.  Over 600 homes, apartments and business were affected by the flooding.  Numerous water rescues had to be performed when people drove their vehicles into flooded roadways and became stuck in the flood waters.

Flash flooding occurred when very heavy rainfall from the remnants of Hurricane Ike fell onto already saturated soils.  Between 3 and 5 inches of rain fell in just under 6 hours.  Numerous roads were flooded throughout the county.  Some towns affected by the flooding were Alton, Fosterburg, Troy, Edwardsville and Granite City.  East Lake Drive near Gerber Road was washed out in Edwardsville.  In East Alton, a home was flooded on Tomilson Avenue.  Near Hamel, 12 girl scouts and 4 adults leaders had to be rescued from a girl scout camp when flood waters washed out a bridge to the campground.  Also, 2 people had to be rescued from their mobile home due to Wood River Creek flooding the surrounding area northeast of Alton.  Numerous other water rescues occurred due to people driving into flooded roadways.

Two and a half to three and a half inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils, causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded and one water rescue was performed on Rangeline Road at David Allen Road.
Two and a half to three and a half inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Highway JJ southeast of Mexico.
Two and a half to three and a half inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Several roads were flooded in around the Fulton area.
An additional 3 to 6 inches of rain from the remnants of Hurricane Ike fell onto very saturated soils causing flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded.

Up to two inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Route V at Tucker School Road and Thomas Hill Road.  In McBaine, two homes and one business were flooded due to several creeks in the area coming out of their banks.

An additional two to three inches of rain, from the remnants of Hurricane Ike, fell onto already saturated soils causing flooding.  Numerous roads remained flooded and numerous creeks were well out of their banks due to the heavy rainfall.  One woman drowned in flood waters on the east side of Columbia.  Her and a friend had stopped to help someone who had been swept off Clark Lane into Hominy Creek.  Against the advise of the friend, the woman attempted to help rescue the man and she was swept away.
Up to two inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Route 54 Business two miles south of Mexico.

An additional two to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time as the remnants of Hurricane Ike moved through the region.  Numerous roads remained flooded including Highway 15 north of Mexico.

Up to two inches fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Route D east of Highway 15 and Route A between Routes DD and J.
An additional two to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time as the remnants of Hurricane Ike moved through the region.  Numerous roads remained flooded.

Between two and three inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils causing flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Route C north of Highway 11, Highway 15 just north of Greensburg, and Highway 15 north of Edina.  Also, water from Bridge Creek was flowing onto Highway V north of Knox City.

Between 2 and 3 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils causing flooding.  This includes rainfall from the remnants of Hurricane Ike.  Numerous roads were flooded.  Also, a creek in the New London area was overtopping the culvert with fast flowing water over the roadway.
Up to four inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils causing flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded and several of them were washed out including Highway D near the Moniteau Creek Bridge.
Up to 6 inches of rain fell in short amount of time as the remnants of Hurricane Ike moved through the region causing flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded countywide.
Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time as the remnants of Hurricane Ike moved through the region causing flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded countywide.

Up to 5 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time as the remnants of Hurricane Ike moved through the region causing flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded countywide and numerous creeks were well out of their banks due to the heavy rain.

Four to five inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils causing flooding.  Some of the rainfall was from the remnants of Hurricane Ike.  Numerous secondary roads were flooded.  The heavy rains loosened up soils in the area causing several trees to fall.  A large mudslide occurred on Ely Street in Hannibal.  Up to ten dump trucks full of mud had to be hauled away from the slide.  No structures were affected by the mudslide.

Between 4 and 5 inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils as the remnants of Hurricane Ike moved through the region causing flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Highway 79 north of Louisiana.

Up to 6 inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils as the remnants of Hurricane Ike moved through the region causing flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded countywide with numerous creeks out of their banks as well.  At least two roads were washed out.  In Washington, a large section of a used car lot was washed out by a nearby creek.  One car was destroyed after falling into the hole.
Winds associated with the remnants of Hurricane Ike blew over several trees, tree limbs and power lines.

Between 3 and 5 inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils as the remnants of Hurricane Ike moved through the region causing flash flooding.  In Silex, the Cuivre River flash flooded the whole town.  Seventy-five homes and 6 businesses reported any where from minor to major flood damage.  Fortunately no injuries or deaths were reported.  Numrous roads throughout the county were flooded.

Between 3 and 6 inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils as the remnants of Hurricane Ike moved through the region causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded countywide including Highway N east of Highway K due to Dardenne Creek overflowing its banks.  Also, water was flowing over Central School Road and McClay Road due to creeks out of their banks.
A large tree was blown over onto a shed 4 miles north of Defiance by winds associated with the remnants of Hurricane Ike.

Between 4 and 5 inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils as the remnants of Hurricane Ike moved through the region causing flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded, especially over northern portions of the county.
Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down by winds associated with the remnants of Hurricane Ike.

Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down by winds from the remnants of Hurricane Ike across Crawford county.  Some of the trees and limbs fell across roadways blocking them for a time.

Three to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on already saturated soils due to the remnants of Hurricane Ike.  Several creeks in the Steelville area, including Yadkin Creek, were out of their banks for a time and several roads in the area were flooded.
Several trees were blown over as well as numerous tree limbs and power lines throughout the county due to winds from the remnants of Hurricane Ike.

Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down due to winds from the remnants of Hurricane Ike.  In Fredericktown, a mobile classroom at the district preschool sustained minor porch roof damage.  Also, a van in Fredericktown sustained minor damage when a large tree limb fell onto it.
Numerous tree, tree limbs and power lines were blown down throughout the county due to the remnants of Hurricane Ike.  In Ironton, a tree was blown over onto an unoccupied car, crushing it.
Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down throughout the county due to the remnants of Hurricane Ike.  Several trees fell across Highway 21 north of Ellington blocking it for a time.

Three to five inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils causing flooding due to the remnants of Hurricane Ike.  Numerous roads were flooded countywide, especially in the Hull, Nebo, Pleasant Hill, Perry and Pittsfield areas.
Strong winds associated with the remnants of Hurricane Ike blew over a large hay barn and overturned an empty hog trailer just north of Perry.

Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down in Germantown, Breese and Carlyle due to the remnants of Hurricane Ike.  One tree landed on a garage in Breese causing moderate damage.  Also, there was lots of corn crop damage countywide.
Numerous tree limbs and power lines were blown down in Nokomis due to the remnants of Hurricane Ike.

Up to 6 inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils causing flooding.  The rain was from the remnants of Hurricane Ike.  Numerous roads were flooded countywide, especially in the Nokomis, Hillsboro, Litchfield, Witt and Raymond areas.  In Raymond, one person drove into the flood waters at the railroad underpass on Route 127 just south of Route 48 and got stuck.  He managed to get out of his truck and get to dry land on his own.

Up to 4 inches of rain from the remnants of Hurricane Ike fell onto already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  In East St. Louis, several dozen homes were flooded.  Also, several people had to be evacuated from their homes and apartments due to the flooding.  The exit ramps on I-255 and I-64 were flooded for a time.
Strong winds associated with the remnants of Hurricane Ike blew down a large tree and a few power lines in Nashville.

Strong winds associated with the remnants of Hurricane Ike blew down several trees and power lines in Waterloo.  Elsewhere, HH Road near Deer Hill Road and Route 156 between old and new Valmeyer had trees down across the roadways.
Up to three inches of rain from the remnants of Hurricane Ike fell onto already saturated soils causing flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded.
Up to 3 inches of rain from the remnants of Hurricane Ike fell onto already saturated soils causing flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded countywide.

Strong winds associated with the remnants of Hurricane Ike blew down numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines countywide.  On Route 140 near Smithboro, a power line and tree limbs were covering the roadway.
Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down countywide due to the remnants of Hurricane Ike.

Strong winds associated with the remnants of Hurricane Ike blew over numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines throughout the county.  Two miles southeast of Pontoon Beach, a tree was blown over onto Illinois Route 162, west of I-255.  Some corn crops were blown over in the Highland area.
Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down countywide due to the remnants of Hurricane Ike.

Up to 5 inches of rain from the remnants of Hurricane Ike fell onto already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded in the Carlinville, Gillespie, Virden and Mount Olive areas.  Route 4 was closed in Carlinville due to the flooding.  Three water rescues had to be performed in just an hour as 3 people drove into flooded roadways and became stranded.  One driver got out of his car and was swept downstream about a quarter of a mile before grabbing onto a tree till he was rescued.  Numerous culverts were washed out countywide.  In Gillespie, rain soaked soil collapsed the basement wall and foundation of a home on South Macoupin Street.
A metal storage shed was torn from its anchors and blown over in Shelbina.
Thunderstorm winds blew a metal patio roof off of a house and flung it over the house into the front yard.  There was also some minor soffit and shingle damage.
Several trees blown down in Canton.
Thunderstorm winds blew the roof off of the concession stand at the Pike County Fairgrounds, as well as a portion of the roof of a barn.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs and a few power lines in Barry.
Several large trees were blown down blocking the intersection of Illinois Routes 104 and 107.
Thunderstorm winds blew some shingles off the roof of a motel in New Florence.
Thunderstorm winds blew some shingles off of three buildings in town.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs north of Beaufort.
Thunderstorm winds blew a section of tin roof off of the public works building on Highway PP on the southeast side of town.  The building sustained some water damage after the roof was blown off.
Thunderstorm winds blew half the roof off of a house in Bourbon.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs.  One tree limb fell onto a truck causing minor damage.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees and power lines in town.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs.

Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs with a few falling onto homes causing minor roof damage.  Part of the roof of a mobile home was blown off. Also, an old barn was destroyed and 2 grain bins were damaged.

A tornado touched down about 2 and a half miles west of Laddonia.  A grain silo was damaged at this location. The tornado rapidly skipped northeast and damaged a large machine shed about three quarters of a mile north of Laddonia. Also, it destroyed an airplane hanger on a nearby farm and blew down numerous trees.

A tornado touched down about 4 miles north of Center near Highway H.  Two machine sheds and large tree limbs were damaged by the tornado.  The tornado rapidly moved northeast and touched down a second time southeast of the intersection of Homestead and Kingsville Lanes.  Three machine sheds were damaged at this location. Further northeast the tornado crossed Highway A west of New London, damaging several large trees before lifting and dissipating.

A tornado touched down on State Highway HH west of U.S. 61 damaging some trees in the area.  The tornado travelled to the east and damaged two small apartment complexes in addition to signs and trees along U.S. 61. It continued to the east, crossing New London Gravel Road causing additional tree damage before lifting and dissipating.

A tornado touched down 3 miles east of Davis in an open field west of a farmstead and destroyed a 2 story barn.  Six by six supports from the barn where driven into the ground near the farm house.  The home was about 60 yards to the northeast of the barn and was heavily damaged by the tornado.  As the tornado travelled to the east, a couple of new homes sustained minor roof damage on Penrod Road.  It continued to the east northeast and damaged three additional machine sheds as well as numerous trees before lifting and dissipating.

A tornado touched down in an open field west of Illinois Route 104.  It damaged several trees in this location.  The tornado travelled to the east northeast.  It damaged the roof of one home just east of Illinois Route 104.  It then destroyed a large barn just south of County Road 1050N.  The debris field extended for a mile to the north northeast of the barn.

A tornado touched down just west of County Road 2250th Street, north of N1025th Avenue. It damaged a machine shed and a mobile home in this location.  It travelled to the northeast and caused some additional tree damage before lifting and dissipating.

Thunderstorm winds caused widespread damage in Vandalia.  Several windows were blown out around town. A large sign for a store was blown over and part of its roof was blown off. Another business had minor roof damage and a home had some siding damage. A local manufacturing plant had two 12 foot by 14 foot doors damaged and a 15 foot by 20 foot section of the metal wall blown away.
Several large cedar trees were blown down on farm off of Highway H...just south of Highway BB.
An apartment building in Fairview Heights sustained major roof damage when thunderstorm winds peeled off part of the roof structure.  No one was injured by the storm.

Several inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on frozen ground in St. Charles county.  This caused flash flooding in several locations including Cottleville, New Melle, Weldon Spring, Harvester and St. Peters.  In Cottleville, Highway N was flooded just east of Highway K and Motherhead Road was closed due to a mudslide.  Highway F, just south of New Melle, was restricted to one lane for a time due to water over the roadway.  Also, water was reported over Highway D and Highway F near Weldon Springs.  In Defiance, Femme Osage Creek was out of its banks along Highway F.
Several inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on frozen ground causing flash flooding.  In Washington, numerous roads were flooded with 6 to 12 inches of water over some of the roads.

Several inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on frozen ground causing flash flooding.  In Chestefield, water was covering the roadway at the intersection of Clarkson and Baxter.  In Hazelwood, 3 to 6 inches of water was over several streets in town.  There was also some street flooding reported in Ballwin, Maplewood and Kirkwood.
Several inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on frozen ground causing flash flooding.  Just northwest of Hillsboro, some water was flowing over Highway BB.
Several inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on frozen ground causing flash flooding.  In Godfrey and Bethalto, several streets were flooded.
Several inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on frozen ground causing flash flooding. Numerous roads in Waterloo were flooded with between 4 and 5 inches of water on several of those roads.
Several inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on frozen ground causing flash flooding.  Illinois Route 16 near Shipman was closed due to 2 to 3 feet of water over the roadway.
Several inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on frozen ground causing flash flooding.  About 3 miles east of Jerseyville, Illinois Route 16 was flooded.
Several inches of rain fell in a short amount of time on frozen ground causing flash flooding.  Several streets were flooded around Carondelet Park on the city's south side.
Ice accumulations across Adams County ranged from 1/4 inch in the Quincy area to nearly 4/10 of an inch in the Northeast corner. Tree limbs were down and there were scattered power outages.
Ice accumulations across Brown County ranged from 1/4 inch to nearly 1/2 of an inch. Tree limbs were reported down in Mt. Sterling and there were scattered power outages.
Ice accumulations across Pike County ranged from 1/4 inch nearly 1/2 of an inch. Tree limbs were reported down and there were scattered power outages.
Ice accumulations across Greene County were generally around 1/4 inch Tree limbs were reported down and there were scattered power outages.
Ice accumulations across Macoupin County were generally around 1/4 inch. Tree limbs were reported down and there were scattered power outages.
Ice accumulations across Knox County ranged from 1/4 inch to just under 1/2 inch. Tree limbs were reported down and their were scattered power outages.
Ice accumulations across Lewis County ranged from 1/4 inch to just under 1/2 inch. Tree limbs were reported down and their were scattered power outages.
From 7 to 8 inches of mainly snow fell across Bond County.
From 8 to 9 inches of mainly snow fell across Clinton County.
Up to 10 inches of mainly snow fell across Fayette County. Vandalia had the highest amount with 10.2 inches.
An average of 6 inches of mainly snow fell across Macoupin County.
From 6 to almost 9 inches of mainly snow fell across Madison County. Highland reported 8.8 inches.
From 7 to almost 9 inches of mainly snow fell across Marion County. Salem reported 8.8 inches.
From 6 to almost 8 inches of mainly snow fell across Monroe County. Waterloo reported 7.5 inches.
From 6 to almost 8 inches of mainly snow fell across Montgomery County.
From 6 to almost 7 inches of mainly snow fell across Randolph County. Red Bud reported 7.2 inches.
From 7 to 8 inches of mainly snow fell across St. Clair County. Mascoutah reported 8 inches.
From 7 to 8 inches of mainly snow fell across Washington County. Nashville reported 8 inches.
An average of 7 inches of mainly snow fell across Crawford County. Steelville reported 7.0 inches.
An average of 6 to 7 inches of mainly snow fell across Franklin County. Sullivan reported 7.0 inches.
An average of 7 to 8 inches of mainly snow fell across Iron County. Arcadia reported 7.7 inches.
An average of 6 to 7 inches of mainly snow fell across Jefferson County. De Soto reported 7.3 inches.
An average of 7 inches of mainly snow fell across Madison County. Fredericktown reported 7.0 inches.
An average of 6 to 7 inches mainly snow fell across Reynolds County.
An average of 6 to 7 inches mainly snow fell across St. Francois County.
An average of 6 inches mainly snow fell across St. Louis County. University City reported 6.3 inches.
An average of 6 inches mainly snow fell across St. Louis City.
An average of 6 to 7 inches mainly snow fell across Ste. Genevieve County.
An average of 6 to 7 inches mainly snow fell across Washington County.
Several large trees were blown down just south of Wesco.
Several trees were blown down onto Highway 8 just west of Berryman.

Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree onto a house in town causing minor damage.  Also, a couple of large trees and several large tree limbs were blown down.  Two billboards and a couple of power lines were blown down and part of the roof of a business was blown off.  The roof of a church sustained minor damage due to the thunderstorm winds.
Several trees were blown down.
One person sustained minor cuts when the large hail shattered a window in their home.

A tornado touched down just southwest of Prairie.  As it travelled to the east northeast it damaged 3 homes on Richfield Road. Two of the homes sustained minor roof damage and the other had a portion of its roof removed. The tornado lifted and dissipated just northeast of Prairie.

A tornado touched down one mile south of Grigg and travelled to the northeast.  It destroyed 2 mobile homes and snapped numerous trees along its path.  The tornado then caused major damage to the second floor of the two-story Kaskaskia River Hotel before lifting and dissipating one mile west of Baldwin.  One of the mobile homes was occupied.  The man sustained minor injuries from the tornado.

A tornado touched down 2 miles east northeast of Baldwin and travelled to the northeast.  It removed the roof from a cinder block outbuilding and tossed it across Doza Creek Road.  Also, several trees and branches were snapped along its path.  It lifted and dissipated 4 miles west southwest of Tilden.

A tornado touched down 5.5 miles west southwest of Oakdale and travelled to the northeast.  A house on County Highway 29 sustained moderate damage with 4 windows blown out, a wall was buckled in, and siding and shingles were blown off.  At this location it also overturned and destroyed a camper and the back end of a machine shed was torn off.  Further down the road, a silo and two sheds were blown down.  The falling silo hit two cows, killing one of them.  The tornado then snapped off 2 large double-poled wooden high tension towers at the base.  Also, it destroyed several pole sheds with the debris scattered hundreds of yards and snapped off numerous trees.  On another farmstead, a brand new garage was destroyed and the home sustained minimal roof and siding damage before the tornado lifted and dissipated about a mile west of Oakdale.

A tornado touched down 2.5 miles west southwest of the entrance to the Washington County Conservation Area on Illinois Route 127 and travelled to the northeast.  It snapped off numerous trees and branches before lifting and dissipating four tenths of a mile north of the conservation area entrance.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree in Ellington.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines and trees in an area from Iron Mountain to Iron Mountain Lake.  One of the fallen trees landed on a carport, destroying it.

Between 2 and 3 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads had water flowing over them including Brown School Road west of Highway 763, Fox Hollow Road five miles west of Ashland, and Wilhite Road east of Evert School Road.

A tornado touched down about 3.5 miles south southwest of Beaucoup and travelled to the northeast.  It blew down several trees and snapped numerous tree limbs along its path before lifting and dissipating about 3 miles south of Beaucoup.

The tornado touched down on County Road 51, about three quarters of a mile west southwest of the intersection of Roodhouse Road and 2000E.  A large machine shed was totally destroyed at this location.  The tornado travelled northeast damaging a number of large trees between CR 51 and 2000E.  The tornado crossed 2000E and damaged a large number of trees east of 2000E.  The damage width at this location was two tenths of a mile.  Further to the northeast, the tornado damaged a church at the intersection of Roodhouse Road and County Road 2075E.  The entire church was displaced about 10 feet.  A machine shed south of the church was destroyed with debris extending to the north towards the church.  Many trees were damaged in this area.  The tornado crossed Roodhouse Road and travelled just south of a farmstead on CR 2100E.  There was minor shingle damage to the home, one machine shed was damaged.  A second farm sustained damage on CR 2600N, about a quarter of a mile west of Illinois Route 267.  At this location, one barn and three machine sheds sustained severe damage while parts of the roof and sides of the farm house were uplifted and displaced to the east.  The damage path width was a tenth of a mile at this location.  Debris from these structures were tossed over 120 yards to the east.  The tornado crossed Illinois Route 267 and travelled over an open field then crossed CR 298 where tree damage occurred.  The tornado severely damaged a large section of mature pine trees just south of CR 304 and CR 2700N in an open field before it lifted and dissipated.

The tornado touched down along the eastern shore of the Illinois River in the Hadley Landing Public Access Area.  Two cabins sustained minor roof and siding damage while a third cabin sustained severe damage.  A fourth cabin was totally destroyed.  Numerous large trees were also severed or snapped off near the base of the trunk just east of the cabin.  Debris from the destroyed cabin extended over 300 yards to the east northeast.  The damage over this area was rated low end EF2.  The tornado travelled northeastward and caused additional tree damage in the flood plain.  The tornado approached the intersection of Illinois Route 100 and Coon Creek Road.  A farmstead at this location sustained varying degrees of damage.  One machine shed sustained roof and side damage while a small garage was totally destroyed.  The farm home sustained minor roof damage before the tornado lifted and dissipated.

A tornado touched down about a quarter of a mile north of Rosedale.  The roof of a machine shed was lifted off and tossed 50 to 75 yards to the north northeast.  The tornado then skipped along and north of Fieldon Rosedale Road.  There was mainly large limb and isolated tree damage along this path.  One area of large tree damage was located southwest of the intersection of Fieldon Rosedale Road and Otter Creek Road.  A water pump house was nearly destroyed at this location before the tornado lifted and dissipated.
Thunderstorm winds caused minor roof and siding damage to several homes.  Also, several power poles and trees were blown down.
Thunderstorm winds snapped off numerous power poles at the base from Beaucoup to half a mile east of Beaucoup.

Between 2 and 3 inches fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  A concrete slab was washed out of a low water crossing at the intersection of county roads 120 an 117 about two miles west of Holliday.
Thunderstorm winds destroyed an old barn and a small shed.  Also, a fuel tank was blown off of its stand and came to rest a few yards away.  Another machine shed nearby sustained minor roof damage.

A tornado touched down about 3.5 miles west of Carlinville.  It destroyed a lumber shed, caused minor damage to a nearby home and two grain bins sustained serious damage.  Also, a small shed and outbuilding were destroyed.  The tornado travelled to the northeast causing tree damage and knocked over two more grain bins.  The tornado finally lifted and dissipated near Route 4 about 1.5 miles north of Carlinville.
Numerous power poles were blown down along Bates Road and Lampie Road.

Thunderstorm winds caused widespread damage from four miles west of Standard City to about a mile north of Standard City to about 5 miles northeast of Standard City.  West of Standard City several outbuildings and grains bins were destroyed and several power poles were snapped off along Standard City Road.  North of Standard City, three empty rail cars were blown off the train tracks.  Further to the north and east, several small outbuildings were damaged or destroyed and power lines blown down.  At the intersection of Boston Chapel Road and Waggoner Road, the thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree onto the road.

Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous trees and power lines along Pike County Road 202 next to the Mississippi River.  Twenty homes sustained minor to major damage.  One home was knocked off of its pilings and into a nearby tree.  Another home had the entire roof and porch torn off and thrown into the Mississippi River.
A power pole was snapped off at the base on Highway 28 on the southwest side of Owensville.

Between 2 and 3 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Water covered Highway 15 in Paris and Highway D had 2 feet of water over it around 2 miles east of the intersection with Highway 15, so it was closed for a time.  In Monroe City, one lane of a road in town was being eroded by fast flowing water from a nearby creek.

Between 2 and 3 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Several roads were impassable or closed including McKee Road at Orchard Lane, Broadway at Old Hawthorne Road and Rangeline Road at the intersection with Highway AB.
Between 2 and 3 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Several roads in and around Fulton were impassable.
Between 2 and 3 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  U.S. Highway 50 had several inches of water over it and Route O north of California was flooded.
Between 2 and 3 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads in Mexico and north of town were flooded.
Between 2 and 3 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Highway 16 east of Monticello had water over it and Highway B south of La Grange had water over the roadway.

Between 2 and 3 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  There were areas of flash flooding around Bear Creek, Munger Lane Bridge was washed out and many county roads were closed due to high water.

Between 2 and 3 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  A water rescue had to be performed due to someone driving into 3 feet of running water over Highway F...about 5 miles south of Highway 19.  No injuries were sustained due to the water rescue.

A downburst moved through portions of Alton, blowing down the third story of an old brick building on East Broadway. Some of the bricks and debris were thrown onto the roofs of adjacent buildings.  Further down the block the winds blew in a wall of an abandoned lumber company's metal storage building.  Numerous vehicles in the area sustained damage from the flying debris as well.  Several large trees in the area were blown over as well.  One tree fell onto the roof of a house causing minor damage.  No one was injured due to this event.
Several trees were blown over onto U.S. Highway 50 five miles west of California.
Between 2 and 3 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Highway 89 had two feet of water over it about 4 miles north of Belle.
Up to 4 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded for a time including Wildcat Road, Van Horn Road and Glaser Hollow Road.
Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Highways C and N.

Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding. Numerous roads were flooded for a time including Mill and Jefferson streets in Potosi and New Diggins Road southeast of Potosi. Also, the Big River overtopped its banks and flooded portions of Highway M northeast of Caledonia.

Up to 4 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.   Several roads were closed including U.S. Highway 67 north of Bonne Terre. Also, some ties were washed out from under train tracks just south of Bismarck and several water rescues were performed in the Park Hills area.  Two homes in Park Hills had up to 8 feet of water in their basements due to the heavy rain.

Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Several roads were flooded including U.S. Highway 61 on the north end of St. Mary.  Also, a water rescue had to be performed near Bloomsdale.

Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Several roads were flooded including U.S. Highway 50 between Summerfield and Trenton and Illinois State Route 13 between Lenzburg and Marissa.
Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding. Several roads were flooded including U.S. Highway 51 and Illinois State Route 153.

Thunderstorm winds blew a semi over on Interstate 55 near mile marker 56.  Also, just northwest of Nokomis thunderstorm winds caused minor damage to the soffits and downspouts of a home and the roof of a machine shed. No injuries were reported.

Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  In Ste. Genevieve, several roads were flooded and some homes had to be evacuated due to rapidly rising creeks.  A few other roads in the county were flooded.

A tornado touched down about a mile northeast of Kenwood and traveled to the east.  Numerous trees were sheared, twisted and snapped.  Also, several outbuildings were damaged with displaced roofs, impacted sides and sheet metal thrown up to half a mile away.  The greatest damage was along a stretch of Highway 15 about 2.4 miles north of Edina and along County Roads 155 and 159.  Also, numerous power poles were snapped.  The tornado lifted and dissipated about 4.5 miles east northeast of Edina.

A tornado touched down about 3.5 miles northwest of Knox City and traveled to the east.  Two outbuildings sustained major damage with a displaced roof to one of the buildings and the other sustained major damage to one of its walls.  Numerous tree tops were twisted, torn and/or snapped off.  The most severe damage was along County Road 164, about half a mile south of Route AA.  The tornado lifted and dissipated about 2.5 miles north northeast of Knox City.

Most of the damage in Bismarck was caused by one small tornado.  The survey of damage indicated a brief tornado touched down near Highway BB and Cherry Street, then moved eastward to the northeast edge of town along School Drive.  Most of the damage was to trees, with minor roof damage also common.  More substantial damage was done to a preschool building along Campus Drive, with the gabled roof torn completely from the well constructed masonry building and thrown into the adjacent parking lot.  Damage patterns showed reliable indications of rotation.  The path length was approximately six tenths of a mile long and 200 yards wide.  The severity of roof damage to the preschool building warrents an intensity ranking of EF1 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale.

The damage west of and in the city limits of Gillespie, Illinois was caused by downburst winds and one small tornado.  The survey of the damage indicated an intermittent tornado track from 1.5 miles west of Gillespie to the west side of Gillespie at the High School.  Several homes and outbuidings were damaged along with a power pole.  The tornado was 30 to 40 yards wide and traveled adjacent to Illinois Route 16 towards Gillespie.  A building on the high school campus lost its roof and the damage was rated EF0 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale. Then the tornado lifted and dissipated.

Directly south of the tornado track downburst winds caused widespread damage, that continued through the center of Gillespie.  Numerous buildings had roof damage and many trees were blown over or snapped off.  Wind speed was estimated to have been between 60 and 80 mph within the downburst swath.

Up to four inches of rain fell in Lewis county with an isolated 6.78 inch amount at Ewing in a short amount of time, causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Highway 16 between Monticello and Canton, Route A just north of Monticello, and Route D just south of La Belle.

Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time, causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Route V a mile north of Route AA and Highway 151 near the bridge that goes over the North River was impassable.
Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Illinois Route 94 north of Golden and U.S. Highway 24 west of Camp Point.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines, large tree limbs and a few trees.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs east of town.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs.

Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Paris Road a little south of U.S. Highway 63, Vandiver Road east of the intersection with Paris Road, Highway 124 between U.S. Highway 63 and Hallsville, and the intersection of Thomas Hill Road and Highway V south of Sturgeon.
Several power lines and a tree were blown down at the intersection of Portage Road and Grafton Ferry Road.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs and several trees.
Thunderstorm winds blew over a semi on Interstate 55 near Worden.
A tornado briefly touched down in an open field.  No damage was reported.
A tornado briefly touched down in an open field and traveled to the east.  It bent one power pole, blew down several large tree limbs and a couple of trees before lifting and dissipating.

Several rounds of thunderstorms remained stationary over Madison county dumping up to 7 inches of rain with isolated 10 inch amounts.  Numerous roads were flooded countywide with some sustaining damage due to the flood waters.  Also, numerous basements were flooded with a couple of basement walls collapsing due to the heavy rain.  One water rescue was performed on the Cahokia Creek Diversion Canal just west of Edwardsville.
Up to 5 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding in the Bunker Hill area.  Several roads were closed due to the flooding.
Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Several roads were flooded including Fiddle Creek Road and Little Tavern Road north of Pacific.

Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  The River Des Peres as well as smaller creeks were out of their banks flooding some roads and homes in the area, especially along Wilson Avenue.
Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Several secondary roads were closed due to flooding.

Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Several roads were closed due to flooding.  Also, U.S. Highway 40 had several inches of flowing water over it after Camp Creek went out of its banks near Brownstown.
A tornado briefly touched down and traveled to the east.  Several trees were blown over by the tornado before it lifted and dissipated.

A tornado briefly touched down near the intersection of County roads 229 and 234. The tornado then traveled east along County road 234 for half a mile before lifting and dissipating.  It blew down a few trees as well as numerous large tree limbs.

It was determined that an EF1 tornado occurred 6.5 miles north of Ellington in Reynolds county.  Significant roof damage to 2 homes was noted, as well as a chaotic damage pattern in the hundreds of downed trees.  Debris was scattered for approximately one quarter of a mile.  The tornado damage path was estimated to be approximately 2 miles long and one quarter mile wide.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous trees along Highway F west of Ellington.  Also, several power poles were blown down and a detached garage was severely damaged.

The survey of damage indicated a large swath of straight line winds with estimated speeds of 60 to 70 mph over the northern third of Reynolds county and parts of northwestern Iron county.  Much of the damage was due to fallen trees.  While trees were down over most of Reynolds and Iron counties, the tree damage was most concentrated in an area between Bixby and Reynolds, eastward to an area between Ironton and Glover.  Within that area, microbursts occurred, with estimated wind speeds up to 100 mph.  Three particularly intense microbursts were surveyed along Highway KK just south of Highway J, along Highway UU north of Bunker, and along Highway 49/72 near Lesterville.  In these areas, it was noted that up to 80 percent of the forest had been felled.  Scattered structural damage, mostly to roofs and outbuildings, was also noted.

The survey of damage indicated a large swath of straight line winds with estimated speeds of 60 to 70 mph over the northern third of Reynolds county and large parts of Iron county.  Much of the damage was due to fallen trees.  While trees were down over most of Reynolds and Iron counties, the tree damage was most concentrated in an area between Bixby and Reynolds, eastward to an area between Ironton and Glover.  Within that area, microbursts occurred, with estimated wind speeds up to 100 mph.  One particularly intense microburst was surveyed along Highway 21 about 4 miles south of Arcadia where a radio tower was blown down.  In these areas, it was noted that up to 80 percent of the forest had been felled.  Scattered structural damage, mostly to roofs and outbuildings, was also noted, including the Brown Shoe building in Ironton.
Two large trees were blown down at the intersection of Illinois Routes 4 and 150.
Several large trees were blown down 5 miles south of Potosi on Highway 21, blocking the highway for a time.

Isolated to scattered areas of tree damage were confined across the southern third of St. Francois County.  One microburst hit Iron Mountain where two large trees smashed through two homes.  Also, numerous power lines were blown down.

Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous trees and power lines between Park Hills and Farmington.  Also, a house at the intersection of Liberty Street and Jefferson Street sustained moderate roof damage and a restaurant in town sustained moderate roof damage as well. A semi was blown over just north of Park Hills on U.S. Highway 67.  No one was injured in the incident.

A swath of straight line winds, commonly known as downbursts, with estimated winds of 60 to 75 mph extended from the northwest corner of Madison county through Fredricktown along Highway 72 to the Bollinger county line.  Much of the damage that occurred was due to fallen trees, that were either uprooted or snapped at the base of the trunk.  Structural damage was observed in the town of Fredricktown where roofs and windows were damaged, and a few trees fell onto houses.  Eye witnesses reported that the severe wind gusts lasted up to 45 minutes in duration.  Within the larger swath of severe winds were pockets of more intense damage caused by microbursts with wind gusts greater than 80 mph.  The most intense wind damage occurred in the area from 3 miles north of the intersection of Highways F and V.  Many large trees were blown down in this area which were caused by estimated gusts as high as 90 mph.
Thunderstorm winds caused widespread tree damage as well as power lines in western Randolph county.  Some buildings sustained minor shingle damage.
Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous county roads across northern Knox county were under water due to the heavy rainfall.
Several trees were blown down south of Potosi.
Several large trees were blown down.
Thunderstorm winds peeled pieces of an artificial brick facade off the Renaissance Suites Hotel next to the America's Center.  Also, several trees were blown over in the area.
Several large trees were blown down near the intersection of I-44 and Highway 109.
Some large tree limbs were blown down around town.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs.
Two large sycamores were uprooted. Both were at least 2 and a half feet in diameter.  Also, a three foot diameter oak tree was uprooted and fell onto a house causing moderate damage.

Thunderstorm winds caused moderate roof damage to the St. Louis County Police Headquarters in Clayton.  About a 50 foot by 50 foot section of the roof was peeled back by the thunderstorm winds.  Also, nearby awnings and store signs were damaged and several small trees were snapped off along the street.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines and trees.  Also, a 30 foot by 50 foot barn was blown down and a camping trailer was blown over.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a small shed.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree and tv antenna.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs and power lines around town.  Also, the winds blew over a semi on Interstate 70.  No injuries were reported.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a two foot diameter tree at the intersection of Highway 79 and Route Y.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs.
Thunderstorm winds blew the top out of a large tree on Skinker Blvd. near Washington University.
Several power lines were blown down.  One power line landed on an occupied car.  No one was injured.
A one and a half foot diameter tree was blown down onto an unoccupied car near the intersection of Delmar Blvd. and Midland Blvd.
The large hail broke a few windows on a mobile home.

Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Over 12 inches of water was flowing over Illinois Route 177 west of Okawville.  Also, water was over Illinois Route 160 just south of Addieville.

Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads had water over them including Illinois Route 4 at School View Drive and on Lickenbrock School Road a mile north of Darmstadt Road.
A large tree was blown down onto the road just north of Venedy and another large tree was blown down on Sandpiper Road south southwest of Okawville.
Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Several roads were flooded including Route F just west of Highway 106.

The tornado touched down just northeast of the intersection of North Green Mount Road and Lebanon Avenue in the Eagles Landing Subdivision, where up to 6 homes sustained minor to moderate damage.  From this point the tornado produced a nearly continuous damage path that extended to about 1 mile southeast of the intersection of Highway 4 and Jefferson Road.  It finally lifted as it approached the Kaskaskia River.  The total path length of the tornado is estimated to be 12.8 miles, with an average width of damage of about one-tenth of a mile.  However, straight line winds did cause lesser damage over a wider swath of up to 3 miles. The greatest damage was to a home located just west of the intersection of Highway 4 and Jefferson Road.  Damage there was rated EF2 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale.  Elsewhere along the path of the tornado, the damage was generally in the EF0-EF1 range.

Thunderstorm winds caused damage in O'Fallon and Shiloh.  The junior high school in O'Fallon sustained roof damage.  A two foot diameter tree was blown down onto an unoccupied truck on U.S. Highway 50 near the intersection with N. Green Mount Road.  Numerous other trees and  power lines were blown down.  One tree landed on a house causing moderate damage near the intersection of Main Street and Caroline Street in O'Fallon.

Thunderstorm winds caused minor damage in the Brownstown area.  Three miles west of Brownstown a few windows were blown out of a trailer. Just south of Brownstown several large tree limbs were blown down.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines and large tree limbs around town.
A large rotten tree was blown down onto the roof of a trailer causing moderate damage.
Up to two inches of rain with locally heavier amounts fell over northern Jefferson county.  Lonedell Road had water flowing over it in spots due to the flash flooding.

Up to two inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Three feet of water was over Highway C west of Old Monroe.  A water rescue had to be performed when a car drove into the flood waters and was washed into a ditch.  No injuries were reported.

Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Southbound lanes of Highway 141 were closed for a time at the intersection with Interstate 44 due to several feet of water over the roadway.

Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Six inches of water was flowing over the intersection of Illinois Routes 177 and 4 in Mascoutah.  Also, several roads in the Smithton area were flooded.

Golfball sized hail fell just north of Addieville causing major siding damage to one home as well as several windows in that home and the home next door.  Crops in the area sustained some hail damage as well.

Rain in excess of 3 inches had fallen in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Several spots along County roads 261 and 262 were flooded as well as U.S. Highway 54 south of Kingdom City.  Also, the north outer road of Interstate 70 three miles east of Williamsburg was flooded as well as the south outer road between mile markers 150 and 151.  Numerous other county roads were flooded as well.

In excess of three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time, mainly along the Interstate 70 corridor.  Interstate 70 and adjacent outer roads at the Montgomery/Warren county line were under several feet of water at various locations. Parts of Interstate 70 had to be shut down due to the flooding.  Also, parts of Highway 19 had to be shut down due to flash flooding as well.

In excess of three inches fell in a short amount of time over portions of Warren county.  Highway U at Booneslick Road was flooded and Highway 47 was flooded in spots south of Warrenton.  Also, Interstate 70 and adjacent access roads were flooded in spots near the Warren/Montgomery county line.

Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time over a large portion of St. Charles county.  Numerous secondary roads were flooded.  An off duty weather service employee reported several feet of flowing water through his back yard in St. Peters.
