Numerous roads were flooded including the intersection of Lindbergh Boulevard and Huntleigh Woods Drive.  Manchester Road was closed in both directions east of the intersection with Brentwood Boulevard.  Also, Highway 141 was flooded where it goes under Interstate 44.

Up to five inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Interstate 70 at Shreve Avenue, so the interstate was closed for a time. Also, as section of Interstate 70 was damaged due to a sewer line collapse near the West Florissant Avenue exit.  Several cars stalled in high water on Interstate 64/Hwy 40 near Grand Boulevard.  Flooding also closed Interstate 55 at Loughborough Avenue for a time.  Several homes in the 4400 block of Dryden Avenue and Dryden Court had to be evacuated due to flooding.  Basements had several feet of water in them.

Up to six inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Highway N between Weiss Road and Dardenne Farms Drive.  Several locations in St. Charles had to be evacuated due to flash flooding.  Residents of an 80 unit apartment complex on Cole Boulevard were evacuated after basement and ground floor apartments flooded with more than 2 feet of water.  Also, houses on Hawthorn Avenue were evacuated as flood waters rose very quickly.

Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time onto already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including the intersection of Illinois Routes 13 and 157.  Water rescue had to be performed at this location.  Not long afterwards the two cars were almost completely submerged in the standing water at this intersection.
Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time onto already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Several roads were flooded including Illinois Route 140 near Greenville.
Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time onto already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Several roads were flooded including Illinois Route 153 southwest of Coulterville.

Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time onto already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Highways C and H, as well as Gravens Road and South Chantilly Road.
Thunderstorm winds destroyed a machine shed.  The debris was thrown against the garage causing moderate damage to the garage.
Up to two inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Several roads were flooded including Highway E between Blackwell and Cadet.

Up to four inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  In Canton, almost two and a half inches of rain fell in about an hour.  Several homes had water in them due to the flash flooding.  Also, numerous roads were flooded.
A bow echo moved eastward across Knox county.  Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down countywide.  Some of the trees blown down were three feet in diameter.

An intense bow echo moved through the Clarence area, blowing down numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines.  Several three foot diameter trees were uprooted three miles south of Clarence.  On the east side of town off of U.S. Highway 36, a feed mill sustained quite a bit of damage.  One 500,000 bushel bin was nearly smashed to the ground and a second one sustained major roof damage.  Two smaller bins were damaged as well.  Just southwest of Clarence, a large machine shed was completely destroyed.  Several 2x4s from the shed were thrown through the roof of a two story home nearby.

The first tornado formed near Elm Street and Douglas Avenue, north of U.S. Highway 36 at approximately 1245 a.m. CDT.  The roof and walls of a corrugated steel building buckled on the west and south sides, along with a portion of the roof.  The tornado moved across U.S. Highway 36 and destroyed three unoccupied house trailers.  Debris was tossed about 100 yards from the trailers. The tornado continued to move east-southeast and caused roof damage to the town power and water plants on Chestnut Street west of Shelby Street. A portion of the gables holding the roof of the power plant was uplifted and tossed approximately 50 yards to the east.  Much of the water plant's roof was removed and tossed 40 to 50 yard to the east. The tornado then caused minor roof damage on homes and snapped numerous large trees about 10 to 20 feet from the base.  Some of the large branches fell on top of vehicles.  The tornado then caused extensive damage to the roof of the two story town museum on Center Street (Highway 15). Several bricks fell to the ground from the top of the museum roof.  Additional tree damage was found east and southeast of the town museum building.  The path length was 1.15 miles with width varying between 50 and 70 yards.  The tornado was rated an EF1.

The second tornadic damage track was just to the south of the first tornado.  It began west of South Center Street, where significant tree damage occurred. Some of the trees fell on top of homes.  The tornado traveled east-southeast and hit an assisted living home on Shelbina Avenue.  Roof damage was found at this location.  Other large trees were damaged in the vicinity of the assisted living home.  The tornado continued to the east-southeast and destroyed a large machine shed built in 2008.  The east, south and west sides and the roof of the machine shed were tossed into several corn fields.  The tornado then crossed County Road 441, where it hit a tree line with several trees snapped 15 to 20 feet from the base and tree trunk diameters ranging from 1 to 2.5 feet. The width of the damage in this area was 50 yards.  The path length was 1.22 miles with a max width of 70 yards.  The tornado was rated an EF1.
An intense bow echo moved through LaBelle, blowing down numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines.

An intense bow echo moved through Lewistown, blowing down numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines.  Two large trees fell onto homes in town causing extensive damage.  One house had its roof shifted which caused the ceiling to crash to the floor.  No injuries were reported.

An intense bow echo moved through Ewing, blowing down numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines.  The radio tower at the Ewing Fire Station was blown down on top of the station.  Also, one tree fell onto a mobile home causing extensive damage.  Another mobile home had part of its tin roof ripped off.  A nearby carport was flipped over onto an unoccupied car.
An intense bow echo moved through Monticello, blowing down numerous tree limbs and power lines.
An intense bow echo moved through Canton, blowing down numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines.  A 62 mph wind gust was measured at Lock and Dam 20.
An intense bow echo moved through LaGrange, blowing down numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines.  Also, a large barn lost most of its roof and parts of several walls.
A intense bow echo moved through the area, blowing down numerous large trees, tree limbs and power lines.  Several power poles were snapped as well.

A tornado touched down about 3.5 miles south of Monroe City on the west side of U.S. Highway 24 and travelled to the southeast, crossing the highway before lifting and dissipating along County Road 591.  There was significant tree damage along the path.  Trees were 60 to 80 feet tall with trunk diameters of 3 to 4 feet.  Some of the trees were snapped a third to half way up.  Other large trees were uprooted.  Some of the large tree limbs were tossed 50 to 70 yards to the east southeast.  The total path length was four tenths of a mile and the max width was 40 yards.  The tornado was rated an EF1.

A tornado touched down on Hereford Lane, about 3 miles southeast of Monroe City in northwestern Ralls County.  It travelled to the southeast blowing down numerous trees.  Several large trees were snapped half way up the trunk or uprooted within a defined relatively narrow path.  Most of the trees were between 50 and 60 feet tall with trunk diameters varying between 2 and 3 feet wide.  Also, a barn sustained moderate damage with part of its roof blown off.  The tornado lifted and dissipated on Demoss Road.  The total path length was six tenths of a mile with a max width of 70 yards.  The tornado was rated an EF0.

An intense bow echo moved through the area knocking down numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines.  The doors were blown off of a couple of hangers at Monroe City Regional Airport, damaging several planes.
Thunderstorm winds blew about a third of the shingles off of two homes in this location.  Also, several large tree limbs were blown down.

An intense bow echo moved through blowing down numerous large trees, tree limbs and power lines.  Just southwest of Center on Highway 19, a line of trees extending about 200 yards (30 to 50 feet tall) were uprooted.  In Center, numerous tree limbs were blown down and a few trees were uprooted.  Four homes sustained minor roof damage from fallen tree limbs.  Further northeast along Highway 19, several power poles were snapped off.  In New London, several more trees were blown down, as well as numerous tree limbs.
An intense bow echo moved through the area, blowing down numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines.  Near Holliday on U.S. Highway 24, a large machine shed was destroyed.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees on the west side of town.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees and tree limbs around town.  Also, several homes lost a few shingles and some siding.  A couple of light poles were blown down as well.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees and uprooted several more.

Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines around town.  One power line fell across part of the west bound lanes of U.S. Highway 54, so the westbound lanes had to be closed temporarily closed until the line was removed.

An intense bow echo moved through Marion County. The most significant damage was over northern portions of the county.  Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down.  Some of the trees blown down were between 3 and 4 feet in diameter.  A few old barns were blown down by the winds.

An intense bow echo moved through Hannibal knocking down numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines.  A large portion of a tree fell onto a house causing damage in several locations on the roof, allowing water into the residence.  The weight of the tree limb caused rear portion of the roof to collapse into the attic area of the house.  No injuries were reported.  Several fallen trees pulled down power lines and poles when they fell.

Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees, tree limbs and power lines around town.  One large tree limb pulled down a power line and snapped the power pole it was attached to.  Parts of the tree limb and power pole caused minor damage to an unoccupied van parked nearby.

An intense bow echo moved through Pike County.  Several large trees, numerous tree limbs and power lines were blown down in Bowling Green.  Part of one fallen tree landed on an unoccupied vehicle destroying it.  No injuries were reported.
An intense bow echo moved through Frankford blowing down numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines.  Several large trees were also uprooted including a tree that was over 200 years old.

An intense bow echo moved through Louisiana blowing down several trees, numerous tree limbs and power lines.  Several large tree limbs blocked a couple of streets in town.  No structural damage or injuries were reported.
An intense bow echo moved through the area, several large trees and a couple of power lines were blown down just southwest of Mendon.

An intense bow echo moved through Quincy blowing down hundreds of trees, tree limbs and power lines.  The fallen trees, tree limbs and power lines blocked a lot of streets in town causing major navigation issues for drivers for several days.  It also took several days to restore power throughout town. Numerous trees fell onto homes causing varying degrees of damage.  Also, several vehicles sustained varying degrees of damage from fallen trees and limbs.  Amazingly no injuries were reported.

An intense bow echo moved through the Payson area knocking down numerous large trees, tree limbs and power lines.  Some of the fallen trees and tree limbs caused varying degrees of damage to several homes in the area.  Also, part of the roof of a house in the Briarwood Subdivision was blown off.

An intense bow echo moved through Coatsburg, Camp Point and Clayton.  Hundreds of trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down.  A couple of power poles were also snapped off.  Several trees and tree limbs landed on homes causing minor to moderate roof damage.  Also, in Camp Point the entire roof of a business was blown off.  One woman was injured after falling down her basement steps as her family was taking shelter from the storm.  It took more than an hour for an ambulance to respond to the woman's home near Coatsburg because of the downed trees blocking highways and lots of secondary roads.
An intense bow echo moved through blown down several trees, tree limbs and power lines in Loraine.
An intense bow echo moved through the Liberty area.  A barn lost part of its roof due to the thunderstorm winds.
An intense bow echo moved through Brown County.  Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down.  Many were blocking roads.
An intense bow echo moved through Baylis.  Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees, tree limbs and power lines.  Also, the winds caused a large dent in a 55,000 bushel grain bin.

An intense bow echo moved through the Perry and Griggsville area.  Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down.  In Perry, a large pecan tree was uprooted and fell onto a house causing extensive damage.  Also, when the tree fell over the roots broke a gas line causing a leak.  No injuries were reported.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees, tree limbs and power lines.  One tree fell onto an unoccupied car in Warrenton causing major damage.
Thunderstorm wind blew down several large tree limbs.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power poles onto U.S. Highway 67 south of Jerseyville near Crystal Lake Road.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines in town.

Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time onto already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Routes K, J and B, as well as Highway 11.  Also, Highway 151 just east of Novelty was flooded.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees as well as numerous tree limbs.  Also, a couple of homes sustained moderate shingle damage.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree limb onto East New Haven Road.  Also, a large tree was blown down onto Highway WW at the intersection with Blackthorn Lane.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs and damaged a sign at an amusement park.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a tree onto Illinois Route 157 near Old Saint Louis Road.  Also, a tree was blown down onto a trailer near Thunderbird Lane.  No injuries were reported.

Thunderstorm winds caused quite a bit of damage around town.  It blew off part of the roof of a commercial real estate building near the intersection of Highway 47 and Veterans Memorial Parkway.  Also, numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down.  The winds blew the roof off of a bank and the accompanying rains caused substantial damage inside the building.  A few trees and tree limbs landed on homes causing minor to moderate roof damage.  One tree landed on a car in the Taco Bell drive through.  The driver was not injured.

Thunderstorm winds blew down two large trees onto Bell Road.  Also, a couple of power poles were blown down.  Further east in town, several trees and numerous tree limbs were blown down.  A church lost its steeple due to the winds.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees, numerous tree limbs and power lines around town.
Thunderstorm winds snapped off a couple of five inch diameter trees.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs.  One tree limb caused minor roof damage to a house.

Lightning struck a two story house on Clark Lane causing a fire.  No injuries were reported and fortunately the fire department was able to extinguish the flames fairly quickly.  Damage was estimated around $25,000.

Up to four inches of rain fell in less than an hour causing flash flooding in and around the Troy area.  Four swift water rescues had to be performed and numerous roads were closed due to flooding for a few hours.  No injuries were reported.  A 5 foot by 12 foot flat trailer from a business was swept away by the floodwaters.  It went underneath a small bridge before coming to rest about 75 to 100 feet away from the business.

Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs.  A couple of the limbs were blocking Highway D about one to two miles north of intersection with Highway Y.  Also, a couple of tree tops were snapped off in this area.
Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time onto already saturated soils causing flash flooding.  Several roads in the northern part of the county were flooded for a few hours.

Up to 6 inches of rain fell in a four hour span causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded especially in Oakville.  Several basements were flooded and a vehicle became stranded in flood waters near the intersection of Pierwood Drive and Broken Horse Lane.  Two people had to be rescued from the car.  No injuries were reported.

Up to four inches of rain fell over the northern portions of Jefferson County in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Highway 30 at Dittmer Road and Highway Z near intersection with Highway A.  Also, several basements in Herculaneum, Festus and Crystal City had water in them.  One car dealership in Herculaneum had water high enough to get into 12 cars on the used car lot.
Thunderstorm winds blew down an oak tree onto a car that was travelling on Lemay Ferry Road.  Fortunately the two occupants were not injured in the incident.

Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including North Market Street in Waterloo, C Road south of Valmeyer and Bluff Road.  Several homes had water in them, as well as a couple of businesses.

Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Several roads were flooded including Highway D at Babiak Road and at the intersection of Highway Y and Snowdell Road.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees and numerous tree limbs around town.

Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous trees, tree limbs, power poles and power lines.  Also, a billboard was blown down onto Highway 79.  A few of the fallen trees and tree limbs landed on vehicles, garages and homes in town.  At least one garage was destroyed by a fallen tree.  A hangar at Hannibal Regional Airport was damaged by the winds.  The doors on the western side of the building were blown open and could not be closed.  No airplanes in the hangar were damaged by the storm.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees and power lines.  Also, some shingles were blown off of a home two miles northeast of Payson.

Thunderstorm winds blew part of the roof off of the library, causing some water damage to the museum that is on the second floor of the building.  Also, numerous tree limbs and power lines were blown down.

Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees and numerous tree limbs.  Also, a small shed had two pieces of plywood blown off and a metal awning at a local business was blown off and landed next to a van causing minor damage to the vehicle.
Thunderstorm winds blew a large tree over as well as numerous tree limbs.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines around town.

The damage across portions of Greene County was due to damaging downburst winds and localized microbursts embedded within the larger area of downburst winds.  The damage area was generally confined from Carrollton to Greenfield and along Illinois Route 108 over the central and eastern parts of Greene County.  One home in Greenfield was severely damaged as a large tree partially fell through the roof of the home.  A few other large trees also fell on the west side of town.  The western sections of the roof of a large machine shed west of Greenfield were also uplifted and tossed between 50 and 100 yards to the east.  A few other homes in Greenfield sustained minor roof damage as some shingles were removed.  A weather station located southeast of Greenfield measured a wind gust to 74 mph.  Between Carrollton and Greenfield, several corn fields sustained damage as corn was partially bent with pockets of flattened corn.  The area of wind damage extended approximately 14 miles along Illinois Route 108.  The damage was 1.5 miles wide at the beginning of the damage path to 3.5 miles wide at the end.
Thunderstorm winds snapped off a large tree and blew down numerous tree limbs.  Some siding was blown off of a house.
Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Several roads were flooded including Highway 15 about three to four miles north of Ednina.
Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Several roads were flooded including Illinois Route 37 near Walnut Hill Road and Interstate 57 near mile marker 113.

Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Several roads were flooded including County Line Road in several locations, at intersection with Illinois Route 154 and about a mile south of intersection with Illinois Route 13.  At least one car became stranded on a flooded road about 7 miles southeast of Walsh.
Up to two inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Several roads were flooded including Highway F north northwest of Potosi.
Thunderstorm winds blew over a wind mill on a far just outside of Plainville.
Thunderstorm winds snapped off several large trees and blew down numerous tree limbs.  Also, the winds blew off part of a metal roof from a barn and blew in a garage door on a residence.

Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees along Vermundy Road northwest of Kinmundy.  Also, a tree was blown across Illinois Route 37 about a mile north of Alma and several other trees were blown down in Kinmundy.
Thunderstorm winds blew half of a large tree onto U.S. Highway 54.  Also, several other trees and numerous tree limbs were blown down around town.

Lightning struck a building that housed the sales/gift shop of a nursery.  Fire spread rapidly through the building and it is considered a total loss.  No injuries were reported and the other buildings nearby were unharmed.

Lightning struck a cell phone that a 39 year old woman was using at Cosmo Park on the northside of Columbia.  She was taken to a local hospital to be checked out.  She only had some initial numbness in her arm.  She was treated and released the next morning.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a tree onto a house causing minor damage.  No injuries were reported.

Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees around town.  Also, portions of corn fields just east of Centralia Municipal Airport were flattened by the downburst winds.  Also, there was some minor road flooding in town after over an inch of rain fell in about 30 minutes.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large oak trees.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees along Highway UU west of Columbia.  Also, a tent was blown over at the Boone County Fair Grounds.  This caused one minory injury.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted several trees, destroyed a machine shed and blew part of the roof off of another building in town.
Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Several roads were flooded including the intersection of Kinlou and Vandeveer Roads.
Lightning hit a tree and transferred to power lines causing some electrical damage.  Two people were injured by the lightning strike and one had to be briefly hospitalized.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several tree limbs as well as one tree.  The tree pulled down some power lines in downtown Marissa.

Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs around town.  One large tree limb fell onto power lines attached to the house.  This pulled the electric meter off of the house.  No other structural damage was reported at this location.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous tree limbs and several power lines.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees, numerous large tree limbs as well as several power lines.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a few power lines and tree limbs.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs around Belgrade.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs around Lake Killarney.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs.  A couple of the limbs pulled down power lines causing power outages around town.
A small tree was blown down onto Main Street in Linn.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs around town.  A couple of the limbs pulled down power lines.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs and shredded a boat canopy.

Thunderstorm winds caused a swath of tree, tree limb and power line damage about two to three blocks wide, extending from Doran Drive and Reavis Barracks Road to the Park Lawn Cemetery.   There was a second swath of wind damage just southeast of the first one, extending from near Wycliffe Court and Rosegarden Road to Teleford Drive and Barnsley Drive.  Several large trees were blown down along each path.  Also, several homes in the area sustained minor shingle damage.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree across West Essex Avenue near Evans Avenue in Kirkwood.  It pulled down several power lines when it fell.

Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large trees onto Midland Boulevard, with some of them blocking the road.  Also, the winds blew gravel off of a roof on Delmar Boulevard damaging several vehicles in a parking lot.  A couple of cars had several windows broken on them due to the gravel.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines and numerous large tree limbs in Brentwood, Rock Hill and Maplewood.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree and snapped a telephone pole.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several tree limbs and power lines.  Also, part of the roof of a barn was blown off.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large pine tree.

Thunderstorm winds destroyed an outbuilding on the north side of Belleville West High School.  Also, the tops of several trees were snapped off in the area and a small shed was destroyed.  Two sets of small bleachers were blown over.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines in town.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a two foot diameter tree limb.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs around town.
Large hail caused minor damage to several cars in town.
Thunderstorm winds picked up a carport and blew it across the front yard of a residence in town.
Thunderstorm winds caused minor roof damage to a residence along old Route 66.

Thunderstorm winds blew the skylight and doors off of a shed on a farm northeast of Addieville.  Also, five windsow were blown out on an unoccupied farm house and a grain auger was blown over.  The debris was scattered up to half a mile from the farmstead.
Thunderstorm winds blew over three power poles near the Ste. Genevieve/St. Francois county line, just east of Farmington.

A tornado touched down on Madison County Road 437 (about half a mile north of intersection with Co. Road 424) at 255 am.  At this location part of the roof of an abandoned house was blown off and several windows were blown out.  Also, there was lots of tree damage in the area.  The damage was rated EF1 in this location.  The tornado continued to the east northeast.  On Madison County Road 431, about a mile north of the intersection with Highway C, a home was completely blown apart and swept off the foundation.  The debris was thrown in different directions.  It was not bolted down into the concrete foundation, only nailed, so the EF rating given for this was EF2.  All the hardwood trees next to the home were uprooted.  The width of the damage path in this location was 200 yards.  Further to the east additional tree damage was found on Madison County Road 411 near the intersection with Highway EE.  As it travelled to the east northeast, the tornado approached U.S. Highway 67 near Zion.  On the west side of U.S. Highway 67, about a third of a mile north of the intersection with Highway JJ, an abandoned single wide mobile home was rolled onto its roof.  A bit further north of the mobile home, there was about a 100 yard wide swath of hardwoods that were uprooted on the west side of U.S. Highway 67.  All of the damage in this area was rated EF1.  Further to the east, about 1.6 miles west northwest of Marquand on Highway A, there was significant roof damage to a large well-constructed barn.  There was some evidence of convergent flow in the tree damage nearby.  A utility pole was bent over back to the south.  Just to the east of the tree damage, about half the roof was lifted off of a business and numerous large oaks were uprooted in the area.  Damage width was about 200 yards in this location with a rating of EF1.  On Highway F, about two tenths of a mile north of the intersection with Highway A, a large swath of trees was uprooted, with additional sporadic tree damage along the rest of the path before crossing into Bollinger County (WFO Paducah���s forecast area) about a mile and a half northeast of Marquand on the south side of Highway A at 320 am.  The path length in Madison County was 21.54 miles with a max width of 200 yards and a max rating of EF2.  Overall, the tornado was on the ground for 31.88 miles with a max width of 800 yards and a max rating of EF2.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a machine shed as well as numerous large tree limbs and a fence in Cherry Box.

Thunderstorm winds uprooted a couple of trees and blew over a few sheds on Highland Drive, just northwest of Cuba.  In Cuba, several power lines were blown down, as well as large tree limbs and a large billboard.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree onto Highway 49, blocking it for a time.
Thunderstorm winds caused minor roof damage and blew down a couple of small sheds between Womac and Barnett.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree onto Highway C east of Annapolis.
Several cars sustained broken windows due to the large hail.

A tornado briefly touched down just west of Illinois Route 160 about a mile north of New Baden.  As it travelled to the east it caused minor roof damage to several homes in a subdivision and topped off several trees.  A couple of fences were blow over as well.  It crossed Illinois Route 160, just south of intersection with Court Road, lifting and dissipating about a quarter of a mile east of Illinois Route 160.
Thunderstorm winds caused minor shingle damage to a few homes just east southeast of Belleville.

Numerous reports of large hail in the New Melle area...with the largest being tennis ball size. Also, there were several reports of siding damage, tree limbs knocked down and a couple of cars sustained windshield damage.
Numerous reports of one inch hail fell in a large swath from just west of Lambert-St. Louis International Airport, across the airport grounds and continued to the northeast of the airport.

A wide swath of large hail fell from areas along and west of I-64 near Highways N and DD to the east northeast through the cities of Lake St. Louis, Dardenne Prairie, and O'Fallon.  The largest hail stones, baseball size, were reported near the intersection of Winghaven Boulevard and I-64. There were numerous reports of one to two inch diameter hail.
Numerous reports of large hail fell over portions of St. Peters and St. Charles.  The largest hail stones, one and a half inches in diameter, were reported in northeastern St. Peters.
Numerous reports of large hail were reported in Carrollton.  The largest hail stones were baseball size.
Numerous reports of one inch hail on the south side of Jefferson City.
There were several reports of one inch hail on the north side of Columbia.
Up to two inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding. Several roads were flooded including Highway N between Bourbon and Anthonies Mill.

Up to two inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Several roads were flooded including U.S. Highway 50 just east of Linn and Highways Y and NN in far southeastern Osage County.
Up to two inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding. Several roads were flooded including Highway A just north of Bland.
There were several reports of one inch hail in Crestwood and Kirkwood.
Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous secondary roads were flooded and several creeks were out of their banks.

Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including streets and yards in Cuba.  Also, Highway C just northwest of Bourbon and Highway ZZ just west of Cuba.
A storm chaser reported a brief tornado in an open field south of Iuka.  No damage was reported.
Nickel size hail was reported at the campground in Stephen A. Forbes State Park.

Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including several in Jefferson City.  Also, a small stream was out of its banks and flowing swiftly over a bridge just east of St. Martins.  One water rescue had to be performed in Jefferson City when they drove into a flooded roadway and got stuck.
Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Several roads were flooded including Highway RA southeast of Linn.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large cedar tree onto Highway C near intersection with Highway CC.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees, power lines and destroyed a large machine shed as well as a couple of smaller sheds just northwest of Rockport along Illinois Route 96.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs near Birdie Hills Road and Mexico Road.
Numerous reports of golfball to hen egg size hail throughout town.
Numerous reports of large hail with the biggest hail stones being ping pong ball size.
Numerous reports of large hail was reported across northern portions of St. Louis County.  There were reports of large hail in Hazelwood, Florissant, Ferguson, Black Jack and Riverview.
There were numerous reports of large hail across Granite City. The largest hail stones were tennis ball size.
There were numerous reports of large hail across Collinsville.  The largest hail stones were tennis ball size. Golfball size hail was reported at Cahokia Mounds State Park.

There were numerous reports of large hail across Fairview Heights.  The largest hail stones were tennis ball size reported near the intersection of I-64 and Bunkum Road.  Also, numerous roofs sustained shingle damage and numerous cars sustained dents from the hail stones.

There were numerous reports of large hail across O'Fallon.  The largest hail stones were three and a half inches by two inch disc shaped stones. Baseball sized hail was reported at Scott Air Force Base.
There were numerous reports of large hail across Lebanon.  The largest hail stones were baseball size.  Numerous car windows and several windows on homes sustained damage.

There were numerous reports of large hail across Belleville and Swansea.  The largest hail stones reported were three inches in diameter. There were numerous reports of damage to vehicles from the hail.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several signs along I-64.  Also, a few large trees were snapped off on the southeast side of O'Fallon.

A swath of large hail was reported in the New Baden area.  There were numerous reports of vehicles with their windows broken both in town and along Interstate 64 between mile markers 27 and 30.  The largest hail stones were baseball size.
Thunderstorm winds blew plywood and other small pieces of debris onto the westbound lanes of Interstate 70 between mile markers 212 and 213.  Source of the debris unknown at this time.

A wide swath of large hail fell in an area from the Missouri River near Highway 364 eastward through the WestPort Plaza area to near Lindbergh Boulevard.  Numerous cars had their windows broken out at WestPort Plaza.  Also, numerous homes sustained roof and siding damage.

There were numerous reports of golfball sized hail across St. Ann.
There were numerous reports of large hail in Olivette, with some of the stones as large as baseballs.
Large hail fell across De Soto with the biggest stones being tennis ball size.
There were numerous reports of large hail across St. John.  The largest hail stones were baseball size near the intersection of St. Charles Rock Road and I-170.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a two and a half foot diameter tree as well as numerous large tree limbs in Brentwood.
Baseball sized hail was reported in on the north side of Brentwood.
Golfball sized hail was reported in University City and on the Washington University campus.

A swath of large hail fell over central portions of the city of St. Louis.  Three inch hail was reported at the Edward Jones Dome with golfball sized hail reported at the intersection of Tucker Boulevard and Market Street as well as at the intersection of Hampton Avenue and Interstate 44.
Another swath of large hail was reported over the northern portions of the city of St. Louis.  The biggest stones were three inches in diameter.

Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees.  One tree fell onto a house on Pernod Avenue causing moderate damage.  Another tree was blown over onto an unoccupied car on Marquette Avenue near Tilles Park.  On Potomac Avenue a large tree was uprooted and landed near a house causing minor roof damage.  A fifteen inch diameter tree was snapped off near the intersection of Mackland Avenue and Southwest Avenue.

About 100 people were injured and one person was killed when a tent collapsed on a crowd that was gathered after a Cardinals game at Kilroy's Sports Bar (720 South Seventh Street). Seventeen people were taken to area hospitals and treated for their injuries. According to radar data and eye witness reports, outflow winds of 50 to 60 mph from the rear flank downdraft of the supercell thunderstorm arrived between 3:40 p.m. and 3:50 p.m. causing the localized damage near Busch Stadium.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines and large tree limbs.
Enough hail fell that it looked like it had snowed in Farina.  Dense fog briefly developed due to the large amounts of hail.
Thunderstorm winds destroyed two garages in town and blew the roofs off of a couple of barns.  Also, some homes sustained shingle damage and several trees were blown over.
Hail was covering the ground.
Hail was covering the ground on the southside of Marissa.

Between 3 and 4 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including U.S. Highway 63 near Ashland, Route Y near the Boone/Callaway county line, and the intersection of Highway 22 and Schunemeyer Road just northwest of Centralia.

Between 2 and 3 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Highway F at the intersection with County Road 341 and Highway PP about a mile north of Highway 94.
Between 2 and 3 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Highway 15 north of Mexico.
Two heat related deaths were reported in Madison County. One in Collinsville and one in Troy.
A 51 year old man was killed by a lightning strike when he stepped out of his front door onto the porch.
On July 3, Brown County was listed as being in D2, severe drought status. By the end of he month it was upgraded to D3, extreme drought status.
On July 3, Pike County was listed as being in D2, severe drought status. By the end of he month it was upgraded to D3, extreme drought status.
On July 3, Monroe County was listed as being in D2, severe drought status. By the end of he month it was upgraded to D3, extreme drought status.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines.
There were numerous reports of large hail in Cottleville, including one inch hail on the campus of St. Charles Community College.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a six inch diameter tree as well as several power lines near the intersection of Clarkson Road and Clayton Road.
Hail mostly the size of quarters, but a few were golfball sized near the intersection of I-64/Hwy 40 and Boones Crossing.
Large hail up to ping pong ball size fell across Ballwin. An eleven year old girl sustained minor injuries to her head and arm due to the large hail.
Hail fell at the intersection of Hillsboro Road and Bridleridge Crossing Spur.
Several reports of large hail with the largest hail reported at the intersection of Rock Creek Road and W 4 Ridge Road.

Thunderstorm winds associated with a line of storms blew down numerous tree limbs and a few trees in Perry, Pittsfield and Pleasant Hill.  One unoccupied vehicle in Pittsfield was damaged from a flying piece of plywood.
Thunderstorm winds caused isolated damage on the west side of Columbia.  A large tree fell onto a house causing roof damage.  Also, a retractable awning on a nearby house was snapped in half.
The high temperature reached 99 degrees in St. Louis. The relative humidity was low thus the Heat Index did not ready advisory criteria. There was one heat related death in the City of St. Louis.
St. Louis County reported 16 people treated and 4 hospitalized due to heat related illness on June 29, and 20 treated and 3 hospitalized on June 30.

The City of St. Louis reported 2 heat related deaths on June 30. An 80 year old man died in his home. There was a window air conditioner but it was not turned on. A 74 year old woman was found dead in her apartment. There was central air conditioning that was not turned on.
St. Charles County reported 1 heat related death. a 64 year old male died in his mobile home. An air conditioner had been removed some time ago due to expense.

St. Louis County reported 2 heat related deaths. In all cases, air conditioners were not working or not turned on. The County also reported 88 heat related cases treated at area hospital emergency rooms.
The City of St. Louis reported 14 heat related deaths. In all cases, air conditioners were not working or not turned on. The City 84 heat related cases treated at City hospital emergency rooms.
A 76 year old LeMay man died in his home from heat related causes. The home had air conditioning but it was not working. The high temperature that day was 95.
A 62 year old homeless died from heat related causes in East St. Louis. He was found in an abandoned home.

An 89 year old man in Ballwin died form heat related causes. The home had air conditioning but it was not working properly. The Health Department also reported 34 heat related cases treated at area emergency rooms.
The City of St. Louis Health Department reported 19 heat related cases treated at hospital emergency rooms.
The County Health Department reported 6 people treated for heat related illnesses at area hospitals.
The County Health Department reported 6 people treated at area emergency rooms for heat related illness.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs in Steeleville and Percy.
Large hail fell on the south side of Marissa.  The large hail cracked a windshield on one vehicle.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees onto Route 221 just east of Pilot Knob.  Also, part of the roof of a patio was blown off just south of Pilot Knob on Highway 21.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees and took some shingles off of a few roofs.
Thunderstorm winds blew over a 5th wheel camper, flattened some corn and uprooted or snapped off a couple of large trees.

Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees, as well as tree limbs and power lines on the west and central parts of St. Clair.  Some of the trees landed on homes causing minor to moderate damage.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees and power lines in Doe Run.  A couple of the power lines were blown down onto Route 221.

A microburst caused extensive damage in Cuba.  The damage area started less than a quarter of a mile southwest of the intersection of Interstate 44 and Highway 19.  In this location, several medium sized trees and large tree limbs fell to the southwest and west.  A little further to the south numerous large tree limbs and a few large trees were blown down along and west of Oak Hill Avenue and south of Grove Street.  Additional large tree branches and a few large trees fell on Florence Street between Forest Street and Oak Hill Avenue.  Most of the branches fell to the south and southwest showing a divergent wind damage pattern.  More tree and large limb damage occurred just northeast of the intersection of School Avenue and Forest Street near the grounds of Holy Cross Catholic Church.  Another microburst occurred at the intersection of West Washington and North Smith Street.  A grocery store lost much of its roof and was displaced into the parking lot south of the store.  A fatality occurred in the parking lot where debris from the roof shattered the front window of a car killing the 28 year old woman who was in the vehicle at the time.  A person in a nearby car sustained minor injuries from the flying debris as well.  Additional minor roof damage occurred at the Cuba post office where some of the roofing material was peeled off.  The length of the microburst damage path was approximately three quarters of a mile and about a third of a mile wide.  Based on the tree and structural damage, winds associated with the microbursts were estimated between 65 and 75 mph.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees and powerlines in Kirkwood.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees and powerlines in Pilot Knob.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees on Vesper Drive.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees on Brookvale Terrace.

Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous tree limbs in Holts Summit and in the New Bloomfield area.  Also, the winds caused a semi to overturn in the median of U.S. Highway 54 just south of New Bloomfield.  The driver sustained minor injuries.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree onto power lines in Waterloo near the intersection of 6th Street and Main Street.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees in Villa Ridge. Also, numerous power lines were blown down in eastern Franklin county as the storm slowly moved to the south.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs in Union.
A small microburst flattened portions of a corn field about a mile north of Bartelso.  Also, a few nearby trees were uprooted and several large tree branches were blown down.
Numerous large tree limbs were blown down between Evansville and just southwest of Modoc.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees on the 400 block of West Mill Street in Waterloo.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs around Mehlville.
Several large tree limbs were blown down in Shrewsbury.
Thunderstorm wind blew down a large tree.  Part of the tree landed on a house causing moderate damage.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs.
Thunderstorm winds caused minor roof and door damage to a machine shed 5 miles south of Hull.  Also, numerous small tree limbs and several power lines were blown down.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous tree limbs as well as a few large trees.

A microburst moved through the Shaw's Garden Subdivision, blowing down several large trees and numerous tree limbs.  A couple of homes and vehicles were damaged by fallen trees or tree limbs.  Also, numerous power lines and a couple of power poles were blown down. The damage extended across Highway 109 into the Augustine Heights Subdivision snapping off a couple of large trees as well as tree limbs.
Thunderstorm winds blew a 24 foot camper into a propane tank along Jj Road south of Waterloo.

Thunderstorm winds caused widespread tree and power line damage across Washington. Two people sustained minor injuries from flying debris in the parking lot of the Washington Town and Country Fair.  Also, several tents were blown down. Fortunately, the fair grounds had been evacuated.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted a one and a half foot diameter tree near the Warren/St. Charles county line just off of Highway 94.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees between Villa Ridge and Pacific.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs in Chesterfield and Maryland Heights.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees and numerous tree limbs and power lines over the northern portions of Jefferson County.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs and power lines between Ruma and Ellis Grove. Also, the winds snapped a power pole.
There were several reports of nickel size hail south of Bland.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree limb.
A line of severe storms moved southeast through Montgomery County. Numerous tree limbs and a few power lines were blown down in Nokomis and Irving.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs as well as a couple of power lines.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines in town.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees around Shobonier.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree limb onto a power line.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs.  One tree was blown down blocking a side road in Centralia.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees just south of Hoffman.
A tornado briefly touched down on the north end of Chouteau Island...north of Interstate 270.  No damage was reported.

The tornado first touched down about 200 yards south of County Road 1150, about 80 yards west of U.S. Highway 67, damaging a four car garage.  The roof of the garage was mostly removed from the structure with some small sections of the roof displaced a quarter of a mile to the north in an open field.  The tornado travelled to the north over County Road 1150 and snapped some medium sized tree limbs.  One power pole was snapped in this area. Also, a medium size storage unit was damaged with pieces of the storage unit displaced over 100 yards to the north.  The tornado moved north nearly parallel to 6th Street where small and large tree limbs were snapped.  Several witnesses including the local street department observed the tornado as it entered and moved through a residential area west of downtown Carrollton.  One home near the southern part of the residential area sustained minor roof damage with shingles removed from the roof.  The tornado crossed Illinois Route 108 just west of U.S. Highway 67 before lifting and dissipating.  Mainly small to medium tree limbs were blown down as the tornado travelled north through this area.  The path length of the tornado was approximately 1.44 miles and had a damage width which varied between 40 and 60 yards.  The damage was rated EF0.

A tornado touched down on the south side of Fort Zumwalt North High School on the south end of the school running track.  The tornado travelled to the northwest along the periphery of the school grounds, knocking down several trees.  Also, some debris was blown onto the tennis courts and a truck parked nearby had one of its windows broken from flying debris.  As the tornado curved back to north, it went over the football field.  A separate set of standalone aluminum bleachers on the south end of the main grandstand were blown over.  The tornado then blew the soccer goal posts, which had been on the ends of the football field, west towards a line of trees that separates the school property from a nearby subdivision.  The tornado then crossed Tom Ginnever Avenue.  It knocked down several small trees and blew unanchored playground equipment belonging to a nearby preschool to the north towards a small parking lot.  Before lifting and dissipating, the tornado knocked over a small set of bleachers and a portion of a 4 foot high chain-link fence that surrounded the outfield of a baseball diamond.  The tornado was on the ground for a little over four tenths of a mile and had a max path width of 120 yards.  The damage was rated EF0.
By the middle of the month most of Boone County was moved into Exceptional Drought (D4) status.
By the middle of the month, most of Moniteau County was moved into Exceptional Drought (D4) status.
Thunderstorm winds snapped an aluminum flag pole.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees in Girard and snapped a power pole off at its base in Nilwood, knocking out power to the town.

A line of thunderstorms moved through the area.  In Raymond, a gutter was torn off of a house and numerous large tree limbs were blown down.  In Litchfield, several large trees were blown down as well as several power lines.

Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree blocking County Road 542 just southeast of Meta.

Large hail was reported at the intersection of State Highway V and State Highway T.

Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs in High Ridge.

Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees between Annapolis and Des Arc.  Some of the trees fell onto roadways blocking them. Also, one tree fell onto a house in Annapolis causing moderate damage.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs.
A large tree was blown over onto Illinois Route 3 just south of Chester.

Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree blocking part of U.S. Highway 67.

Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees, as well as tree limbs, north of Belle.  One tree fell onto a house causing moderate damage near the intersection of Highway 89 and Highway Y.  Another large tree fell onto Highway 89.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees between Bismarck and Park Hills.  A couple of homes sustained minor roof damage from fallen trees.

Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees in Dittmer near Highway 30.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees onto Amy Clark Road east of Hillsboro.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous tree limbs around town.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees as well as numerous tree limbs.
Large hail fell across Trenton. Some of the hail stones were up to tennis ball size.  Several cars had their windows broken out or cracked.
Large hail up to tennis ball size damaged shingles on numerous homes in Aviston.

A tornado touched down near I-64 on the north side of Okawville where it blew an eastbound tractor trailer to the southwest into the median.  The driver sustained minor injuries.  The tornado travelled east and damaged a barn and other outbuildings at a farm along Illinois Route 177 about a quarter of a mile west of Cord Road.  Roof panels were blown off, some large tree limbs blown down and several calf hutches blown about, some of which had calves in them.  At Cord Road and Illinois Route 177, tin roof panels were blown off of another barn.  About a quarter of a mile east of Cord Road, along Illinois Route 177, power lines were blown down, a small barn lost its roof and a mason block building was blown down.  The tornado continued to move almost due east along Illinois Route 177 where it damaged a home at the intersection of IL Route 177 and Phobe Road.  Roof shingles were blown off and several large tree branches were broken.  One branch went through the roof of the garage and another damaged a car in the driveway.  All of the damage so far was EF0.  Near the intersection of Illinois Route 177 and County Road 4, the tornado destroyed a small barn.  This damage was rated EF1 with a maximum wind speed of 100 mph.  The tornado then turned a bit to the southeast and quickly dissipated over open fields.  Overall, the path length was approximately 4 miles with a max path width of 100 yards.

Rear flank downdraft winds associated with a tornadic thunderstorm destroyed an empty grain bin on a farm on Canary Road, just south of I-64. Then the winds blew over an east bound tractor trailer on I-64 near where the interstate crosses over County Road 4.  The driver sustained minor injuries.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a couple of small trees and a few signs around town.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines along Illinois Route 3 in Sauget.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs and a couple of trees in Fairview Heights.

A line of severe thunderstorms moved through Bland.  Twelve buildings in town sustained some type of damage.  Most of the damage was minor, to shingles, siding and windows.  However, the post office sustained major damage with the roof lifted and shifted off to the north.  This caused the front wall, which was made up of windows to fall into the building.  A postal employee was briefly trapped in the building but she managed to get herself out.  She only sustained minor injuries.  Also, numerous trees, tree limbs and a few power lines were knocked down.  One home owner sustained minor injuries from flying glass.  Two vehicles had their windows broken from flying debris. Winds were estimated between 80 and 90 mph.
Thunderstorm winds snapped off several 1 to 2 foot diameter trees.

A line of severe thunderstorms moved through Owensville damaging 13 buildings.  The damage was minor, i.e. shingles and siding.  Also, a trailer and a garage sustained moderate damage.  Several large trees were blown over as well as numerous tree limbs and a couple of power lines.  No injuries were reported.
A line of severe thunderstorms moved through Rosebud.  One building sustained minor damage.  Several trees and numerous tree limbs were blown down.
A line of severe thunderstorms moved through Gerald.  Numerous large trees, tree limbs and a couple of power lines were blown down.
A line of severe thunderstorms moved across Warren County.  Numerous tree limbs and power lines were blown down.

A line of severe thunderstorms moved through Foristell and Wentzville.  Several trees and power lines were blown down.  Also, the goal posts at Progress Park on northeast side of Wentzville were blown over.
Several large tree limbs were blown down.
Several trees blown down near the intersection of Fee Fee Road and Olive Boulevard.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees in Bellefontaine Neighbors.
Thunderstorm winds damaged a machine shed and caused minor damage to a nearby house.  Also, several power lines and power poles were blown down.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a power pole and several power lines.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees around town.

Between one and three inches of rain fell over an extended amount of time onto partially frozen ground causing runoff.  Numerous creeks and rivers rose due to the runoff.  Several low water crossings were flooded.  On Highway V about a mile southeast of where it intersects with Highway F, there is a low water crossing over the Castor River.  The river rose and flooded the roadway.  A 59 year old man was a passenger in a truck with two other people.  The driver of the truck drove through the flooded roadway and the vehicle was swept off the road.  All three people got out of the truck. The two women were rescued, but the man was swept downstream and died.  His body was recovered the next day about 100 yards downstream.  Several other secondary roads and highways were flooded as well, including some streets in Fredericktown.

Between one and three inches of rain fell over an extended amount of time onto partially frozen ground causing runoff. Numerous creeks and rivers rose due to the runoff. Several low water crossings were flooded as well as Highway BB west of Vulcan and Highway 49 near Des Arc.

A father and his two young sons, as well as their 4 month old Labrador retriever, went on an approximately 16 mile round trip hike on the Ozark Trail in Mark Twain National Forest on January 12th.  They were heading south to Sutton���s Bluff.  The weather had been unusually warm with a high of 62 degrees recorded at the co-op station at Belleview 4SE on January 12th.  The family was dressed for the warmer weather so they were not prepared for a strong cold front moved that through during the day, bringing in much colder temperatures as well as heavy rain.  On their way back to their camp, they missed the turnoff to the Brushy Creek Lodge where they were staying and became lost further north along the trail. Other family members became concerned when they did not return and a search party was sent out to find them Saturday evening.  However, the search was called off a little after midnight.  The search resumed the next morning, just after daybreak.  By Sunday morning the temperature had dropped to 28 degrees at Belleview 4SE.  The search party found the father and boys about a mile north of the turnoff to the lodge.  The father, 36 years old, was pronounced dead at the scene.  The two boys, 10 and 8 years old, were pronounced dead several hours later at a local hospital.  The puppy survived.

Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines in St. Martins.  Further east in western portions of Jefferson City, thunderstorm winds uprooted a large tree at the intersection of U.S. Highway 50 and Business 50, blocking the roadway.  Also, several power poles in this area were blown down.
Thunderstorm winds blew down small metal shed in Holts Summit.  In New Bloomfield, a large tree was blown down.
Thunderstorm winds blew over a semi on Interstate 70 near mile marker 158. No information on if the driver was injured or not.
Thunderstorm winds snapped a couple of trees and caused considerable damage to a shed in Argyle.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree onto Highway RA.  Also, numerous tree limbs were blown down in the same area.

A tornado touched down south of Concord Hill Road and west of State Highway 47.  A concentrated area of tree damage was found approximately 165 yards south of Concord Hill Road across from an open field.  This tree damage was consistent with wind speeds near the low end of the EF-1 range.  Some loose siding was observed just west of State Highway 47 between Concord Hill Road and New Boston Lane.  Additional structural and tree damage was then found between New Boston Lane and Charette Creek Road northeast of State Highway 47.  This damage was consistent with wind speeds near the high end of the EF-0 range.  The roof of a small barn, both the west and east sides, were uplifted and carried between 80 and 90 yards northeast.  Material from the barn roof was lifted into the nearby trees.  A couple of supporting poles from the barn were also uplifted approximately 8 inches.  Several wooden 2x4s were found driven into the ground northeast of the barn.  These 2x4s were driven approximately 8 to 10 inches into the ground with varying angles of entry.  The tornado continued eastward where a two story residence was damaged.  A few sections of the fascia on this home were uplifted and the brick veneer had become partially detached from the front wall.  A large healthy cedar tree in the front of the residence was snapped near the ground and the tree was tossed to the northeast.  Additional EF-0 damage was found on the property.  The tornado lifted just east of this residence based on the lack of tree damage found to the east.

A tornado touched down along Sycamore Bend Road just southwest of Chain of Rocks.  A clear path of tree damage was found south of Sycamore Bend Road, where small branches were snapped from most of the trees within a path that was approximately 20 to 30 yards wide.  Some minor roof damage was also noted in this area.  The top of one pine tree was snapped off and the tree top was thrown to the northeast.  The tornado crossed Sycamore Bend Road and continued northeastward along Jordan Road.  A few tree trunks were snapped and several large branches were snapped among the trees along both sides of the road near the Jordan Branch Creek.  Minor roof damage was found to several residences along Jordan Road north of the creek.  The tornado lifted just south of Highway C.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted an 8 inch diameter tree on Townview Drive.  Also, several large tree limbs were blown down nearby.
Thunderstorm winds blew down three trees that were at least a foot in diameter as well as several power lines around town.

A tornado touched down just north of Illinois Route 16 between St. Marys Road and Washington School Road. As it travelled to the north northwest it caused some minor crop damage.  It then hit a residence and caused minor damage.  Several trees around the house were snapped off.  The tornado continued to the north northwest for a little bit more before lifting and dissipating.  The damage was rated EF-0.
A tornado briefly touched down in a field just northwest of Damiansville.  No damage or injuries were reported with this tornado.
Thunderstorm winds snapped off the tops of a couple of trees along Brighton Bunker Hill Road about halfway between Brighton and Bunker Hill.
Golfball sized hail fell at the Rivers Edge Restaurant.
Numerous trees blown down around town.
Several large trees and numerous tree limbs were blown down in Leasburg and Bourbon.
A phone line was blown down in Gasconade.

A microburst caused minor damage at Sullivan Regional Airport.  A small section of one hanger was removed with a door of a nearby hanger also sustaining damage.  Also, one private aircraft sustained minor damage.  The AWOS recorded a wind gust of 101 mph with this microburst. Further downstream the damage from the microburst was sporadic.  About a mile east southeast of the airport, south of I-44, the winds destroyed a vacant mobile home and caused considerable damage to 5 other mobile homes.  One of the mobile homes had a large tree land on it, but only caused minor roof damage.  No one was inside the destroyed mobile home at the time.  However, three residents of the trailer park were taken to the hospital with minor injuries and eight other people walked into the hospital to be treated for minor injuries as well.

A microburst caused damage at a farm stead about 3 miles east northeast of Bourbon.  A barn was totally destroyed by winds that were estimated around 100 mph.  A nearby garage was heavily damaged.  Four large trees were uprooted and the house sustained damage due to the winds and flying debris from the trees.
Another microburst caused significant tree damage in Meramec State Park.

A line of severe thunderstorms moved through the Union area.  Several large trees were blown down as well as numerous tree limbs.  A business on the north side of town had minor roof damage. A microburst occurred on the south side of town at the First Baptist Church.  The attached brick building had the majority of its metal roof peeled off with insulation thrown downwind toward the intersection of East Main Street and Highway 47.  Other small trees were observed to be snapped off in this area in addition to minor shingle damage to the roof of the church itself.  The estimated wind speed in this location was 70 mph.

A microburst started at the intersection of St. Johns Road and State Highway V and continued northeast to Wolf Hollow Golf Club, ending near Highway 100.  Significant tree damage was observed with many pine trees topped and/or snapped along with uprooted hardwood trees.  All of the damage pointed in the same northeast direction with wind speed estimated around 80 mph.

Two miles north of Villa Ridge, 18 power poles were snapped or lying on the ground along a three quarter of a mile stretch of Old Highway 100 between State Highway T and Mary Lane.  The damage was caused by a microburst.  The estimated wind speed at this location was 90 mph.

Thunderstorm winds caused minor roof damage to a motel on Highway 100 near intersection with Manor House Lane. Also, several large trees were blown down.  One large tree blocked Coleman Road just north of intersection with Highway 100.

A tornado touched down in the Labadie Bottoms, north of St. Albans and lifted after traversing, on a slightly curved path, for 1.5 miles east northeast across St. Albans Island.  Extensive tree damage was noted along the track. The overall damage was rated EF1.  The path length was 1.5 miles and the max damage width was 200 yards.
Thunderstorm winds snapped and/or twisted off numerous large trees against the bluff. The lower brush was laying in convergent pattern to northeast.
Thunderstorm winds blew some siding off of a house near the intersection of Interstate 70 and Bryan Road.
Thunderstorm winds snapped a power pole on the east outer road just north of Dauphine Drive in Lake St. Louis.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree branch and two large trees.
Thunderstorm winds peeled part of the siding off of two homes in New Town.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large trees and tree limbs in Homestead Estates.

Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees and tree limbs on Island Road north of intersection with Highway H.  Also, a number of power poles were blown down along Highway 94 between Portage Des Sioux and West Alton.  Highway 94 was shutdown for a time due to power poles and lines across the roadway.
Thunderstorm winds blew a mobile home off its foundation, on Highway 21 just south of intersection with Highway 47.  No injuries reported.

A weak tornado touched down near the intersection of 59th Street and Reber Place in the city of St. Louis.  It moved to the northeast across Dalton and January Avenues before lifting along Columbia Avenue.  Many trees were snapped and numerous homes and garages/sheds were damaged along the path of the tornado.  The most extensive damage occurred to several homes and a garage near and just east of the intersection of January Avenue and Columbia Avenue.  One house on Columbia Avenue lost the entire east facing side of the roof.  Pieces of the roof and insulation were scattered north and east along Columbia Avenue.  Several cars were badly damaged along Columbia Avenue due to the falling debris.  No injuries were reported.  The overall rating for the tornado was EF0.  The maximum path width was 50 yards and the path length was a quarter of a mile.

Thunderstorm winds partially uplifted a large spruce tree onto a house on Sublette Avenue just south of Columbia Avenue.  Also, a home on Columbia Avenue, just east of Sublette Avenue, had minor roof damage.
One inch hail fell at Westport Plaza.

The tornado began in Bridgeton on Pennridge Drive, just northeast of St. Charles Rock Road.  A skating rink in this location suffered EF-1 roof damage.  The tornado moved northeast causing sporadic EF-0 and EF-1 tree damage for about 3 miles crossing Highway 370 in the process. The tornado intensified to EF-2 strength in Hazelwood near Woodcrest Lane where the roof was torn off a home.  The tornado was also at its maximum width at this location reaching 500 yards wide.  Along Teson Road, north of Howdershell Road, 10 apartment buildings were damaged with 5 buildings losing portions of their roofs.  The tornado then turned a bit to the east and caused EF-2 damage at Lynn Haven Lane and Howdershell Road.  Two homes at this location lost most of their roofs. Also, across the street on the north side of Howdershell Road a strip mall had small portions of the roof removed, as well as glass windows and doors shattered.  Tree damage, EF-0 to EF-1 strength, occurred along Lamplight Lane, Coach Light Lane, Caposele Lane, and Gerardini Drive.  Several homes on these streets suffered roof damage from falling trees and large tree limbs.  The area from Lynn Haven Lane to Gerardini Drive had the highest concentration of damage.  As the tornado moved east northeast into Florissant sporadic EF-0 to EF-1 tree damage occurred to just east of St. Ferdinand Park along Beverly Drive.  Also, just south of St. Ferdinand Park, another strip mall at the intersection of Lindbergh Boulevard and St. Jean Street sustained minor roof damage. The tornado moved very fast, covering 6.75 miles in about 5 minutes.  Sporadic thunderstorm wind gust damage, mainly tress uprooted or large limbs downed, was noted north and south of the tornado track.  Several business signs were also damaged along Lindbergh Blvd. in Florissant.  Two people sustained minor injuries.  One had a broken leg and another just had some scrapes and bruises.  Almost 400 structures sustained some kind of damage.  Fifty five of these structures were either destroyed or sustained significant damage.  The tornado was rated EF-2 overall. The maximum path width was 500 yards and the path length was 6.75 miles.
Thunderstorm winds on the south side of the tornado blew down numerous large trees, tree limbs and power lines.  Some caused minor damage to homes and businesses in the area.
Thunderstorm winds on the north side of the tornado blew down numerous large trees, tree limbs and power lines.  Some caused minor damage to homes and businesses in the area.
Thunderstorm winds blew off part of the roof of Shenandoah Valley Elementary School.  Six class rooms sustained both wind and water damage.  School was not in session, so no injuries reported.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs around Wood River and snapped a power pole.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees and numerous tree limbs around Godfrey.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted a six foot tall spruce tree and knocked a few shingles off of a nearby house.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a couple of two foot diameter trees next to Illinois Route 159 about 1.5 miles south of intersection with Illinois Route 16.
Thunderstorm winds blew an anchored 10 foot by 10 10 foot metal shed approximately 300 feet.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree in town which knocked down some power lines.
Thunderstorm winds caused minor roof damage to a home on Witt Avenue just east of Illinois Route 127.
Thunderstorm winds blew over a couple of empty semi trailers at a business on Kimmel Lake Road just south of Highway O.  A couple of large tree limbs were blown down as well.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines onto Interstates 270 and 170 causing both highways to be closed at the interchange.
Large hail fell across Columbia with the largest stones as big as baseballs.

A tornado briefly touchdown in southwest Monroe County a mile north of the intersection of Highways M and C on Highway C. Six power poles were snapped at the base of the pole. Width of the damage in this location was 100 yards and damage was rated EF1.  Further northeast...the tornado briefly touched down on County Road 840 just east of intersection with County Road 819.  A barn was severely damaged. Debris from the barn was tossed to the east about 100 yards. The tornado continued to travel to the northeast...where it briefly touched down again...just south of Highway AA...just west of intersection with County Road 835. Two machine sheds in this location sustained minor to moderate damage.  Also...a large barn sustained significant damage where the south part of the barn was removed.  Damage width in this area was 70 yards wide. Damage was rated low end EF1. Further to the east...on Highway AA...just west of intersection with County Road 857...numerous large trees were snapped at the base and showed a convergent damage pattern. Width of damage in this area was over 60 yards wide and the damage was only on the north side of Highway AA. Damage in this location was rated low end EF1.  The tornado continued to travel to the northeast and briefly touched down one last time just west of Highway 15...two miles south of Paris, Missouri.  Three machine sheds sustained significant damage with debris being thrown 300 to 400 yards to the north northwest. Damage was rated EF1 in this location.  Overall the path length was 7.45 miles...with a max damage width of 70 yards. The tornado was rated EF1.

Another tornado, about half a mile south of the first tornado, briefly touched down on County Road  835, half a mile north of the intersection with County Road 840.  A barn sustained minor to moderate damage, where 2x4 missiles were driven into the roof of the barn.  Width of damage was 30 to 40 yards wide with a path length of less than a tenth of a mile.  The tornado was rated EF0.

Structural damage occurred at a farmstead southwest of the corner of Highways M and C.  A few large panels from a machine shed were tossed to the east northeast.  A few large trees were snapped near the base on the northeast corner of Highways M and C. This damage was caused by straight line winds around 75 mph.

A tornado briefly touched down on the south side of U.S. Highway 24, about 4 miles northeast of Stoutsville.  It snapped large tree branches about a third of the way up and other branches were snapped half way up.  Damage width in this area was about 60 yards wide.  As it traveled to the northeast, it took the metal panel roofing off of the north side of a medium size out building, before lifting and dissipating. Overall the path length was 0.45 miles with a max path width of 60 yards.  It was rated EF0.

Just south of Monroe City, along U.S. Highway 24, several power poles were snapped and tree damage was observed.  Cedar and oak trees were damaged.  On the far southwest portions of Monroe City, nine homes sustained roof damage where shingles were removed.  Also, several large tree limbs, between three and nine inches in diameter were blown down.  One large tree was blown down, crushing a medium sized storage shed.  In town, the roof of a retail store was removed and displaced approximately 80 yards to the east northeast.  Another nearby business sustained minor roof damage.  Also, 3 large storage sheds sustained minor roof damage.  Additional tree damage was observed on the east side of Monroe City in a residential area.

Two grain bins, located on Highway J just north of Hazard Lane, in far northwestern Ralls County, sustained minor damage.  The grain elevator sustained minor damage as well.  There was minor tree limb damage that extended for about a mile south of the grain bins.
Thunderstorm winds blew a wooden swing set approximately 100 yards.
Thunderstorm winds blew over three semis on U.S. Highway 36, about 5 miles west of Hannibal.  No injuries were reported.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs north of Palmyra.

Thunderstorms winds caused a wide swath of damage extending from downtown Quincy near the Mississippi River eastward to Quincy Regional Airport.  Numerous power lines and tree limbs as well several trees were blown down around town.  One building had a portion of a wall peeled off at the intersection of Broadway and 48th Street.  A bank at the intersection of Koch's Lane and 24th Street had minor roof damage.  An 18 foot long construction trailer was blown south through the front wall of a Staples store on Broadway Street across from the mall.  A restaurant near the airport sustained moderate damage.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines in Golden.
Thunderstorm winds blew off part of the roof of a large shed on the southwest side of Kingston.
