The tornado then crossed Ivy Road and took off a side section of an old barn before lifting and dissipating on the south side of Bluff Road.  The tornado was rated EF0.  It was on the ground for a third of a mile with a max path width of 40 yards.

A tornado touched down just north of Lohrberg Drive and broke several large tree limbs.  The tornado continued to the northeast and crossed Ames Road.  More tree damage occurred on the east side of Ames Road just north of intersection with Lohrberg Drive before lifting and dissipating.  The tornado was rated EF0.  It was on the ground for a third of a mile with a max path width of 30 yards.

The tornado first touched down just south of Owl Branch Road west of the intersection with Cherry Lane.  Several large tree branches were snapped off in this location and several tree tops were broken.  The tornado travelled to the southeast.  On the west side of Cherry Lane, a wall of a garage on the north side of the home was pushed in about 6 inches and some shingles were removed.  Also, several large tree limbs were snapped off.  The tornado crossed Cherry Lane and damaged a few more trees before lifting and dissipating.  The tornado was rated EF0.  It was on the ground for 1.44 miles and the max path width was 30 yards.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs.

Up to five inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Highway P had two to three feet of water flowing over it.  Two unoccupied cars were submerged up to their windows on Fawn Oaks Drive near Fawn Ridge Drive.

Up to five inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Illinois Route 4 just south of Carlinville.  A vehicle was submerged on West County Lane Road near Quail Lane.  The person was rescued but sustained no injuries.

Up to 4 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  The town of Hillview became isolated as all the roads travelling into town were impassable due to flooding from Hurricane Creek.  A number of homes in town had water in them.
Thunderstorm winds blew down about 20 power poles along U.S. 40 between Illinois Route 162 and Triad Middle School.  Also, several power poles were blown down in St. Jacob.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous 4 to 6 inch diameter tree limbs in Payson.
Thunderstorm winds split a large tree with parts of it blocking the nearby road in Barry.
Thunderstorm winds snapped two power poles along County Road 230 and an aluminum shed was blown over.
Thunderstorm winds produced scattered tree damage with one metal light pole snapped at its base.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees, large tree branches and blew off part of a roof on a building.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees and power lines around town.
Thunderstorm winds destroyed two mall sheds and blew over a horse trailer.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree as well as large tree limbs in Godfrey.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs and power lines around town.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree onto a power line.  Also, numerous large tree limbs were blown down around town.

There were numerous reports of large hail across southern St. Louis County.  The largest hailstones were two inches in diameter which was reported in Affton.  There were reports of quarter to golfball sized hail in Shrewsbury and Lemay.
There were numerous reports of large hail across the southern portions of the City of St. Louis.

Within 20 minutes of the first storm a second severe thunderstorm moved through far southern portions of St. Louis County.  There were numerous reports of quart to golfball sized hail. Some of the towns affected were Mehlville and Oakville.
Lots of quarter sized hail was reported over Mascoutah.
Large hail fell over the Cedar Hill area.
A swath of large hail fell between House Springs and just northwest of Imperial.

Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs between Bethel and Shelbyville.  Also, a large tree was blown across a gravel road 3 miles southwest of Bethel.  Some shingles were blown off of a house 5 miles north of Bethel.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs and power lines across far southern Knox County.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs and power lines in La Belle.

A line of severe thunderstorms moved through Columbia and tracked southeast through rest of county.  A 67 mph wind gust was measured at University of Missouri Jefferson Farm and Gardens just southeast of town on East New Haven Road.  Also, the ASOS at Columbia Regional Airport measured a 58 mph wind gust.  Numerous trees, power lines and tree limbs were blown down, especially on the southern sections of Columbia.  A couple of the fallen trees blocked roads in the area.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs as well as a stop sign at the intersection of U.S. Highway 61 and Highway HH.
Thunderstorm winds blew in several windows on businesses downtown as well as blowing down a traffic light.

Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees, numerous tree limbs and power lines around town.  Seven power poles along U.S. Highway 54 were blown over knocking power out to several businesses in the area.  One tree limb fell onto an unoccupied car causing minor damage and another limb fell onto a house causing minor roof and siding damage.  Some of the fallen limbs and power lines briefly blocked roadways. No injuries were reported with this storm.
As a line of thunderstorms moved across Callaway County, thunderstorm winds blew down numerous tree limbs and power lines across the county.

Thunderstorm winds blew several large trees and numerous large tree limbs and power lines across northern Cole County.  In Wardsville, two thirds of the gymnasium roof was damaged at Blair Oaks High School.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees, numerous tree limbs and power lines.  One tree was blown down across Highway 161 near intersection with Highway V.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines.  Also, a shed was destroyed in town.  One building in town sustained moderate roof damage.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous power lines between Center and New London.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a tree blocking Route A in Bonnots Mill. Also, a tree was blown over onto a house in town causing moderate damage.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several power lines in Meta.
Thunderstorm winds blew over several mail boxes in Linn.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree blocking West North Street in Mt. Sterling.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees along Route Y southwest of Bowling Green.  Also, several trees were blown down around Bowling Green.
Thunderstorm winds blew over a large tree onto Highway J just southwest of intersection with Highway 100.
Thunderstorm winds blew over a large tree onto Highway A near intersection with Pin Oak Church Road.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous trees across Pittsfield. Also, a large tree was blown down across Illinois Route 107 just north of Interstate 72.

Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree onto a house in Troy causing moderate damage.  Several trees were blown down about two miles southwest of Moscow Mills on Highway U.  A couple of fences were destroyed in this area as well.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous trees in Elsberry.  One large tree fell onto two unoccupied vehicles and a house.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous trees and tree limbs in Wentzville and Lake St. Louis.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs in Chesterfield and Olivette.
Thunderstorm winds pushed over several power poles in Tipton.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs.
Up to 5 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  U.S. Highway 24 just west of Stoutsville had a foot of water over it at the Otter Creek bridge.

Up to 5 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Some county roads were washed out around Lewistown.  Some culverts were popped out of the ground due to the heavy runoff.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs around town.  A couple of the limbs pulled down some power lines.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees and power lines around town and along Highway AT between U.S. Highway 50 and Highway 100.  Some shingles were blown off of houses as well.
Thunderstorms blew down a medium sized tree briefly blocking a roadway.
Thunderstorm winds blew a large tree limb down and blew an empty grain bin across a yard and onto a road.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree onto a power line.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs.
Thunderstorm winds damaged a couple of windows on the Forest Park campus of St. Louis Community College.

Storms moved through the St. Louis metro area.  A cyclist traveling along Maryland Heights Expressway, Highway 141, was struck in the head by a bolt of lightning.  He went into cardiac arrest.  Numerous motorists and paramedics stopped to assist him and were able to revive him, but he was in critical condition.  The 51 year old man has since recovered and was back to work after a month off.  He has hearing loss due to a perforated ear drum, which is where the lightning struck him.

Lightning struck a church in Hoyleton, Illinois at approximately midnight.  The fire smoldered in the rafters for several hours before erupting into flames.  The fire department was not called til around 2 am.  Most of the damage was confined to the attic and bell tower, rest of the building sustained major water damage.  No one was in building at the time and no injuries were reported.  The building is considered a total loss.

Lightning struck a home on Woodmere Trail Court around 802 pm on June 21st.  It smoldered for several hours. It became fully engulfed in flames by 2 am and that is when it was noticed by neighbors and they called 911.  The family that lives there was out of town for the weekend.  So no injuries reported.  The house was destroyed and damage was estimated around $487,000.

Up to six inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including Sinclair Road south of Nifong Blvd. West, Highway WW at Old Hawthorne Road, and Highway ZZ.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees. One tree fell onto a barn and another onto a home causing moderate damage.
Thunderstorm winds were estimated around 70 mph in Valley Park.

A tornado touched down on John McKeever Road just north of intersection with Autumn Leaf Drive. It caused tree damage in this area. The tornado traveled to the southeast, crossing Byrnesville Road then crossed the Big River about two miles west of Highway W. It caused considerable damage to a business on the north side of the intersection of State Highway 30 and Highway W.  A quarter of the roof was torn off and the deck was uplifted.  The air conditioning units were moved as well.  From here the tornado turned to the northeast, south and east of State Highway 30.  Sporadic tree damage was observed before the tornado lifted and dissipated on Elizabeth Drive just north of intersection with Victoria Drive.
Up to six inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads had water over them including U.S. Highway 54 just south of Kingdom City.
Up to five inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded including part of Highway 19 in New Florence.
Up to six inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Highway J southwest of Troy was closed due to running water from Big Creek.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs on the southeast side of town.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees.  One tree fell onto a mobile home causing moderate damage.  No injuries were reported.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a couple of small trees.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a couple of trees near the intersection of Hawthorne Blvd and Milton Blvd.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several tree limbs just north of Caledonia onto Highway 21.
Thunderstorm winds snapped off several trees near Highway D and Sneak Road.

A tornado touched down on Pasture Ridge Drive causing minor roof, siding and fence damage to a couple of houses.  As the tornado traveled to the northeast it snapped off numerous tree limbs and uprooted a couple of trees along the path.  It crossed Jungermann Road just south of intersection with Briarwick Trail and continued to the northeast.  The tornado lifted and dissipated near Peach Street just north of intersection with Nugget Drive.  No injuries were reported.

Up to seven inches of rain fell causing flash flooding. Numerous roads were flooded including roads in Hurdland and Edina.  Also, Route V north of Knox City, Highway K near Colony, Highway 151 at Highway 156, and Highway 11 west of Baring were flooded.

A downburst blew down a section of corn in a field and broke large tree limbs in a half mile long path.  The width of the damage was initially 50 yards wide then spread out to about 100 yards wide along the damage path.

Up to eight inches of rain fell causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads throughout the county were flooded.  Some highways flooded were Highway E off of Highway 81, U.S. Highway 61 north of Canton, Highway 16 east of Monticello, and Highway D south of La Belle.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large telephone pole in Breese.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree onto a house causing moderate roof and wall damage.  No injuries were reported.
An 18-year old male was killed by a lighting strike while retrieving a book from a pick-up truck.
Lightning struck a historic church built in the 1880s and caught fire.  It was a total loss.
Thunderstorm wind blew down several large tree limbs around town.
Thunderstorm winds blew down three power poles on Illinois Route 111.

Up to seven inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Several roads were flooded in the area. Also, there were numerous ditches overflowing and several creeks were out of their banks.
Between 5 and 6 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads throughout the county were flooded.
Between 5 and 6 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Numerous roads were flooded throughout the county.

Between 5 and 6 inches of rain fell causing flash flooding. Several consignment shops on the far north side of Troy had up to 4 inches of water in them as water overwhelmed a drainage ditch and flooded the parking lot and shops.  Two shops sustained minor water damage.  Also, numerous roads were flooded.
The St. Louis County Health Dept. reported 5 heat related injuries.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a couple of small trees on Dittmer Ridge Road.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted a couple of trees and snapped a few others as storms moved through the region.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a couple of trees in Mehlville.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a couple of trees and a billboard in town.
The St. Louis County Health Department reported 56 heat related injuries during the heat wave.
Thunderstorm winds caused damage to the bleachers and backstop at South Shelby High School.
The St. Louis County Health Department reported 2 heat related injuries.

A tornado touched down near the far western extension of St. Patricks Road. In this location, a barn had one of it's walls blown out and part of the roof torn off. Several other buildings in the area sustained minor to moderate roof damage. Then the tornado tracked to the north northeast, crossing Illinois Route 155 west of Ruma, about a tenth of a mile west of intersection with Pioneer Lane.  Just north of Illinois Route 155, two large trees were snapped off.  One tree landed on a nearby house causing minor roof damage. The tornado then lifted and dissipated.

A tornado touched down around a quarter of a mile southwest of the Illinois Route 13/15 and Jefferson Road intersection, where it uprooted or snapped off several large trees.  It traveled to the north northeast and crossed Illinois Route 13/15, moving through the Maple Hills Subdivision. In this area it caused minor to moderate roof damage to several homes.  It then moved into the Orchards Golf Club where it caused minor damage to a couple of homes and either uprooted or snapped off several large trees.  The tornado then lifted and dissipated on the northern end of the golf club.

A tornado touched down one tenth of a mile northwest of the intersection of Illinois Route 161 and Ruth School House Road.  It moved almost due north striking a farm, destroying a couple of outbuildings before lifting and dissipating.

The tornado crossed the Jefferson/Marion County line from WFO Paducah's county warning area into WFO St. Louis's CWA (Walnut Hill Road) about two tenths of a mile west of the intersection of Walnut Hill Road and North Tulip Lane. In this area several large trees were blown over. The tornado continued to move north northeast. It caused moderate roof damage to an outbuilding and destroyed a carport on Kell Road, about seven tenths of a mile east of Kell.  The tornado then lifted and dissipated. The path length in Marion County was 1.05 miles with a max path width of 75 yards. This section of the tornado was rated EF1.  Overall, the path length was 3.5 miles with a max path width of 100 yards and was rated EF1.
