A line of severe storms moved through Reynolds County. There were numerous reports of trees and power lines blown down, especially between  Centerville and the county line with Iron County.

Betwen 2 and 4 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding across parts of Warren County. MODOT closed Route A where it goes over Camp Creek due to the creek rising well out of it's banks flooding the roadway. Several other secondary roads were flooded as well.

Betwen 2 and 4 inches of rain, with isolated amounts up to 6 inches, fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding across Osage County. Numerous roads were flooded including Highways E, W, and 133.
Up to 6 inches of snow fell across Osage County. Numerous roads were snow covered and slick.

Three to four inches of rain fell over Osage county over a short period of time on already saturated soils.  Numerous roads were closed due to flooding including County Roads 508 and 542 near Meta, Highway W northwest of Linn, and Highway P west of Koeltztown.

A wide swath of large hail between an inch and 1.5 inches in diameter fell along the I-70 corridor in St. Charles County.  Large hail was reported in Flint Hill, Wentzville, Saint Paul, O'Fallon, St. Peters and St. Charles.

A wide swath of large hail between an inch and 1.25 inches in diameter fell along the I-270 corridor in northern portions of St. Louis County.  Large hail was reported in Florrisant, Black Jack and Spanish Lake.

A wide swath of large hail between an inch and 1.50 inches in diameter fell along the I-270/I-70 corridor in central portions of Madison County.  Large hail was reported in Wood River, Roxana, Poag, Edwardsville, Glen Carbon, and Highland.

A wide swath of large hail fell between St. Martins and Jefferson City. The largest hail stones were 3 inches in diameter.  There were numerous reports of dents on vehicles and car windows broken out.  At least 800 hundred cars sustained damage at car dealerships in the Jefferson City area. The largest hail stones were reported in St. Martins, Elston, and Jefferson City.

A wide swath of large hail fell across southern portions of Callaway County. Hail up to the size of baseballs was reported in Holts Summit and the Lake Mykee areas. There were reports of damage to several vehicles including broken windshields.
Large hail up to baseball size was reported in far northern portions of Osage County in the Chamois area.
Large hail up to baseball size was reported in southern portions of Montgomery County, including in the Big Spring area.
Large hail up to baseball size was reported in Warren County along the I-70 corridor. The large hail was reported in Warrenton and Wrights City.
Large hail up to 2.5 inches in diameter was reported in southern portions of Lincoln County. The large hail was reported in near Troy, Moscow Mills, Old Monroe, and Winfield.

Thunderstorm winds blew a section of shingles off of a house just northwest of Mokane.
Thunderstorm winds blew off a large section of shingles from a garage about 3 miles southeast of Gerald. Also, a large machine shed was blown down two miles east of Beaufort.

Also, numerous tree limbs and several power lines were blown down in this area. A couple of cars sustained damage from flying debris and falling trees. No injuries were reported.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted a large tree near Scott Air Force Base.  About a mile south southeast of Mascoutah, a small tree was blown down as well as a power pole.

Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees and blew an awning off of a residence just north of U.S. Highway 61.
Thunderstorm winds caused minor roof damage to a residence about 2 miles northeast of Roodhouse.

Wind equipment at the Cuba EOC recorded a 58 mph wind gust as a line of severe storms moved through town. Also, a small shed was blown into a street and numerous small tree limbs were blown down around town.

Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time over portions of southern Jefferson County. Joachim Creek rose above it's banks in and around Victoria, flooding several secondary roads as well as Highway P.

Up to 3 inches of rain fell in about a two hour period over portions of Ralls County causing flash flooding. Highway F, just north of intersection with Highway C, was flooded where it crosses over Spencer Creek. Also, Highway 19 between Perry and Center was closed due to flooding.

A short-lived tornado was observed by several individuals from a distance. There were no reports of damage observed. The time and location was estimated from the reports and radar.
Up to 3 inches of rain fell in about an hour and a half causing flash flooding. Several secondary roads near Olney were flooded.
Up to three inches of rain fell in about an hour causing flash flooding, including on Illinois Route 106 between Hull and Kinderhook.

Based on multiple images and videos provided by several parties, a landspout tornado formed at approximately 2250 UTC and tracked along the I-55 corridor. The starting and ending points are estimated and based on information received.

Three to four inches of rain fell over Gasconade county over a short period of time on already saturated soils.  Numerous roads were closed due to flooding including the intersection of Highways B and C south of Bland, Piezuck Road and Highway 19 on the north side of Owensville, Kings Highway in Mount Sterling, as well as Moore Road and Highway 19 in Bay.  Water was flowing over U.S. Highway 50 east of Mount Sterling, but it was not closed.

Up to three inches of rain fell over Franklin county over a short period of time on already saturated soils.  Numerous roads were closed due to flooding including Beemont Road, Beemont School Road, Detmold Road, Hoeman Road, and Highway C about a mile north of U.S. Highway 50.

Up to three inches of rain fell over a short amount of time on already saturated soils in St. Charles county. Numerous roads were closed due to flooding including the intersection of T.R. Hughes and Highway 79, Highway T one mile south of Foristell near Peruque Creek, and Highway N between Highway K and Weise Road.

Up to three inches of rain fell over a short amount of time on already saturated soils in Crawford county.  Numerous roads were closed due to flooding including Highway 19 south of Cuba, Highway C west of Bourbon and Highway N southeast of Bourbon near Blue Springs Creek.

Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time over already saturated soils in Warren county.  Numerous secondary roads were closed due to flooding including Highway TT half a mile northeast of Dutzow.

Up to two inches of rain fell over a short amount of time over already saturated soils in northwestern Washington county. Water was over Primrose Road northeast of Venedy and Elkhorn Creek was out of its banks in this area.

Up to two inches of rain fell over a short amount of time on already saturated soils in southwestern Marion county. Several county roads between Centralia and Salem had several inches of water over them and a few secondary roads were closed in the area.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees and numerous tree limbs in Maeystown and areas just to the northeast of town. A couple of sheds sustained minor damage.

A weak tornado initially touched down a quarter of a mile northwest of the intersection of Levee Road and Berger Road in the flood plain.  Three witnesses saw the tornado move east across an open field.  The tornado did damage a garage about a quarter of a mile northwest of the intersection of Berger Road and B Road.  Some large tree limbs were also down at this location.  About a quarter mile east of the garage, a barn sustained minor damage before the tornado lifted and dissipated.

Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time over northern Boone county on March 17th.  Several secondary roads were flooded including Highway CC at the intersection with Tri City Road, just west of Centralia.

Two to three inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils in Crawford county from the evening hours of March 17th through March 18th. Numerous roads were flooded including Highway 19 southeast of Steelville.

Two to three inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils in Washington county from the evening hours of March 17th through March 18th. Numerous roads and low water crossings were flooded including streets in Potosi, Highway 47 at Kingston Road northwest of Cruise Mill, and New Diggins Road in Springtown.

Two to three inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils in St. Francois county from the evening hours of March 17th through March 18th. Numerous low water crossings in the northern portions of the county were flooded.
Two to three inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils in Ste. Genevieve county from the evening hours of March 17th through March 18th. Numerous low water crossings were flooded.

Two to three inches of rain fell onto already saturated soils in St. Clair county from the evening hours of March 17th through March 18th. Several roads had water flowing over them including Jefferson Road between Illinois Routes 13/15 and Illinois Route 4.

Very heavy rain fell over Reynolds county beginning late on the 17th of March and throughout the day on the 18th. The co-operative observer in Ellington reported a storm total of 9.7 inches. Four inches of rain fell in Ellington through 8 am on the 18th, then another 2 inches fell between 8 am and 11 am on the 18th, with an additional 3.7 inches in the hours after that. This caused the creeks in the area to rise rapidly including Logan Creek which flows through the middle of Ellington.  The creek began to rise rapidly around 7 am, rising nearly 10 feet by noon. Around 8 am, an 81 year old man was trying to clear some flood debris from a bridge that goes over the creek next to his business and was possibly knocked into the flood waters by a camper trailer that had been washed away from its location.  He was pronounced dead at 830 am.  A number of homes and businesses were flooded in town and several propane tanks were floating in the flood waters. Numerous roads throughout Reynolds county were flooded due to the heavy rains.

Up to 6 inches of rain fell on already saturated soils in Iron county from the late evening hours of March 17th through March 18th.  Numerous roads were covered with water countywide.  Also, 8 to 10 homes in Des Arc were flooded and the bridge north of town on Highway 143 was washed out.  In the Ironton/Arcadia area, Knob Creek and Stouts Creek were out of their banks and overtopping the bridge that goes over them.  Highway D, Highway 21 were impassable in spots and Highway 49 about half a mile south of Highway 72 was flooded.

Up to 4 inches of rain fell in a 3 hour period which caused flash flooding. Highway 141 at the intersection with I-44 was flooded in both the north and south bound lanes. Also, several creeks, including Yarnell and Williams creeks, rose above flood stage causing a number of road closures in the immediate area.
Several dozen power lines were blown down around town.

Up to 4.5 inches of rain fell in a 2 to 3 hour period, causing flash flooding in Quincy. Water levels in some areas was between 3 and 4 feet deep which caused a number of roads to be washed out. Blessing Hospital sustained minor flood damage when water flooded parts of the basement and first floor. Also, numerous basements in other buildings were flooded. Five water rescues were performed after vehicles became trapped in flood waters. No injuries were reported.
Up to 4 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding. Numerous roads in the Farmersville and Waggoner areas. Macoupin Creek is out of its banks in Farmersville.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs on Highway U near intersection with Highway J.

Up to five inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding. Highway N about a mile west of intersection with I-64 was briefly flooded.  Also, water was over Mexico Road about a half mile south of intersection with Highway P.

A brief, weak tornado touched down in the early evening just to the northwest of Cuba, Missouri. The tornado first touched down to the west of Indian Lake, along Lakeshore Drive. The tornado did some minor damage to a roof on the west side of Lakeshore Drive. The worst of the damage occurred to two residences on the east side of Lakeshore Drive, on the west side of Indian Lake. A few trees were uprooted or snapped, and a home lost the majority of its roof. Additionally, a boat dock was completely flipped over. The tornado moved east across the lake, snapping a few other trees and doing some minor roof damage to a home along Indian Hills Drive. The tornado quickly lifted just before it hit Seminole Road. Additional tree damage and some minor house damage (a few shingles and siding peeled off) was noted along DD Highway well to the south and east of the damage near the lake. This damage was deemed to be straight line wind damage, caused by a surge in the rear flank downdraft of the thunderstorm. Overall the tornado was rated EF0 with a path length of 0.76 miles. The max path width was 100 yards. No deaths or injuries were reported with the tornado.

A tornado rapidly developed near Hillsboro Road to the east of Park Hills, Missouri. This tornado initially caused sporadic tree damage to a grove of trees west of Hillsboro Road. As it approached Hillsboro Road, the tornado widened and became a bit stronger, causing EF-1 damage to a home by collapsing its southward facing exterior wall. Minor roof damage also occurred to another home, along with several trees that were snapped. The tornado then crossed Hillsboro Road and did some minor roof damage to an outbuilding on the east side of the roadway. The tornado lifted as it approached a large grove of trees on the eastern side of Hillsboro Road. Overall, the tornado was rated EF1 with a path length of 0.74 miles. The max path width was 125 yards. No deaths or injuries were reported.

Tree damage and some minor house damage (a few shingles and siding peeled off) was noted along DD Highway well to the south and east of the tornado damage near Indian Lake. This damage was deemed to be straight line wind damage, caused by a surge in the rear flank downdraft of the thunderstorm.

Up to seven inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding, especially on the south side of Quincy. There were two water rescues. One motorist was stranded on top of their vehicle roof in the 1300 block of Seminary Road. Also, another motorist was stranded in her vehicle at 33rd and Broadway. Otherwise, a number of other streets were flooded and Curtis Creek was well out of its banks.
Up to seven inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding. Several roads were flooded including County Road 775 S about 2 miles south southeast of Mount Sterling.
Thunderstorm winds snapped off a large tree limb and flipped over a large play set.

Up to 4 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Lakeshore Drive around Indian Lake was impassable which cutoff access to parts of the community. Numerous other roads in the area were flooded as well.

Up to three inches of rain caused flash flooding in and around the Spalding area. Water two to three feet deep was over Highway M about 3.5 miles west of U.S. Highway 61. Also, a vehicle was stuck in water up to 18 inches deep on Highway H just south of intersection with Highway A.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs onto the MetroLink tracks near the Fairview Heights station and onto Highway 15 near the Lady of the Snows Shrine.

Two spotters reported a tornado briefly touched down in a field verified with a picture.  This tornado touched down northeast of Hettick, IL, southwest of Otter Lake.  The tornado was very short lived and did not damage any rating indicators, thus it will be labeled an EF-unknown.

A combination of a ground survey and satellite data shows an intermittent tornado path. The tornado touched down just south of Prange Avenue. It snapped and uprooted some trees near a residence on Prange Avenue. Satellite data shows the tornado continued northeast through cornfields, damaging more trees near Sewing and Mt. Olive Trails. Satellite data shows the tornado continued northeast, before lifting just west of Niemanville Trail. The tornado was rated as EF0 with a path length of 3.2 miles and max path width of 75 yards.

A combination of a ground survey and satellite data suggests a brief, weak tornado touched down northeast of Walshville, IL. The tornado first touched down in a corn field west of Durbin Road. The tornado then continued northeast, mainly causing tree damage, though some minor structural damage to a house west of Durbin Road also occurred. The tornado quickly lifted as it approached Durbin Road. The tornado was rated as EF0 with a path length of 0.57 miles and max path width of 50 yards.

A tornado developed about 3 miles north-northwest of Farmersville, Illinois, near the intersection of Rovey Lane and East 1st Road. A few storm chasers captured video of the tornado as it moved northeast and then north toward the Montgomery and Sangamon County line. On video the tornado appeared to be multivortex and violent, yet damage in the St. Louis county warning area was limited to a few broken tree branches, flattened corn and the partial destruction of a small outbuilding. Therefore, it was rated as an EF-0 in Montgomery County with a path length of 3.89 miles and a max path width of 300 yards. The tornado continued north into Sangamon County (WFO Central IL CWA) before lifting and dissipating about 2.4 miles south of Divernon. Overall, the tornado was rated EF0 with a total path length of 4.24 miles and a max path width of 300 yards. No deaths or injuries were reported.

Thunderstorm winds caused widespread tree, tree limb and power line damage between Lake St. Louis, Dardenne Prairie and St. Peters. A couple of trees fell across a roadway about 4 miles south of Dardenne Prairie. Several power lines were knocked down at the intersection of Sommers Road and Highway N. Also, an 8 inch diameter tree limb fell onto a house in St. Peters causing minor roof and gutter damage.

Thunderstorm winds caused widespread wind damage across the northern portions of St. Louis County. In Chesterfield, power lines were knocked down across the west bound lanes of I-64 near Boones Crossing exit. In Woodson Terrace, a gas station canopy was blown over onto an occupied vehicle at the intersection of Guthrie Avenue and Woodson Road. The driver and her daughter were uninjured. The vehicle sustained only minor damage. Otherwise, numerous trees and tree limbs were blown down including in Ballwin, Maryland Heights and Dellwood.

Widespread wind damage occurred across portions of Madison County. In Alton, several large trees were blown down and two homes sustained moderate roof damage from the fallen trees. One unoccupied car suffered major damage from a fallen tree. Also, numerous tree limbs and trees were blown down in Roxana, Wood River, Granite City and Edwardsville.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a tree across Abbey Lane.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree in town.

Widespread thunderstorm wind damage occurred from Belleville eastward through Mascoutah. In Belleville, multiple trees were blown down as well as power lines. Also, a couple of buildings sustained minor roof damage. In Mascoutah, multiple trees and tree limbs were blown down throughout town. Also, a tree split with one portion falling onto a house and the tornado siren on top of city hall tipped over.
Thunderstorm winds blew down multiple utility poles along Hamacher Street.

Thunderstorm winds blew down several power poles along Knab Road. Also, a nearby machine shed was destroyed and another one sustained moderate damage. A number of trees and tree limbs were blown as well.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees between Butler and Hillsboro. Some of the trees fell onto road ways briefly blocking them.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a tree onto Terrapin Ridge Road.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees in New Baden. One of the trees fell onto a power line knocking it down. In Breese, a large tree limb brought down a power line.
A line of severe storms blew down several large trees. Also, several power lines were blown down in Vandalia.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees just south of Eden.
Thunderstorm wind blew down several trees in town.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree near Stadium and Southwest Boulevard. Also, numerous tree limbs and several small to medium trees were blown down around town.

Up to six inches of rain fell in a about a two hour period causing flash flooding. Numerous roads were closed including U.S. Highway 50. Apartments were flooded near the intersection of McCarty Street and East High Street and ones located on nearby Christopher Place due to Gray's Creek rising well out of its banks. This forced the residents to evacuate both complexes. Nine water rescues were performed in Jefferson City after vehicles were driven into the flood waters and stalled.  Area around U.S. Highway 50 and Missouri Blvd., as well as The Millbottom Area, were flooded when Wears Creek rose well above its banks. Also, Wears Creek flooding affected the Washington Park and Vivion Field areas. No injuries were reported.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a 4 foot diameter tree as well as nearby power lines.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees around town.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large road signs.

Emergency management relayed a report of a brief tornado just northeast of intersection of Black Diamond Trail and North 35th Avenue. The tornado occurred over a field, resulting in no observed damage. The tornado was rated EFU (Unknown) with a path length 0.2 miles and max path width of 10 yards.
Thunderstorm winds blew down two large tree limbs at intersection of Oregon Trail Drive and Woodstream Drive.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees around town. One tree fell onto a house and caused moderate damage.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree limb about 2 miles north of Woody, damaging a deck on a house. In Carrollton, several trees, as well as power lines, were blown down around town.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees in Modesto and Virden. Near Modesto a couple of sheds were damaged.
Thunderstorm winds snapped off a large tree limb.
Thunderstorm winds blew down multiple trees, tree limbs and power lines in Park Hills and Elvins.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees, tree limbs and power lines on the west side of town. Also, a building had a portion of its roof blown off.
Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding. Numerous roads were flooded including portions of Highway 47 between Troy and Hawk Point.
Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding. Several roads were flooded including Aubochon Road. Two vehicles were stranded but the drivers were uninjured.

Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding. Numerous roads were flooded across the southern portions of Cole County, including over the western portions of Brazito.
Up to 6 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding. Several roads were flooded including Highway 100 near Gasconade.

Up to 7 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing widespread flash flooding in northeastern Gasconade County. Numerous roads were flooded including Highway 19 and roads throughout Hermann.  Also, Frene Creek near the Adam Putcha Winery was well out of its banks with at least 3 to 4 feet of water flowing over Frene Creek Road just south of the intersection with Highway 100.
Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding. Baileys Creek was out of its banks about 3 miles southwest of Morrison, flooding sections of County Road 275.
Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding. Several roads were flooded including Highway 94 near Rhineland.

Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding across the southern portions of Warren County. In Treloar, several roads were flooded as well as a couple of basements. Also, Highway N was closed due to high water and several roads in the Concord Hill area were flooded.

Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding. Several roads were flooded around the Ellington area including Highway F leading up to the bridge that crosses Logan Creek, just north of intersection with Highway 106.

Up to four inches of rain fell in about a two and a half hour time period causing flash flooding. Several roads were flooded in and around the Wright City area, including the intersection of State Highways M and H. One road, Roelker Road south of intersection with Appaloosa Way, was completely washed out from the flash flood. Also, Edgewater Circle was flooded in several locations and sustained minor damage.

Up to 6 inches of rain fell in about a three hour period causing flash flooding, especially across the far southern portions of the county. Numerous roads were flooded in this area including the intersection of Highway 79 and Highway C.

Up to 7 inches of rain fell in about a four hour period causing widespread flash flooding. Numerous roads were flooded across the county, including Highway 79 at Vomund Road, Winghaven Blvd and Highway N, and Belleau Creek Road just south of intersection with Veterans Memorial Parkway.  At least 5 motorists drove into the flood waters across the county, became stuck and had to be rescued.  Also, the first floor of a two story apartment building on Riverview Lane (just north of the intersection with Highway 94) in St. Charles, MO was flooded with several feet of water.  Residents from 12 of the units had to be evacuated from the apartment building. Several basements were flooded and at least one home near Belleau Creek had several feet of water in it. No injuries or deaths were reported.

Up to 7 inches of rain fell in about a four hour period causing flash flooding, especially across the northern half of the county. Numerous roads were flooded and at least 13 water rescues were performed after vehicles were driven into flood waters. One of the rescues involved two vehicles that were swept away as a creek had risen well out of its banks near the intersection of Conway and White Roads. Three total occupants were rescued. No injuries or deaths were reported.

Up to 6 inches of rain fell in about a three hour period causing flash flooding. Several roads were flooded including some in the Collinsville and Glen Carbon areas. The intersection of Illinois Routes 162 and 157 was flooded.

Up to 5 inches of rain fell in about a three hour period causing flash flooding. Numerous roads were flooded including Illinois Route 177 just west of Mascoutah and Illinois Route 158 south of Scott Air Force Base between Illinois Routes 161 and 177.
Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding. Numerous roads were flooded. About a foot and a half of water was over Paris Road near Brown Station Road.

As storms were moving through the region, four men were struck by lightning while at Marquette Park in the Dutchtown neighborhood of St. Louis.  A witness said that the lightning bolt struck one man directly and the others were impacted by the force. Two were able to begin performing CPR on the one who was directly hit. All four were rushed to area hospitals with one person being in critical condition. The man in critical condition died 11 days later on July 30th. He was 28 years old.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted several trees that were in very wet soil.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several tree limbs around town.

A storm chaser observed and photographed a tornado west of Rockport, IL. Based on this chaser���s observations and radar data, the tornado formed around 0019 UTC and tracked northeastward mainly across open fields before dissipating at 0022 UTC. Photo showed a condensation funnel not reaching the ground, but lofted debris was still noted beneath the funnel.  The starting and ending points are estimated and based on information received.

Intermittent, low end tornado damage was found on a path from just north of Saint Jacob, IL eastward into the Highland, IL area. The tornado first touched down north of Saint Jacob, IL along Marine Road where it toppled several trees and partially tore the roof off a large metal shed. The tornado then likely lifted briefly, but then touched down again intermittently along Lake Road. The tornado did minor roof and siding damage to many homes along Lake Road, as well as topple several trees and snapped a power line. The worst of the damage, which was rated EF-1, was to a large metal shed that was destroyed and the roof was lofted into nearby trees and pushed hundreds of feet down the street. In addition, a 2x4 from this roof was driven straight into the roof of a nearby building. The tornado then likely lifted briefly, before touching down again and doing additional damage to large trees in a neighborhood along 15th and 16th Streets. The tornado then lifted and dissipated. Overall the tornado was rated EF1 with a path length of 5.29 miles and a max path width of 700 yards. No injuries or deaths were reported.

Additional significant damage was noted to the south of the tornado path, likely associated with a strong surge of the rear flank downdraft. This damage, with straight line windspeeds nearing 80 to locally 90 mph, included two large barns that were destroyed, along with some large trees that were toppled in a concentrated area across two neighborhoods off Poplar Street.

This caused the Crooked Creek to overflow its banks where it crosses West Line Road, about 4 miles south southeast of Odin.  A 16 year old girl was traveling southbound on West Line Road at approximately 815 pm. She crossed the bridge over the creek and drove into the flooded area.  The flood waters carried the car about 20 to 25 feet to the southwest off of the roadway.  She managed to climb out of the car and onto the roof.  The car became completely submerged so she clung to a nearby tree that the car was pushed up against.  She managed to yell for help and was rescued.  She did not sustain any injuries.

Thunderstorms winds blew down several trees and tree limbs between Bethel and Shelbyville. In Shelbyville, one tree fell onto a house and vehicle. No injuries were reported. Also, several trees were blown over onto Highway 15 about two miles south of Shelbyville.

Thunderstorm winds caused damage to a farmstead on the north side of Highway WW near intersection with County Road 425, southwest of Shelbina. In Shelbina, several large trees and numerous tree limbs were blown down around town. One large tree landed on a house causing major damage. A large tree limb fell onto a pickup truck causing damage.
Thunderstorm winds blew over a semi truck at a business on the west side of town. Also, numerous trees and tree limbs were blown down around town.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous tree limbs around town.

Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous tree limbs around Mexico and Laddonia. In Mexico, one large tree limb landed on a parked car causing moderate damage. Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees in town, a couple of which blocked roadways.

Widespread wind damage across the central portions of Boone County from Midway southeastward through Columbia. Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down. Several trees were blown down across Highway E blocking the roadway northeast of Midway. On the south side of Midway, a large tree was blown onto a home along South Trails Terrace causing moderate damage.  A 25 foot by 75 foot section of Boone Electric Co-op building on Rangeline Street was blown off. Also, another near by business sustained moderate roof damage.  A large tree fell onto a house on Thilly Avenue causing considerable damage. On Cook Avenue, a tree limb was blown off of a tree, hitting a person in the head.  The person sustained moderate injuries and was briefly hospitalized after the incident.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees in Kingdom City. Also, a large tree was blown over onto Highway Z near Calwood.
Several trees were blown down between Hawk Point and Troy, some of which were blocking roadways.  Also, an electric pole was snapped in half.
A large tree was blown down on West 6th Street in Montgomery City.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree onto a house causing minor roof damage.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs in New Haven. Also, southeast of New Haven a small communications tower was blown down.

A storm chaser observed and photographed a tornado 5 miles west of Virden, IL. Based on this chaser���s observations and radar data, the tornado formed around 0118 UTC and tracked northeastward across an open field before dissipating less than a minute later at 0119 UTC. Video showed a condensation funnel reaching the ground.  The starting and ending points are estimated and based on information received. Thus the tornado is rated EFU with a path length of approximately 0.23 miles and path width of 10 yards. No damage reported.

A brief tornado was observed touching down in a field southwest of Shelbina. The tornado was on the ground less than a minute and did no damage.  The tornado was rated EFU with a path length of approximately 0.10 miles and a path width of 10 yards. No damage was reported.

A brief tornado touched down to the northeast of Renseselaer very early in the morning on June 25th. The tornado first touched down along County Road 429. The tornado quickly pushed northeast, doing damage to a few sheds at the intersection of County Road 429 and Highway MM. One shed was completely destroyed and its roof was lifted into a nearby tree. The tornado spread northeast across Highway MM, before lifting just to the north of Highway MM. The tornado was rated EF0 with a path length of 0.21 miles and a max path width of 50 yards. No injuries or deaths were reported.

A brief, narrow tornado touched down in a residential subdivision northwest of Hannibal, MO early Friday morning. The tornado first touched down along Rosewood Drive, where it ripped the siding off the westward facing wall of a residential home. The tornado then continued northeast towards Deer Ridge, completely destroying a couple of vinyl fences and breaking limbs off a large tree on the north side of Deer Ridge. The tornado quickly lifted as it pushed east towards Munger Lane. The tornado was rated EF0 with a path length of 0.13 miles and a max path width of 25 yards. No injuries or deaths were reported.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous tree limbs. Also, in Farber some shingles were blown off of the roof of a house on west side of town.
Thunderstorm winds caused widespread damage across Hannibal. Several large tree limbs and minor roof damage was reported on Lilly Street. Several trees were blown down onto Lindell Avenue.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous tree limbs around the intersection of U.S. Highway 36 and Highway H.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree onto a house causing major damage to the walls, which were buckling under the weight of the fallen tree. Several windows were broken on the house as well.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous large tree limbs around town.
Widespread tree damage around RV Resort about 3 miles north of Pittsfield.

Widespread flash flooding was reported across the southern half of Boone County, when up to 7 inches of rain fell in a span of 6 hours. Several water rescues were reported, including one swift water rescue.  Columbia firefighters rescued a man who was clinging to a tree in Bear Creek downstream of North Creasy Springs Road after his car got swept away by the swift current.  They also rescued two people from a mobile home on North Hinkson Creek Road.  At least an additional 10 water rescues were performed after the drivers drove into flood waters in a number of locations around the county. Numerous roads were flooded including U.S. Highway 63 at intersection with Highway 163, Nifong Boulevard at Glen Eagle Drive, Highway WW at Old Hawthorne, Creasy Springs and Bear Creek, North Route V at Barnes School Road, and U.S. Highway 40 near Midway.  The rain pushed Hinkson Creek to a record high level, flooding Wilson���s Total Fitness and the Missouri Athletic Center at Forum Boulevard and closing Providence Road through midday on Friday.  A section of West Dripping Springs Road was washed out due to flash flooding from Silver Fork Creek.  Highway E was flooded where it crosses over Perche Creek and Route ZZ was flooded by Harmony Creek. Also, Route Y east of Ashland was closed due to flooding from Cedar Creek.  No deaths or injuries were reported.

Even though the rain had tapered off, flooding continued to affect the southern half of Boone County. Numerous federal, state and local roads remained flooded.  Also, a number of creeks were well out of their banks including Hinkson Creek, Perche Creek, Harmony Creek and Bear Creek.
Up to five inches of rain fell in about a 6 hour period causing flash flooding. Several roads were flooded including Highway 94 near Rhineland.
Up to four inches of rain fell in about a 6 hour period causing flash flooding. Several roads were flooded including the intersection of Highway B and West Veterans Memorial Parkway.

A brief, narrow tornado touched down in a field to the northwest of Roodhouse, IL on Saturday afternoon. A sheriff`s deputy reported that the tornado briefly touched down before lifting as the storm moved toward Manchester, IL. No damage was noted. The tornado was rated EFU with a path length of approximately 0.15 miles and a path width of 25 yards.

Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous power lines, tree limbs and trees through out town. A large tree was blown down at the intersection of Washington Avenue and Dysart Street. On the northeast side of town a tree was blown down onto a mobile home causing considerable damage. No injuries were reported.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous trees across the far northern portions of Calhoun County.

Another round of heavy rain fell across Boone County, less than 12 hours after the flash flood event from June 24th through the morning hours of June 25th, where up to 7 inches of rain fell. Up to an additional 2 to 3 inches fell causing another round of flash flooding across the county. Numerous roads were flooded.  One water rescue due to swift water took place about 3 miles northeast of Murry. Another swift water rescue occurred about 2 miles northeast of Easley where two occupants of a vehicle were trapped by the flood waters.  Two vehicles were stuck in swift water from Rocky Fork Creek on North Creekland Drive, just north of intersection with East Calvert Hill Road, so the occupants had to be rescued.  Three miles northeast of McBaine, water was flooding a residence, so fire fighters had to rescue the two occupants and their dog.  A section of road was washed out about 5 miles east southeast of Harrisburg.  No injuries were reported.

Up to four inches of rain in a short amount of time caused flash flooding in Hannibal, especially for areas along Bear Creek. Numerous streets in the area were flooded due to Bear Creek rising well above its banks.

Up to five inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding. Numerous roads were flooded including the intersection of Highway U and Booneslick Road, at the intersection of Highway B and Veterans Memorial Parkway and on State Highway 47 at Willow Road. A swift water rescue had to be performed on Township Line Road near where it crosses Big Creek. Another water rescue took place at the intersection of Highway W and Powerline Road.  No injuries were reported.

Up to five inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.  Several roads were flooded including Highway J west of Troy.  Two water rescues were performed. One about 4 miles west of Winfield and another one about 4 miles west northwest of Old Monroe.  No injuries were reported.
Up to 4 inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding. Numerous roads were flooded across the southern half of the county.

After up to three inches of rain fell from late evening on June 24th through the early morning hours of June 25th, another round of heavy rain developed and moved across Cole County. Up to an additional 4 inches of rain fell causing flash flooding. Numerous roads were flooded across the northern half of the county, including portions of Walnut, West Miller, Waverly, Virginia and Kansas Streets in central portions of Jefferson City. Numerous water rescues were performed on the west side of town as well as in the central sections of town after a number of vehicles were driven into the flood waters.  No injuries were reported.

After an initial round of heavy rain, up to two inches, late in the day on June 24th into the early morning hours of June 25th, another round of heavy rain developed during the evening hours of June 25th through the early morning hours of June 26th. So the region received another 2 to 3 inches of rain which caused Hurricane Creek to rise well out of its banks in and around Hillview.  Several roads in the area were flooded.
Thunderstorm winds snapped two power poles about 3 miles north of  Chapman. Also, several power lines were knocked down.
Thunderstorm winds snapped off a couple of large pine trees and blew down numerous tree limbs at the Ramey Lake Golf Course.

Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding. There was fast running water over several roads around the intersection of South 30th Street and Fox Run West. Depth was unknown. Also, there was fasting moving water over the intersection of Illinois Route 96 and St. Anthony Road due to Mill Creek flowing out of its banks in that location.

Up to 4 inches of rain fell in a about a 2 hour period causing flash flooding across the southern half of Boone County.  A water rescue occurred about 4 miles east northeast of McBaine. Numerous roads were flooded. No injuries were reported.

Hail up to baseball size fell over Mt. Sterling and surrounding areas causing widespread damage to several dozen vehicles, buildings and crops. At least one farmer lost about a 1000 acres of corn and soybeans due to the large hail.

Widespread wind damage from the north side of Mt. Sterling to south of Hersman. Numerous trees, tree limbs, power poles and power lines were blown down.  Several businesses and homes, especially on the south side of Mt. Sterling, sustained roof damage from fallen trees and tree limbs. One of the baseball dugouts at the high school was destroyed, with other minor damage around the school campus. A couple of trees fell onto unoccupied vehicles causing major damage.
Widespread wind damage across the central sections of Marion County. Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down. Some of the debris landed on roads blocking them.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous tree limbs around town.
A wide swath of large hail, up to two inches in diameter, fell across portions of St. Louis County including Bridgeton, St. Ann, Overland, Maryland Heights, Creve Coeur, and Brentwood.

A wide swath of damaging winds from Perry southward into Griggsville and Valley City. Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down. Some of the trees fell onto Illinois Route 107 both north and south of Perry. A power pole was blown down in Griggsville.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines around the county, especially between Monroe City and Paris. Also, several power poles were blown down along Highway W.

An NWS storm survey discovered a macroburst that first initiated to the north of Rensselaer, MO. This macroburst caused extensive tree damage in town, especially on the western side of Rensselaer where several large branches and trees were snapped or uprooted and a few roofs sustained damage. Winds in this area were determined to be around 80 mph. The large swath of damaging winds then pushed south towards Mark Twain State Park. Extensive tree damage was noted in the state park. In addition, the Blackjack Marina sustained quite a bit damage from straight line winds around 80 mph. These winds were strong enough to cause damage to several boats, damage to the metal roofing of the marina, and the winds were even able to pull part of the marina off its mooring. The dollar amount damage to the marina is estimated to be around a million dollars.  The worst of the damage occurred to the south of the marina in the town of Perry, MO. Extensive tree damage was noted in this area along with some damage to roofs and siding to a number of residences. The degree of tree and structural damage was consistent with fairly widespread 80 mph winds across town, with localized areas of 90 mph present in some of the observed damage. Straight line wind damage continued to the south of Perry, but it became less intense and more scattered in nature south of town. No deaths or injuries were reported.

Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs onto Highway O near intersection with County Road 111. Also, in Mokane a large maple tree was blown over onto a home causing moderate roof damage.

A dead tree fell onto a vehicle that was traveling southbound on Highway 21, injuring the driver and killing the passenger. A witness trailing the vehicle reported there was only light wind and rain, as did a Missouri State Trooper. The vehicle was destroyed.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a couple of power lines and caused damage to nearby corn crop.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees as well a a couple of power poles around town.

High resolution satellite data and information from storm spotters indicates the tornado touched down in an open field a little less than a mile south-southwest of the Berdan Road and Wrights Road intersection. The tornado moved north-northeast and intensified as it moved into the west side of the town of Wrights, IL. In Wrights, the tornado destroyed two new, well-built farm buildings, ripping one of from a concrete foundation around the perimeter of the building. The tornado then moved to the northeast, destroying two more farm buildings before crossing Wrights road, where it snapped a number of trees and rolled a camper onto a boat. The tornado continued to the northeast causing intermittent damage to trees and vegetation. The high resolution satellite data showed a prominent track in the open fields northeast of the NE 850 Ave and Super Slab Road Intersection. The last identifiable damage and where the tornado appeared to have ended is around a third of a mile west of the NE 1000 Street and NE 950 Ave Intersection. The tornado was rated EF2 with max wind speed of 115 mph. The path length was 5.83 miles with a max path width of 75 yards. No deaths or injuries were reported.

Thunderstorm winds destroyed an open sided barn on the east side of Illinois Route 267, that was about six tenths of a mile north northeast of the intersection of Illinois Routes 267 and 108. Also, a few large tree limbs were blown down.

A tornado touched down just outside of Johnson`s Shut Ins State Park on highway N, east of Black, MO. This tornado snapped the trunks of several large trees along the road before moving into the park where it caused widespread tree damage. Overall, the tornado was rated EF1 with a path length of 1.17 miles and a max path width of 100 yards. No deaths or injuries reported.

The tornado began between Highway H and U.S. Highway 67 around 5.4 miles south-southeast of Farmington. The tornado crossed U.S. Highway 67 where it topped, snapped, and uprooted trees. The tornado traveled northeast paralleling a portion of Possum Hollow Road where tree damage was extensive with numerous snapped and uprooted trees. Several homes along this stretch were damaged, primarily due to fallen trees. The tornado then struck a farmstead near a bend in Possum Hollow Road where it completely destroyed two outbuildings. Neither of these structures were well-anchored and damage was rated at EF-1. The tornado continued to the northeast snapping and uprooting trees. A homeowner with 40 acres of land along Knob Lick Road estimated that 60-70% of the trees were destroyed. Extensive damage was found near the intersection of Knob Lick Road and Old Fredericktown Road. Three homes in this area lost all or large portions of their roof with one home also losing portions of several walls. This damage was rated EF-2. Damage from the homes, a destroyed garage, and trees was strewn hundreds of yards to the north. The path width of the tornado at this point was just over 400 yards. The tornado then crossed Highway OO where the width was around 450 yards. A home lost part of its roof, a barn was damaged, and numerous trees were snapped or uprooted along this stretch. All of this damage was rated at EF-1. The tornado crossed Smith Road destroying several barns and damaging a manufactured home, and then crossed Busiek Road damaging a small barn, several farm outbuildings and totally destroying a large well built farm outbuilding. Damage in this area was rated EF-1 or EF-2. The 400+ yard wide tornado crossed the St. Francois County/Ste. Genevieve County line just north of Green Acres Lane.

The 400+ yard wide tornado crossed the St. Francois County/Ste. Genevieve County line just north of Green Acres Lane. The tornado then traveled to the northeast crossing Route F multiple times as it traveled towards Coffman. Numerous trees were snapped or uprooted along this path, a number of farm outbuildings and barns were damaged or destroyed, and several homes suffered partial roof damage. The worst damage occurred to a home on Route AA just north of Route F. This home was completely destroyed. All of the walls were completely blown into the rear of the foundation and the roof was totally removed. Little anchoring was evident to the walls. One minor injury occurred to a male at the residence who found shelter in the pantry area. Tree damage in this area was some of the worst noted with every tree snapped or sheared supporting an EF-3 damage rating to the home. Another home on McDaniel Road just north of Route F sustained severe damage. The roof was completely removed and a large portion of the northeast walls were removed. Little if any anchoring of the walls was evident which supported an EF-2 damage rating. Numerous power poles and trees were snapped along Route F as the tornado traveled to the northeast into Coffman. Crown Valley Brewing and Distilling suffered minor damage, however the building on the north side of Route F was heavily damaged, rated at EF-1. A small building adjacent to the main Coffman Baptist Church was completely destroyed with debris blown into the main church building. There was no anchoring evident in this small building and damage was rated at EF-1. The tornado continued to the east-northeast crossing Madden Creek. The last detectable damage and thus end point was around 4 miles east-northeast of Coffman, southeast of Brands Lake near Goat Hill Trail. Overall, the tornado was rated EF3 with a path length of 16.74 miles and a max path width of 450 yards (St. Francois/Ste. Genevieve Counties).

The tornado moved out of Missouri (Ste. Genevieve County) into Illinois (Randolph County) moving though flood plains and crossing the Mississippi River just north of the Menard Correctional Center.  The tornado crossed Route 3 south of Lochhead Drive destroying a small barn, snapping or uprooting trees, and caused minor damage to several homes and a hardware store. Snapped or uprooted trees and downed power poles were found along the remainder of the tornado track through Chester with roof damage to several homes on Brenda Street. The worst damage in Chester occurred just northeast of the Palestine Road and Three Spring Roads intersection, where two farm outbuildings were completely destroyed. The larger of the two buildings was well-built with anchor bolts every 18-24 inches in the concrete foundation. This damage was rated EF-2. Further northeast, minor roof damage and the loss of the roof-mounted HVAC unit was found at the nursing home near Old Lodge Lane and Three Springs Road. The tornado continued to the northeast into Bremen paralleling and crossing Route 150, producing tree damage and minor roof damage to several homes. Minor roof damage to several homes, damage to several farm outbuildings, and snapped and uprooted trees were found along parts of Chester Road and Paradise Road. The worst of this damage was rated EF-1. The tornado dissipated around 1.6 miles northeast of Bremen, just west of Route 150. Overall the tornado was rated EF2 with a path length of 16.47 miles and a max path width of 400 yards.

A tornado touched down on south side of County Road 124, 1.3 miles west intersection with Highway E, in southern Iron County. This tornado uprooted several trees and broke branches on numerous other trees before continuing into a field where it damaged a manufactured home. The tornado then moved into a densely wooded portion of Mark Twain National Forest where it uprooted or damaged many trees as it crossed from Iron County, about 8 miles east of Glover, into Madison County.  The tornado was rated EF1 with a path length of 4.35 miles and a max path width of 250 yards in Madison County. No deaths or injuries.

The tornado touched down near the St. Francis River approximately 5.5 miles to the WSW of Fredericktown, MO, where it topped or snapped the trunks of several trees. The tornado continued to the northeast along the river and began impacting homes as it approached Fredericktown. Here the tornado ripped half of the roof off of one home, rolled a manufactured home onto its side, pulled roofing material from another home, and continued to cause considerable tree damage. The tornado widened to about 1/2 mile as it approached MO Highway 72 from the southwest, damaging multiple homes and businesses. A business on the south side of Highway 72 is where the only known injury took place, where an individual was hurt climbing out of the debris after the tornado had exited the area. The tornado strengthened as it moved north of Highway 72, completely destroying a number of homes. It was determined that the frames of these homes were largely only toe-nailed into their foundation, which precluded a higher rating than a low-end EF-3. The tornado then impacted the Black River Electric Co-op. Here the tornado ripped a well-built canopy from between two small warehouses, completely destroyed one of these small warehouses, and then completely destroyed a larger steel warehouse attached to the main office. The steel warehouse was very well constructed, with steel I-beams approximately 1 foot in width, bolted into the concrete foundation roughly every 20 feet. These beams spanned the roof of the structure and supported a thick, crimped sheet metal exterior. This is believed to be where the tornado reached peak intensity, with approximately 150 mph winds. The attached office fared notably better, sustaining mainly roof damage and the loss of several windows. The office was very well constructed, consisting of brick and concrete walls. The tornado then crossed US highway 67 and continued to cause considerable damage. Two newly built self-storage buildings with north facing bay doors were completely destroyed, while a third identical building with south facing doors was damaged, but remained standing. Two more homes were also impacted in this area. The roof was completely ripped from one of these homes, though most of the walls, which were bolted into the concrete foundation, were left standing. Only a few interior walls remained on the second home, though it appeared that the frame of this home was only toe-nailed into the foundation. The poor construction of the second home, and the lack of hurricane clips on the roof of the first, precluded a higher rating than EF-2 in this area. As the tornado continued northeast, it moved through additional residential areas, damaging several more homes and businesses. The tornado may have begun to weaken somewhat at this point, as the walls largely remained standing on most of these buildings. The tornado then began to move into more rural areas to the northeast of Fredericktown, where it caused consistent tree damage for several more miles, ripped most of the roof from one home, and completely destroyed a barn. The tornado may have briefly lifted as it moved into northeastern Madison County before coming back down and causing considerable tree damage along Madison county road 252. Along the Madison/Perry county line, where it moved into WFO Paducah's County Warning Area, the width was about 1/2 of a mile wide with numerous trees snapped and uprooted. The portion of the tornado path in Madison County was rated EF3 overall with a path length of 14.83 miles and a max path width of 880 yards. There was one injury and no deaths in Madison County. Overall, the tornado (Madison/Perry Counties) was rated EF3 with a path length of 18.95 miles and a max path width of 880 yards. There was one injury and no deaths with this tornado.

This tornado touched down just north of I-64 causing primarily tree damage, but one home was damaged on Chestnut Road. The tornado traveled northeast, again primarily causing tree damage and crossed Tower Road. Damage occurred to two machine sheds just west of U.S. Highway 51 and south of Holly Road with the tornado lifting shortly thereafter. Overall, the tornado was rated EF0 with a path length of 2.05 miles and a max path width of 180 yards. No deaths or injuries were reported.
Up to four inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding. Several roads were washed out in the Clayton and Concord townships, including N 1353rd Lane near Walnut Fork Creek.
Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous tree limbs near Pike along U.S. Highway 54. In Griggsville, several power lines were blown down.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree near the Ralls County Sheriff's office in New London.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees at the intersection of Highway E and County Road 283, west of Hatton.

Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous trees across the southern portions of Callaway County. Several trees were blown down onto U.S. Highway 54 near Guthrie. Also, several trees were blown down onto Highway 94 near intersection with Highway AA and near Portland.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large trees in New Florence.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree in the spotter's yard.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees around town.

The tornado crossed from Iron into Madison County, about 4.8 miles WSW of Braddy Ford, and continued moving to the northeast. The damage in western Madison County was extensive tree damage as seen on high resolution USGS satellite imagery. Shortly after lifting, around 1.7 miles north northeast of Braddy Ford, the storm that produced this tornado went on to produce the Fredericktown tornado. This portion of the tornado track is rated EFU because it was surveyed from satellite images. The path length is 5.93 miles with a max path width of 50 yards. Overall, the entire tornado (Iron/Madison Counties) was rated EF1 with a path length of 10.23 miles and a max path width of 250 yards. No deaths or injuries.

A swath of damaging winds occurred over St. Clair County from Swansea through O'Fallon, Scott AFB, and Mascoutah. Several large trees were blown down. The roof of a storage building was blown off at Air Force Base Storage. The debris landed on a house east of the storage building near the intersection of Illinois Route 161 and Hannah Chase Court. In Mascoutah, a pole barn was lifted and flipped, landing on a nearby business about 30 feet to the east.
Downburst winds blew a vehicle off of the roadway in New Minden. No injuries were reported. Also, several large tree limbs were blown down in the area.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several large tree limbs on the south side of town.
Trained spotter estimated a wind gust of 65 mph in Aviston.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a one and a half foot diameter tree in town.

Widespread wind damage occurred across Boone County. One large tree was blown down at the intersection of Highway F and Stidham Road. A large tree was blown over onto Old U.S. Highway 63 near Dripping Springs Road. Several trees were blown down across Old Plank Road near the intersection with Route K. Also, several power lines were blown down at Providence Road and Wilkes Boulevard and a street light was snapped off falling onto the intersection of 7th Street and Cherry Street. More trees were blown down near the intersection of Highway WW and S. Rangeline Road.
Widespread wind damage across the Quincy metropolitan area. Numerous large trees were blown down.
Thunderstorm winds snapped a telephone pole in town.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree on Rock Quarry Road near intersection with Gans Road.

Thunderstorm winds blew off part of a metal roof on a storage building in St. Thomas. Just southeast of Osage Bend, a large tree with a shallow root ball was tipped over. Also, numerous large tree limbs were snapped off.

Widespread wind damage across Osage County. A roof was blown off of a storage building at the intersection of Highway 133 and County Road 503. Also, there were numerous trees blown down along Highway 133. A roof was blown off of a business on U.S. Highway 63 about two miles north of Westphalia. A large tree was blown down onto U.S. Highway 63 blocking both lanes. Just east of Loose Creek a home sustained minor damage and another home sustained minor damage from a trampoline being blown into it. Otherwise, numerous large tree limbs were blown down.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a tree onto Highway J near the intersection with Highway B.
Thunderstorm winds blew a large tree down at the intersection of State Highway AA and Platinum Road.

Widespread wind damage across portions of Kingdom City and Fulton. A large tree was blown down onto Route FF near intersection with Old U.S. Highway 40, blocking the roadway. Also, a large tree was blown down onto a house in Fulton causing moderate roof damage. Numerous large tree limbs and several additional trees were blown down.
Four large trees were blown down onto Highway 79 near the intersection with Route TT.
Widespread wind damage between Morrison and Gasconade. A number of trees were blown down onto Highway 100.
Several large trees were blown down along County Highway 4 near El Dara.

A weak tornado touched down just northwest of Wellsville east of Highway 19 where it broke several power poles. It then moved northeast toward the intersection of Morgan School Road and Route A and traveled northeast to Orchard Road. Minor tree damage and flattened corn was observed. The width of the tornado was around 50 yards, and the damage was rated EF-0. Interestingly, the WSR-88D identified debris (lowering correlation coefficient), likely from the lofted corn stalks. Overall, the tornado was rated EF0 with a path length of 4.27miles and max path width of 50 yards. No deaths or injuries were reported.
Pike County dispatch reported three to four trees blown down at the intersection of Illinois Routes 104 and 107.  In Griggsville, a transformer was blown and several power lines were blown down.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree across Highway Y near the intersection with Wheeler Road. Also, a large tree was blown down at the intersection of Evergreen Loop and Three Oaks Road.

Widespread wind damage across Franklin County. A large tree was blown down onto roadway along St. Louis Inn Road about 5 miles southwest of St. Clair. Another large tree was blown down on to Highway 47 near intersection with Eastview Drive.  On the southwest side of Union, several power lines were blown down at the intersection of Koelling Avenue and West Springfield Avenue.  About 3 miles north northwest of Moselle, there were numerous trees damaged or uprooted, as well as damage to a car port, power lines blown down and damage to several roofs.  Several trees were blown over on the northwest side of Pacific.
Several street lights were blown over in town.
A hay wagon was blown onto U.S. Highway 67 between White Hall and Carrolton. In Carrolton, a couch was blown onto U.S. Highway 67. In Greenfield, several power lines were blown down.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large section of fence near Chesterfield Mall.

A tornado touched down around 10:05 PM CST to the northeast of Ellington, southwest of County Road 440, snapping numerous trees rated EF1 damage. The tornado proceeded east- northeast across Sinking Creek and damaged a house and single-wide trailer along County Road 428, as well as continuing to snap numerous trees. As the tornado continued east-northeast and crossed County Road 447, it intensified to an EF2 and completely tore off the roofs of two homes off of County Road 442 and County Road 442B. The home off of County Road 442B was where the most significant damage was observed, as it also lost an exterior wall. Two outbuildings were also destroyed by the tornado, and significant tree damage was observed. The tornado crossed the Black River and weakened, though it still caused EF1 damage to trees and power lines on County Road 456, where it lifted around 10:11 PM CST. Overall, the tornado was rated EF2 with a path length of 6.86 miles and max path width of 300 yards. No deaths or injuries were reported.

The tornado began on the south side of I-270 around three-quarters of a mile west of the I-270/I-255 interchange at 8:27 PM CST. Damage in this area consisted of several downed highway signs and a bent light pole. The tornado moved northeast and intensified rapidly after crossing I-255, striking an Amazon warehouse. The west-facing walls of the warehouse collapsed inward, which was followed by multiple structural failures as the tornado moved through the complex, including the collapse of additional walls and the loss of a large segment of the roof. This was the worst damage along the entire tornado track rated EF-3. Cars in the rear of the building were strewn eastward and power lines and several large high tension towers were also destroyed. There was one person injured and 6 fatalities at the Amazon facility. The tornado weakened as it moved northeast across Sand Road, where it destroyed an unanchored mobile home and an outbuilding, snapped trees, and downed power poles. Damage in this area was rated EF-1. Further northeast, the tornado crossed South University Drive where it snapped a power pole and downed additional trees. It then crossed into the Sunset Hills Country Club subdivision. Throughout a portion of the subdivision, there were downed trees, snapped branches, and superficial home damage consisting of missing shingles or small portions of roof covering. The tornado weakened further as it moved northeast, and lifted just west of Butler Boulevard at 8:35 PM CST. Noteworthy is debris from the Amazon warehouse was found along the entire track of this storm, tens of miles to the northeast of the warehouse. Overall, the tornado was rated EF3 with a path length of 4.22 miles and max path width of 300 yards. Six deaths and one injured were reported.
Thunderstorm winds blew a large tree down onto an apartment building causing moderate damage.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a metal sign and numerous tree limbs on the east side of town along Illinois Route 16.

Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree onto Illinois Route 159 about a mile south of Bunker Hill. Several power lines were blown down onto School House Road east of intersection with Dorchester Road.

The tornado first touched down south of Sorento on New Douglas Road (Bond County), west of Sorento Reservoir, where it snapped several trees. The tornado moved northeast, passing 3.2 miles east of Donnellson crossing Mt. Moriah Avenue, moving into southern Montgomery County.  The tornado was rated EF1 in Bond County with a path length of 8.94 miles and a max path width of 150 yards. No injuries or deaths were reported in Bond County.

As it moved northeast into Montgomery County 3.2 miles east of Donnellson, it moved over the southern portion of Coffeen Lake. The damage in this area consisted of downed and snapped trees rated EF-1. As the tornado continued northeast, it crossed IL Route 185 where it destroyed an outbuilding, snapped trees, and downed power lines. Near the intersection of School House Avenue and Dads Trail, extensive tree damage was observed. Further northeast, the tornado crossed Fillmore Lake, moving into Fayette County.   The tornado was rated EF1 in Montgomery County with a path length of 10.11 miles and a max path width of 300 yards. No injuries or deaths were reported in Montgomery County.

As it tracked to the northeast across Fayette County, it moved through Bingham, snapping additional trees. The tornado intensified and widened as it moved across the southeast portion of Ramsey State Park and across US Highway 51 north of Ramsey. The tornado continued to track northeast, crossing IL Route 14 around 2 miles west of Herrick, continuing into Shelby County (WFO Lincoln IL County Warning Area). The tornado was rated EF1 in Fayette County with a path length of 14.8 miles and a max path width of 690 yards. No injuries or deaths were reported in Fayette County.

The tornado developed about a third of a mile northeast of the intersection of Highway 94 and Osage Ridge Road in southwestern St. Charles County around 7:32 PM CDT. As it moved to the northeast, two houses sustained minor damage and one outbuilding was destroyed on Highway T, just north of intersection with Hemsath Road. The tornado continued northeast and strengthened as it approached Highway F, northwest of Defiance. Multiple homesteads and farms suffered varying degrees of property damage along Highway F to Highway 94. Two homes were completely destroyed. The first home was 110 years old and did not appear to have any anchoring to the concrete foundation. The second home just 100 yards east of the first was swept clean to the subfloor, which was still anchored to the concrete foundation. One fatality and two injuries occurred at this location. The damage was rated EF3 with winds to 165 mph. The tornado continued northeast, crossing the Missouri River and Howell Island before entering St. Louis County in Chesterfield Valley. Dollar amount damage is estimated around $3.4 million.

After crossing into St. Louis County the tornado caused extensive tree damage along the river, a mere half mile from a large outlet mall. It crossed Highway 40/61/Interstate 64 east of the Boone Bridge causing minor damage to vehicles that were on the highway. The tornado continued northeast, crossing the Missouri River again, back into St. Charles County near Greens Bottom Road.

After crossing back into St. Charles County there was additional tree damage, broken power poles, and structural damage noted along Greens Bottom Road. The tornado crossed the Missouri River a third and final time, back into St. Louis County traveling across Highway 364 and north of the Creve Coeur Airport.

Once back in St. Louis County, there was additional tree damage and other minor damage noted. The tornado lifted at 8:01 PM before entering the Hollywood Casino Amphitheatre Complex. Overall, the entire tornado (St. Charles/St. Louis counties) was rated EF3 with a path length of 27.30 miles and a max path width of 150 yards. There was one death and two injuries with this tornado. Dollar amount damage is estimated around $3.4 million in St. Charles County.

A wide swath of damaging winds across Franklin County. In Gerald, several phone and power lines were blown down in town. Several large trees and power lines were blown down on Camp Mo-Val Road, as well as North Bend Loop, southwest of Union. Additional power lines were blown down in St. Clair. About 3 miles west northwest of Robertsville, a large tree was blown over onto Highway O near intersection with Route AM.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees and power lines just northwest of Reno.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees and caused minor damage to a machine shed in Coffeen. Also, several power lines around town in Fillmore.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree in town.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree onto Highway C, about 8 miles south southwest of Fredericktown.
